News.title: Fears ‘suitcase killer’ using ‘every trick’ to delay probe as he appears in court YARDS from where Brit was found dead
News.content:
'VERY CALCULATING' Fears ‘suitcase killer’ using ‘every trick’ to delay probe as he appears in court YARDS from where Brit was found dead

THE Afghan boxer accused of killing a Brit and dumping her body in a suitcase has arrived at court in Athens.

Officials fear a “cunning” Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, may use “every trick in the book” to try and delay the murder probe against him.



He is accused of killing Scottish charity worker Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, after she was discovered by a homeless man in a derelict building on July 18.

Ahmadzai arrived at court for a initial hearing in an unmarked grey Hyundai i30 car, alongside a number of police officers.



The court house is located on Evelpidon Street in the Greek capital – just a few minutes away from where Elisabeth’s body was found.

The hearing will be held in private but the case has already gathered global attention.

After allegedly murdering Elisabeth, Ahmadzai is accused of texting her friends and family before switching off the device.

He is then said to have bought another phone and texted his wife, Alaina Hall, Elisabeth’s friends and even himself.

In an attempt to cover his tracks he pretended to be an unnamed jihadist who killed the Scottish national because she was trying to convert people to Christianity, Greek news outlet Proto Thema reports.

Ahmadzai fled Afghanistan in 2016 after his entire family were wiped out by the Taliban.



He reportedly paid smugglers to bring him to Britain, but later crossed through Pakistan, Iran, and Turkey before eventually settling in Greece.

After converting to Christianity in 2017 he met his wife Alaina, from Georgia in the US, and they married in 2023.

Bombshell testimony from Alaina suggested that he visited Elisabeth’s apartment on the night of her disappearance.

She said she woke up in the early hours of July 15 to find him missing – and when she traced his location using Find My Friends it showed him at her apartment.

George Kalliakmanis, an ex-cop who heads the police union in Athens, told The Sun: “He went to the flat where she was staying for a reason.



“What was it? Nothing can be ruled out. Did she reject him? Nothing can be ruled out.”

Elisabeth reportedly met Ahmadzai and his wife Alaina while volunteering for a refugee charity.

News.title: TikTok star Cesar Gastelum shot dead during livestream outside restaurant by two armed gunmen on motorbikes
News.content:
INFLUENCER KILLED TikTok star Cesar Gastelum shot dead during livestream outside restaurant by two armed gunmen on motorbikes

TIKTOK star Cesar Gastelum has been shot dead while livestreaming to fans after a gunman on a motorcycle allegedly open fire outside a fast food restaurant.

The Mexican influencer, who had nearly 600,000 TikTok followers, was killed in the horror attack in the violence-plagued city of Culiacan as horrified viewers watched the bloodshed unfold live.



Gastelum, known for his comedy videos and livestreams, was reportedly broadcasting with friends outside the restaurant when two people wearing motorcycle helmets pulled up.

Footage on the livestream seen by Reuters appears to show the motorcycle driver firing a gun directly at Gastelum before fleeing the scene.



A security official in the Mexican state of Sinaloa confirmed the influencer’s death and said a significant security operation was underway following the shooting.

No arrests have been announced.



Gastelum’s killing comes as Culiacan, the capital of Sinaloa state, continues to be rocked by persistent violence as rival organised crime factions battle for control of the region.

The city has become a hotspot for deadly attacks as criminal groups compete for influence, with authorities regularly launching major security operations in an attempt to curb the bloodshed.

The murder has also drawn chilling comparisons to the killing of Mexican beauty influencer Valeria Marquez, who was also shot dead during a TikTok livestream earlier this year.

The 23-year-old was working inside her beauty salon in Zapopan, Jalisco, when a gunman entered and opened fire.



Viewers watched in horror as Marquez was reportedly shot once in the chest and twice in the head before collapsing to the floor.

Earlier in the livestream, she chillingly told followers: “Maybe they were going to kill me or something.”

Prosecutors later launched a femicide investigation into her death.

It comes after Mexican authorities announced the arrest of Ramon Nagel Alvarez Ayala, also known as “El R1,” a senior alleged figure in the Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), over claims he was behind the influencer’s murder.

Ayala was captured during a special forces operation that also left one member of his security team dead.



Federal Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch claimed Ayala’s son, Francisco Alvarez, had been in a romantic relationship with Marquez before they split up.

According to Harfuch, Francisco allegedly phoned his father and asked him to arrange the killing.

Authorities claim Ayala then ordered a hitman to go to Marquez’s salon disguised as a delivery driver.

The alleged gunman reportedly entered the salon, asked the influencer to confirm her identity and, once she responded to her name, opened fire, shooting her three times.

The CJNG, one of Mexico’s most notorious criminal organisations, was designated a foreign terrorist organisation by the Trump administration last year.



The cartel has long been accused of trafficking cocaine, fentanyl and methamphetamine, as well as extorting businesses across Mexico.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Its founder, Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, better known as El Mencho, was killed by authorities earlier this year after being captured by the army in Tapalpa, Jalisco.

His death triggered a wave of violence across Jalisco, with cars and businesses set alight and schools temporarily forced to close.

News.title: Faulty fans are urgently recalled in UK over risk of electric shock and fire with users warned ‘stop using immediately’
News.content:
A batch of faulty fans has been urgently recalled in the UK over risk of electric shock and fire.

B&Q has recalled its 23cm OPP White 9” table fan FT23A that was sold between March and July this year.

B&Q has also urged shoppers to “stop using it immediately and return to your nearest B&Q store.”



If you think you may have purchased the product you can also check the product for its barcode, which is 5063022605689.



An update from the Office for Product Safety and Standards said: “The product presents a risk of electric shock and fire as there is a fault within the oscillation mechanism that can damage internal wiring.”

It also warned that it does not meet the requirements of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.

A full update from the retailer read: “A potential safety issue has been identified in relation to the below product. In some cases an electrical component may overheat leading to a fire or electric shock risk.

“If you have purchased one of these models during the time period above, please stop using it immediately and return to your nearest B&Q store.”

If you are worried or have any other inquiries you can contact your local B&Q or call 0300 303 4482.

You should be able to return it to the store and receive a full refund, even if you don’t have the receipt.

But it is always worth double checking with customer service.



It is the latest in a string of recalls, revealed by retailers this week.

Shoppers are also being urged to return a Toy Story water bottle, sold in Home Bargains, after it was identified as a choking hazard.

Meanwhile, Lay‘s Sour Cream & Dill crisps have been recalled following the presence of undeclared allergens.

News.title: Dad charged over death of girl, 9, in Arbroath after family camped in industrial park
News.content:
A DAD arrested over the alleged killing of his nine-year-old daughter has now been charged in connection with her death.

The tragic schoolgirl was found fatally injured during a family ‘camping’ trip in Arbroath’s Elliot Industrial Estate around midnight on Monday.



The schoolgirl was rushed to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee alongside four other casualties but doctors were unable to save her.

Her dad, 35, has since been arrested and charged in connection with the “suspicious” death.



He is due to appear at Dundee Sheriff Court today.

We told previously how the family, of West Yorkshire, had pitched a tent in the industrial estate less than a mile away from the seafront alongside another child.



Witnesses told how they were seen cooking on an outdoor stove by the roadside just hours before the girl was found fatally injured.

Passing motorists told of their surprise at seeing the makeshift camp on the edge of an oil firm’s car park, a short distance from the beach, on Sunday evening.

The youngster was found a short time later dying from injuries.

Police cordoned off the scene on Monday at Elliot Industrial Estate, close to the Halliburton manufacturing firm.



Forensics officers were seen looking inside the car while an incident tent is believed to have been covering the family’s shelter.

Officers say they are not looking for anyone else in connection with the young girl’s death and the other members of the family, who were camping in the area, are being supported by specialist officers.

A police presence will remain in the area as the extensive investigation continues.



Detective Inspector Mike Ness of the Major Investigation Team said: “Our thoughts remain with those affected by these events.

“A police presence will remain in the area while our enquiries continue.

“Anyone with any concerns, or information, should approach these officers or contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 0008 of Monday, 3 August 2026.”

A Police Scotland spokesperson added: “A 35-year-old man arrested in connection with the death of a nine-year-old girl in Arbroath has been charged.

“Around 12.02am on Monday, 3 August 2026, the girl was found seriously injured in Elliot Industrial Estate.



“She was taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she later died.

“Her death is being treated as suspicious, and a 35-year-old white British man has been arrested and charged.

“He is due to appear at Dundee Sheriff Court on Wednesday, 5 August, 2026.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The nine-year-old girl and the 35-year-old man are known to each other.

“Officers are not looking for anyone else in connection with her death and the other members of the family, from West Yorkshire, who were camping in the area, are being supported by specialist officers.”

News.title: ‘Heavily armed’ man, 38, arrested at Donald Trump’s California golf course days before President’s visit to West Coast
News.content:
A MAN said to be heavily armed has been arrested at Donald Trump’s California golf course just days before the President arrived to host a high-profile fundraiser.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, was allegedly found with a loaded gun, ammunition and later an arsenal of weapons after authorities said he was spotted taking photos of security preparations at the exclusive club.



Federal agents first noticed Taele during a security assessment on July 31 at Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, where the President was due to headline a Republican National Committee fundraising dinner on Tuesday.

According to court documents, agents allegedly saw Taele walking around the course wearing an earpiece while taking pictures and videos of officers planning security for Trump’s visit.





He left the area but reportedly returned two days later, when golf course staff alerted federal agents after spotting him back on the property.

Authorities claim Taele approached the agents and falsely identified himself as a State Department employee assigned to help with security.

He later admitted there was a loaded firearm inside his vehicle parked at the golf club, investigators said.

Los Angeles County Sheriff’s deputies allegedly found a loaded magazine in his pocket before searching his pickup truck, where they recovered a loaded pistol and additional ammunition, the LA Times reported.



A search of his Downey home the following day uncovered what investigators described as an alarming cache of weapons, including an illegally modified AR-style rifle, a .45-caliber pistol, body armor, high-capacity magazines and bulk ammunition.

Detectives also said they found notebooks containing “concerning statements” along with two radio devices.

Taele was arrested on suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possessing prohibited ammunition.

He has since been federally charged with possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison if convicted.

He also faces state charges linked to the same incident and remains under investigation over a separate robbery in nearby El Segundo.



Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles field office, said: “Mr. Taele’s troubling behavior at the President’s public golf course merely days before the President was expected to arrive raised serious red flags for law enforcement.

“There is no room for error, particularly in light of previous attempts on President Trump’s life.”

First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli added: “While we are still investigating the motives of this individual, we are thankful he was apprehended before the President’s visit.



“Federal and local law enforcement stepped in early and prevented what could have been a dangerous situation from occurring.”

Authorities stressed there is “no credible threat to our communities” and Trump’s fundraiser went ahead as planned.

Asked about the incident, Trump brushed off the security scare during an interview with Fox News.

“The only thing I get a little solace from is they say only consequential presidents, and I am definitely consequential,” he said.

Rather than dwell on the arrest, Trump went on to discuss Iran and the economy.



The President’s trip marked a rare visit to California as he sought to contrast his agenda on the economy, border security and crime with that of Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom ahead of November’s congressional elections.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump has been the target of multiple assassination attempts in recent years, including when he was shot during a campaign rally in Pennsylvania in 2024.

A jury last year also found a man guilty of attempting to assassinate Trump at his Florida golf club, while an armed suspect was recently arrested after allegedly trying to force his way into the White House Correspondents’ Dinner while the President was attending.

News.title: ‘Talented footballer’, 14, who drowned after going into River Thames to ‘cool down’ is named
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

RIVER TRAGEDY ‘Talented footballer’, 14, who drowned after going into River Thames to ‘cool down’ is named

A 14-YEAR-OLD boy who drowned after vanishing in the River Thames has been named as a talented local footballer.

The Mayor of Tower Hamlets – Lutfur Rahman – identified the teenager, who disappeared from Millwall outer dock, London, as Banta Sillah.



Banta, who sadly passed away on Monday was described as a “talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week.”

Speaking to The Standard, the mayor added that young Banta “had immense potential and was dearly loved by his peers.”



He continued: “As we mourn Banta, I urge families to speak with children and young people, we should all be aware of the dangers swimming in open water.

“Swimming should only take place in officially designated areas with lifeguards present.”

Emergency services were called to Ferry Road on Monday after receiving reports that a teenage boy had entered the water and vanished.

A lengthy search operation followed, involving rescue boats, police, fire crews and paramedics.

The frantic search operation was concluded when the 14-year-old was recovered from the water at around 10pm.

He was sadly pronounced dead at the scene, despite the best efforts of paramedics.



His family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

Cops said the boy’s death is being treated as unexpected but not suspicious.

Enquiries continue as the force prepares a report for the coroner.

The Met Police is asking anyone with any information that may assist their investigation into the sad death to come forward.

Detective Superintendent Oliver Richter said: “Our thoughts remain with the family and loved ones of this young boy at this incredibly difficult time.



“As the warm weather continues, I would urge everyone to remember that open water can present serious dangers.

“Please only swim in designated areas and take the time to speak with children and young people about staying safe around water.”

A spokesperson for the London Ambulance Service said: “We were called at 6:52pm, 3 August, to reports of a drowning incident by East Ferry Road, E14.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We sent ambulance crews, paramedics in fast response cars, an incident response officer and an advanced paramedic.

“Our crews assisted our emergency services partners at the scene but were later stood down.”

News.title: At least 17 killed & 27 injured as Russia unleashes massive blitz on Kyiv sparking huge inferno in city
News.content:
RUSSIA has unleashed a deadly missile and drone barrage on Kyiv with at least 17 people killed and 27 injured across the capital.

Moscow pummelled the Ukrainian city with dozens of homes left in ruins as rescuers warn people may still be trapped under the rubble.



Vladimir Putin’s forces launched 28 missiles in a 20-minute nightmare blitzkrieg sparking over an hour of air raid alerts.

The attack is one of the deadliest strikes on Kyiv this year, with four civilians wounded being rushed to hospital in a critical condition.



President Volodymyr Zelensky said the night of attacks resulted in “horrific casualties and destruction”.

He said: “The main targets of the attack were warehouses belonging to civilian enterprises, but there were also strikes on infrastructure and a railway station.

“The targets were not related to the war: a brewery, warehouses of building materials, and civilian logistics facilities.”

Nine people were killed in the Boryspil district with at least eight civilians fatally struck while waiting at a railway station in Kyiv.



Four others died in the Bucha district, and one in the Fastiv district with the remaining victims yet to be identified.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said brave rescuers pulled two people from the ruins of a warehouse near the city centre which was destroyed in the attack.

He added: “There may still be people under the rubble. Search and rescue operations are proceeding.”

Head of Kyiv’s military administration, Timur Tkachenko, said the “enemy is once again massively attacking the Kyiv region” as strikes started just after midnight.

Russia‘s defence ministry claimed it had only struck logistics hubs and supply centres in Kyiv and the surrounding region.



Klitschko confirmed several warehouses were struck but said dozens of ballistic missiles and drones also hit homes and public buildings.

A major fire broke out on the outskirts of the city with a fallen Russian missile seen beside a residential building.

The Kyiv military administration added the attack caused an ammonia leak that emergency crews were tackling long into the night.



Ukraine responded to the strikes by blitzing another of the Russian Amazon logistic hubs – known as Wildberries – in Aleksin.

Strikes between Russia and Ukraine are continuing to intensify after major attacks by both sides.

Ukraine brought war to Putin’s doorstep earlier in the week by dragging the tyrant’s personal palaces into the crosshairs in an explosive show of force.

A Black Sea blitz left smoke billowing into the sky over Putin’s secret hideouts while a fatal bombing in Moscow last weekend struck just one mile from the Kremlin.

Since mid-July, Ukraine has struck dozens of sites belonging to Wildberries – the country’s biggest e-commerce platform dubbed Russia’s Amazon.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

This followed a genius campaign of targeting Russian oil hubs and transport links, to paralyse Putin’s regime and spark fuel shortages.

Ukraine’s strikes deep inside Russia are part of a wider effort to push Moscow to the negotiation table and end the fighting.
