In the years since rising to global stardom, Phoebe Bridgers has tended to guard her personal life with increasing privacy – but for a singer-songwriter, it’s never that simple.

A lot has happened in the six years since she last released a solo album, including the explosion in popularity of her supergroup Boygenius (comprising Bridgers, Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker), an engagement and breakup with Irish actor Paul Mescal, and a relationship with her current partner, comedian, musician and film director Bo Burnham. On her accomplished new album Lost Weekend, she finds herself ready to talk – or at least sing – things through.

The breakup with Mescal is seemingly alluded to in the title track in which Bridgers sings over a slow, drumless beat: “I’m supposed to be married, but I called it off/ I’ve been known to throw a tantrum/ When things are not the way I imagine them/ I am restoring the natural order/ Learning the same lesson over and over again.”

open image in gallery Phoebe Bridgers’ new album ‘Lost Weekend’ is out this month ( Olof Grind )

The subject of the song, however, is ambiguous, with Bridgers closing on the line, “You know me, and I’ll never forgive you for that,” before the song erupts into instrumental energy.

In a glowing five-star review in The Guardian, Alexis Petridis speculates that a line in “The Governor’s Waltz”, a lush, almost anecdotal song showcasing Bridgers’ knack for storytelling, “could be interpreted as a swipe at Mescal’s current partner”, the musician Gracie Abrams: “She can pretend to be me/ Since she took my place in my bed, on that stage.”

Bridgers and Mescal started dating during the pandemic, and were subsequently the subject of engagement rumours before separating in late 2022. Both have refrained from discussing their relationship, and breakup, in the press, with the Normal People star telling Harper’s Bazaar that his personal life is “nobody else’s business”.

References to Bridgers’ relationship with Burnham (whose full name is Robert Pickering Burnham) run through the album, most prominently on “Bobby”, a catchy and uptempo song about love, written with Bridgers’ characteristic black humour. “So you followed me home like you’d done it before/ And you had to bend over to get through the door/ And if you didn’t like either one of my friends/ I’d kill them, I’d kill them,” she sings.

It’s a song that makes love sound both euphoric and unhealthy: “Bobby, this could be the end of wanting/ I exist only if you’re watching.”

In another of the album’s standout tracks, “Liberty Tree”, an uplifting and defiant song, Bridgers seems to again address Burnham, who is credited as a co-writer on several of Lost Weekend’s songs, and also provides backing vocals. “Don’t die, Bobby/ Before I die/ It feels so good to have you in my life,” she sings.

Other credited collaborators on the album include prolific superproducer Jack Antonoff, and Bridgers regulars Marshall Vore, Christian Lee Hutson, and Boygenius bandmates Baker and Dacus. Stranger Things star Maya Hawke is also a credited co-writer on the songs “Haunted” and “Never Going Back!”. The track “I Can’t Wait” features a credit from an artist listed as “Son John-Johnson”, whom Rolling Stone speculates “sounds a lot like Geese [frontman] Cameron Winter”.

open image in gallery Bridgers with Boygenius bandmates Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker at the 2024 Grammy Awards ( Getty )

Bridgers’ songwriting has always tended towards the autobiographical, dating back to her early career; her 2017 breakthrough track “Motion Sickness” was written about her relationship with the older musician Ryan Adams, who produced Bridgers’ first EP and whom she later accused of emotional abuse.

Bridgers’ difficult relationship with father, Tony Bridgers, who died in December 2022, has also been a key inspiration on her music, and was notably the focus of the 2020 song “Kyoto”. The pain of grief, and her complicated feelings about him, are another pervasive theme on Lost Weekend. “I can’t imagine you dead/But you are every day,” she sings on the swelling and sorrowful “Still Standing”.

Though Lost Weekend is just Bridgers’ third studio album (not counting her work with Boygenius, or the album released as Better Oblivion Community Center, her now-defunct project with Connor Oberst), it looks set to ossify her standing as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation.

The distinctive, ethereal sound that first made her reputation with Stranger in the Alps in 2017 has been maintained but iterated on; likewise her capacity for wordplay and exacting control of lyrical tone.

Fans hoping for a “tell-all” album might be left frustrated by an album that opts more for messy emotional soul-baring than gossipy tidbits – though for those wondering just how exactly Bridgers has been doing these past few years, they finally have an answer. As she sings on the final track, the bittersweet “Lost Weekend (Reprise)”: “If I ever come out of hiding, you won’t have to know how to find me again.”

Lost Weekend is released on 14 August through the label Dead Oceans.

News.title: The five men at the center of Tupac’s murder mystery as trial begins
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Nearly 30 years after Tupac Shakur was gunned down in Las Vegas, a jury is set to hear evidence in the long-unsolved killing when Duane "Keffe D" Davis goes on trial next week.

Davis, 63, is charged with orchestrating the Sept. 7, 1996, drive-by shooting that killed Shakur and wounded Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight. He has pleaded not guilty, and his trial is scheduled to begin Aug. 10.

Prosecutors allege the shooting was retaliation after a fight earlier that night at the MGM Grand involving Shakur, Knight and Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson, Davis' nephew. Authorities say the attack reflected the bitter East Coast-West Coast rap rivalry of the 1990s, as well as gang tensions between Bloods and Crips affiliates.

Here's a look at the key figures at the center of the case.

Tupac Shakur

open image in gallery Duane “Keffe D” Davis is the last living suspect in one of hip-hop’s most enduring mysteries — the 1996 death of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas

Shakur was one of hip-hop's biggest stars, with five No. 1 albums, six Grammy nominations and a posthumous induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2017. He also received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2023.

The rapper, born Lesane Parish Crooks in New York in 1971, was riding in the passenger seat of a black BMW driven by Knight when a white Cadillac pulled alongside near the Las Vegas Strip and opened fire. Shakur was struck multiple times and died six days later at age 25.

His family has long criticized authorities for taking nearly three decades to bring criminal charges in the case.

Marion "Suge" Knight

open image in gallery Shakur, left, and Death Row Records Chairman Marion Suge Knight, attend a voter registration event in South Central Los Angeles, on Aug. 15, 1996. ( AP )

Knight, who founded Death Row Records and signed Shakur to the label, survived the shooting after being grazed by bullet fragments.

Now 61, Knight is serving a 28-year prison sentence in California after pleading no contest to voluntary manslaughter in the 2015 fatal hit-and-run death of Terry Carter.

In his 2019 memoir, Davis described himself and Knight as the only surviving eyewitnesses to the shooting.

Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson

open image in gallery Shakur was in Las Vegas to watch Mike Tyson fight Bruce Seldon ( AFP )

Authorities have long identified Anderson as the suspected gunman, although he was never charged and repeatedly denied any involvement.

According to prosecutors, Anderson was assaulted by Shakur and members of his entourage during a fight at the MGM Grand just hours before the shooting, providing the alleged motive for the attack.

Davis wrote in his memoir that he handed a gun to the back seat of the Cadillac but did not identify who fired the fatal shots.

Anderson was killed in an unrelated gang shooting in Compton in 1998.

Deandrae "Freaky" Smith

open image in gallery Duane Davis, left, talks with his attorney Michael Sanft in Clark County District Court during a calendar call and motion hearing for Davis' upcoming trial

Smith, also known as "Big Dre," was riding in the back seat of the Cadillac beside Anderson.

Although investigators have long believed Anderson fired the shots, grand jury testimony introduced another theory.

Former Davis associate Denvonta Lee testified that Smith confessed to firing the shots after taking the gun from Anderson because Anderson did not have a clear angle.

Lee was not in the Cadillac and testified about what he said Smith later told him.

Smith died of natural causes in 2004, according to the Los Angeles County Coroner's Office.

Terry "Bubble Up" Brown

Brown was allegedly driving the white Cadillac during the shooting.

Davis wrote that the group spotted Shakur's BMW after seeing the rapper leaning out of the window and greeting fans. According to the memoir, Davis told Brown to turn the car around before they pulled alongside the BMW moments before the gunfire.

Brown was killed in a 2015 shooting at a medical marijuana dispensary in Compton.

Investigators have said neither the Cadillac nor the gun used in the shooting has ever been recovered, leaving prosecutors to rely heavily on witness testimony, Davis' own statements and other evidence when the long-awaited trial begins.

Several athletes are currently "unaccounted for" following the conclusion of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Police Scotland said.

The development comes after four members of Uganda’s boxing team have gone missing in Scotland, according to the Ugandan sporting news website NBS Sport.

These athletes failed to rejoin their delegation ahead of the team’s scheduled return to Uganda on Tuesday.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “Police Scotland has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for.

“Inquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking place with the Home Office.”

It is understood that the Home Office will take action accordingly if it is made aware of any breaches of immigration law ( Alamy/PA )

Speaking to the Press Association on Monday, Commonwealth Games chief executive Phil Batty said: “We’ve welcomed nearly 3,000 athletes to the city from 74 nations.

“We want to deliver a safe and secure games, so we work really closely with Police Scotland, the Border Force, and UK visas and immigration to make sure everyone arrives and departs in line with regulation.”

PA understands that the Home Office will take action accordingly if it is made aware of any breaches of immigration law, and that it takes all necessary steps to prevent people who could abuse the immigration system from entering the UK.

The Home Office maintains a policy of not routinely commenting on individual asylum cases, with claims considered on their individual merits in accordance with the UK’s international obligations.

The Ugandan ministry of education and sports has been contacted for comment.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

Sports.title: When can Mykhailo Mudryk play for Chelsea again, and when was his last appearance for the Blues?
Sports.content:
TAKING THE MYK When can Mykhailo Mudryk play for Chelsea again, and when was his last appearance for the Blues?

CHELSEA winger Mykhailo Mudryk has seen his four-year ban from football end early, ahead of the new season.

The Blues signed Mudryk from under the noses of Arsenal in January 2023, but his first spell with the club failed to live up to expectations.



The 25-year-old had scored 10 times in 73 appearances for the Blues, prior to being banned in 2024.

The £80million winger shared a number of training clips on his social media platforms throughout the ban, but new manager Xabi Alonso will be boosted by the ending of the ban.



The Blues are currently on a pre-season tour in Hong Kong, where they will meet Spurs tomorrow.

SunSport can reveal when Mykhailo Mudryk can return for Chelsea, and when his last appearance was.



When can Mykhailo Mudryk play for Chelsea, and when was his last appearance?

After being banned in 2024, he is now available to play immediately for the Blues, and has joined the squad in Hong Kong.

Mykhailo Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since a 2-0 win in the Conference League against Heidenheim.

The Ukrainian winger was an unused substitute three days later in a 3-0 win over Aston Villa, the last time he was allowed to play.

The 25-year-old is set to be a part of Xabi Alonso’s squad, as they prepare to take on Juventus in pre-season.



Why was Mykhailo Mudryk banned from playing football?

Mykhailo Mudryk was panned for four years for a positive test of meldonium, a banned cardiovascular substance.

He tested positive for the substance while with Ukraine in late 2024.

Mudryk was suspended in December 2024, and formally charged in January 2025.

In January 2026, he was handed a four-year ban, but has been allowed to return to just six months later.

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez reveals what Cristiano Ronaldo told her in emotional conversation over body shaming trolls
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ has revealed the touching line Cristiano Ronaldo told her as she opened up to him about vile trolls body-shaming her.

Ronaldo and Georgina got engaged last year and are due to be wed in Madeira this weekend.



However, dating one of the most high-profile athletes in the world comes with a high degree of scrutiny both professionally and from fans.

And unfortunately, far too often that scrutiny can turn into outright hate and trolling.



That is exactly what Georgina, 32, has had the misfortune of experiencing, revealing as such in a heartfelt post on her Instagram.

In the emotional post, the internet personality and model revealed what Ronaldo, 41, had said to reassure her.



She said: “I was talking about it with Cris and I told him, ‘I’m worried that they’re calling me fat now, because I make a living from my image’.

“And he replied, ‘You don’t live off your image. You live off who you are. A perfect woman. Beautiful, with a great body, a mother, a good person, successful, and who lives life with love. What more could you want? It’s normal to be envied’.

“Sometimes we all need someone to remind us what truly matters.”

Georgina and Ronaldo first met in 2016.

She raises all five of his children under one roof.

Alana Martina, 8, and Bella Esmeralda, 4, are biologically hers.

The identity of Cristiano Jr’s biological mother has been kept a secret, while twins Eva Maria and Mateo, both 9, were born via surrogacy.

The sixth child, Bella Esmeralda’s twin Angel, tragically died during childbirth in 2022.



Hitting out at the body-shaming trolls, she said: “My body will change, as all women’s bodies do. And I hope it continues to do so for many years, because that will mean I’m still alive.

“I’m the mother of six wonderful children, three of whom are girls who will one day be great women.



“And if there’s one thing I want to teach them – along with Cris, whom I’m deeply proud of for the values ​​he embodies as a father and as a man – it’s that a person’s worth can never depend on their physical appearance or the opinions of strangers.

“These past few days I’ve seen all kinds of comments about some photos of me on a boat. Some people are commenting on my body, others are defending me.”

What is body shaming? BODY shaming is described as "humiliating someone by making inappropriate or derogatory comments about their body size or shape". In addition, “commenting on a person’s clothing, body hair, eating habits, make-up skills or attractiveness” could be constituted as body shaming too, PsychCentral explained. While body shaming has become more of an issue in recent years, a study conducted by Glamour magazine in 2000 found that a staggering 97 per cent of women surveyed admitted to having an “I hate my body” moment. And those who shame people about their figures can include doctors and medical professionals too. A 2019 report found that more than 3 in 5 adults encounter “weight bias” from their doctors – particularly those who are obese. And body shaming someone can have massive effects on their mental health, and could potentially lead to depression, anxiety, low self-esteem, eating disorders and self-harm. If you have been body shamed and are struggling to deal with the effects, you can call the Samaritans on 116 123 for confidential, emotional support.

She added: “The funny thing is, this happens every summer. Every year my body makes the news again.

“And then I wonder… where is the standard? Who decides what the ‘right’ body is? Do we really still think happiness has a size?

“I love my curves. I love the freedom to live in the body I choose. In the body that supports me, that has allowed me to embrace, create life, fall, and get back up.



“A body that deserves respect, love, and gratitude in all its versions.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘forced to shatter Premier League transfer record and club wages record to sign Vinicius Jr as Real name price’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL will have to break the Premier League transfer record to sign Vinicius Jr, according to reports.

The Gunners are looking to make one of the biggest upgrades possible to their squad’s current firepower by adding the Real Madrid star to their ranks.



Vinicius, 26, has one year left on his existing Real contract, where he currently earns £15million a year.

However, it is reported the Brazilian wants to be compensated for his years of service as he enters the prime of his career.



To that end, the winger is reportedly demanding fresh terms of more than £25m.

Real tabled an offer for Vinicius on Monday to the tune of around £19m, and won’t go above that valuation.



With the gap in offers so big, Vinicius seems destined to move if he wants a big pay cheque.

That’s where Arsenal come in, with the Premier League champions open to signing the two-time Champions League winner.

According to ESPN, Spanish giants Real would expect to receive a bid of around £128m (€150m).

That would see Arsenal shatter the current Premier League transfer record held by Liverpool when they signed Alexander Isak from Newcastle last summer in a £125m move.

Then there are wages to consider – and it is a factor Arsenal will consider ripping up their wage structure for, having indicated they would be willing to make him the highest-paid player in Prem history.

Such a deal would see Vinicius earn more than Bukayo Saka‘s £350,000-a-week and more than Erling Haaland‘s record reported £525,000-a-week wages.

As well as Vinicius, Arsenal are simultaneously working on a move to land Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Sports.title: Man Utd share 1,698-word statement over controversial ticket tout crackdown after 1 device accessed over 1,000 accounts
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED say ONE device gained access to 1,088 membership accounts to fuel a ticket touting operation.

United have been pilloried by fans after thousands were locked out of their accounts amid apparent suspicious activity.



The club restricted accounts where login details were shared with more than six people in a bid to clamp down on touting.

SunSport revealed the most skilled touts had not been affected as they used innovative methods to bypass settings.



Fan groups were scathing in their assessment of the process.

And the Manchester United Supporters’ Trust was “inundated” with complaints from supporters affected.



That prompted a 1,698-word update on the club website.

The Red Devils acknowledged its approach had caused “genuine upset and distress”.

United did not offer an apology.

But they vowed to share findings once their investigation was over and thanked fans for their “feedback and challenge”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The club said: “Our intention is to protect fair access to tickets for genuine United supporters and to tackle organised ticket touting and abuse of the ticketing system.”

Meanwhile, Red Devils have given boss Michael Carrick a boost by striking a record £20million training kit deal with gambling firm Betway — the largest in world football.

And United are set to name ex-Hearts chief Eva Olid as women’s manager.

Sports.title: Beleaguered Fifa boss Infantino holed up in desperate crisis talks to cling to power as Wenger joins blackmail rebellion
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has called an emergency crisis Fifa meeting in a desperate attempt to cling on to his power.

And now Arsene Wenger has joined the growing group distancing themselves from the Swiss chief.



Infantino, 56, sparked chaos around world football last week when news broke of his shock plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

That sparked a furious backlash from swathes of football – including Uefa and other continental confederations, who threatened to boycot the World Cup and even plotted to launch a rival tournament to “paralyse Fifa”.



Under overwhelming and mounting pressure, Infantino was forced to make an embarrassing U-turn and ditch his money-grabbing scheme – and now faces a fight to keep hold of his Fifa presidency.

Now he is taking extreme measures to try and retain any support he can.



According to The Times, Infantino is currently holed up in Rabat and has called senior Fifa staff to the Moroccan capital for the urgent gathering.

There was also said to be a meeting of senior Fifa staff on Tuesday without Infantino present, where all but one opposed the controversial World Cup financial plot.

Even so, the chief’s remaining loyal right-hand men are shamelessly appealing to many of the 211 member associations to publicly back the president, who faces an election in March if he survives that long.

But few have done so – including, crucially, Saudi Arabia, hosts of the 2034 World Cup.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein launched a damning attack on the Swiss and his organisation, making accusations of “blackmail”.

It is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.



“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.



“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Within the top brass at Fifa, both Arsene Wenger and Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom have slammed Infantino’s disgraceful plans.

Wenger admitted it was “absolutely necessary” to scrap the scheme – which included setting up a company called Fifa Forward Enterprises (FFE) with a stake held by Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s brother Joshua Kusher – and that he had no idea about it until it became public knowledge.



Fifa’s head of global football development does not intent to quit and said: “The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side.

“I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity.”

Grafstrom, meanwhile, sent an email to Fifa staff in an attempt to boost morale after “a sad and reproachable series of events”.

Grafstrom said: “We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations.



“A sad and reproachable series of events — which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned — for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

“I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience.

“You do not need to worry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go.

“The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Sports.title: Liverpool legend Mo Salah ‘agrees two-year deal with Trabzonspor’ on free as Turkish club release transfer statement
Sports.content:
MOHAMED SALAH has agreed to join Turkish side Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

The Liverpool legend left the Premier League side at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.



Salah, 34, has reportedly agreed to move to the Turkish Super Lig on a two-year contract.

Trabzonspor confirmed that they were in negotiations with the attacker on social media.



The club then revealed that Salah would be arriving in Istanbul on Wednesday ahead of finalising the transfer.

A statement read: “Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5 (tomorrow).



“The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

“The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club’s official communication channels during the day.”

Salah will be familiar with at least one of his new team-mates, with one being former Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana.

The stopper spent last season on loan at the club and has returned for a second stint this summer.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He will also join former Manchester City defender Stefan Savic and Cape Verde’s World Cup star Sidny Lopes Cabral in the squad.

Salah announced he would leave Liverpool back in March after nine years with the club.

He signed for the club in 2017 from Serie A side Roma and went on to become one of its best-ever players.

The forward has scored an astonishing 255 goals in 435 appearances in all competitions.



He helped the Reds to two Premier League titles, the Champions League, Fifa Club World Cup, FA Cup and two EFL Cups.

In the summer, Salah helped Egypt reach the last-16 of the World Cup, which is the furthest ever made by the nation.

He scored one goal and assisted twice in five tournament appearances.

Last season, Trabzonspor finished third in the Super Lig, eight points behind champions Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Rapper Drake called me to convince me to quit Tottenham.. I thought it was Aaron Lennon winding me up says Jermain Defoe
Sports.content:
JERMAIN DEFOE says music icon Drake persuaded him to join Toronto from Tottenham – but only after thinking Aaron Lennon was playing a cruel prank.

The legendary striker, 43, hit the headlines when his spell as Woking’s boss ended after only SIX competitive showdowns last month.



But Defoe, who was blasted by the non-league minnows following his exit, had a stunning career with Spurs.

He made 363 appearances across two spells on Tottenham’s books – notching 143 goals along the way.



Defoe quit the North Londoners when MLS side Toronto came calling in 2014.

And Canadian rapper Drake was tasked with convincing the England icon to make the stunning move.



But Defoe was certain Tottenham team-mate Lennon, 39, was winding him up when he picked up the phone.

The former West Ham and Portsmouth marksman told the Mirror: “I remember being out for dinner with my cousin.

“I got a phone call, said ‘hello, who’s this’, and he said ‘It’s Drake’. Yeah, good one – I thought he was winding me up!

“I actually thought it was Aaron Lennon, I thought, ‘Wow, your Canadian accent is unbelievable’. But no, it was Drake.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We had a conversation and I remember he spoke about Toronto, the city, what it’s like, the people, the football club, and that was it. I decided to sign and I loved it.”

Defoe went on to find the net 12 times in 21 appearances for the Canadian side, whose home was on hosting duties for this summer’s World Cup.

And it allowed him to reunite with ex-Tottenham pal Ryan Nelsen, who was in charge of Toronto, despite initially having doubts.

The lethal finisher, who bagged a brace at Soccer Aid in June, added: “I remember getting a call from Ryan Nelsen.



“I played with Ryan at Tottenham towards the back end of his career. Obviously, he got the Toronto job and we spoke about the opportunity of going there.

“At the time I said I don’t think it’s going to happen because I was at Tottenham and I was settled and didn’t really think I was going to leave.”

Defoe reignited his Premier League career by joining Sunderland after a year-long spell with Toronto.

And he returned to the Stadium of Light, following stints with Bournemouth and Rangers, before announcing his retirement in 2022.

Sports.title: Jordan FA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘BLACKMAIL’ in most scathing statement yet: ‘We certainly won’t endorse him’
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO and Fifa have been accused of “blackmail” in the most scathing statement yet.

The head of world football’s governing body has come under intense criticism since his failed plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa events.



He backed down after a chaotic few days which saw football bodies around the world threaten a rebellion.

But despite the plans being thrown in the bin, Infantino continues to come under heavy fire as he desperately tries to cling on to the Fifa presidency.



However, the president of the Jordan FA launched a damning attack on the Swiss.

And it is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.



But the Jordan FA took a strong stance and insist they “refuse to give in” or “endorse” Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time.

“We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets – which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

“Secondly, we are being taxed by the US govt through Fifa for our participation.

“Money that should go to players and staff.

“This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico.



“But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

“Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.

“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.



“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

SunSport has contacted Fifa for comment in response to Prince Ali’s tweet.

Interestingly, the support of national associations in Asia could be critical to Infantino’s re-election campaign in March.



However, he may not even reach that far if Fifa council members opt to oust him.

Uefa cranked up the pressure on Arsene Wenger to quit as Fifa’s head of global football development – but he has no intention of doing so.

European football chiefs, meanwhile, are ready to team up with other confederations to set up a rival World Cup to “paralyse Fifa”.

Infantino’s furious opponents are also prepared to boycott Fifa council and committee meetings, as well as refuse to ratify decisions.

The shameless lawyer has only notched 15 declarations of support from the 211 member nations since his botched project was revealed.

Sports.content:
Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met

Arsenal and Newcastle have finally come to an agreement that will see Bruno Guimaraes move to north London - with the Premier League champions paying the entire fee up front

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to join Arsenal in a deal worth £75m

Arsenal are set to finally get their man in a £75million deal with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes, who had been pushing for the move.

‌



The Brazilian made it clear several weeks ago that he wanted to quit the Magpies so that he could move to the Premier League champions and, after weeks of talks and speculation, a deal has finally been struck between the two teams.

‌



Guimaraes arrived late to Newcastle's training camp in La Manga, but was afforded extra time off following his role in Brazil's World Cup campaign. The club have been unable to convince him to stay however and they will go their separate ways with the decision made amicably, the Chronicle exclusively reported this morning.

‌



New Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle had been hoping to change Guimaraes' mind when he arrived, but has been unsuccessful and the player remains determined to secure his exit.

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours as medical completed for transfer READ MORE :

The transfer fee will be paid up front in full with no add-ons, meaning Newcastle will get the full £75m to reinvest in this window. The Magpies ultimately feel they are getting good value for a player who will turn 29 in November. It also represents good profit for a player that cost the club £38m back in 2022.

Despite a desire to keep Guimaraes at the club Newcastle ultimately want players at St James' Park who are committed to the cause and it became clear that the Brazilian saw his future elsewhere.

‌



Arsenal have been linked with a number of major names this summer, including Vinicius Jnr, but the addition of Guimaraes will add even more quality to a midfield that already includes the likes of Declan Rice, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

View 2 Images The Brazilian will bolster an Arsenal side that is looking to defend the Premier League title (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

Guimaraes becomes the third blockbuster name to leave Newcastle as their team continues to be gutted of their best players. Anthony Gordon's move to Barcelona was followed by a mega swoop from Tottenham, who signed Sandro Tonali in a £100m deal. Guimaraes will now follow them out the door.

‌



It comes after Alexander Isak pushed for a move to Liverpool last season. All four transfers have earned Newcastle huge profits, but raised questions about their direction and ambition under their Saudi Arabian owners, who have spoken about being among the world's best clubs.

Eddie Howe departed the club last week, with the potential sale of Guimaraes likely the last straw. Jaissle was quickly identified as his replacement, with the Magpies now set for a busy end to the summer window to give the new boss a side capable of competing for the European places.

Sports.title: Alan Brazil gives health update as radio legend returns to air after life-saving operation
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil gives health update as radio legend returns to air after life-saving operation

Radio legend Alan Brazil has made his return to the talkSPORT breakfast show this week after spending months recovering from a life‑saving operation

View 2 Images Alan Brazil has returned to talkSPORT

Alan Brazil has issued a fresh update on his recovery after returning to talkSPORT following a life‑saving operation. The long‑time broadcaster had been off air for nearly four months while dealing with serious health issues.

‌



Brazil, who underwent a liver transplant, revealed in June that he spent eight hours on the operating table and that his heart briefly stopped during the surgery. Following months of recovery, he made his comeback to the station's Breakfast show on Wednesday (August 5).

‌



He is joined on air by former Aston Villa striker Gabriel Agbonlahor while Scotland icon Ally McCoist is on a 'well‑deserved' break after his stint as an ITV co‑commentator at the World Cup.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking about his health ahead of his return, Brazil said: "I am not going to bore everyone but it is remarkable really what happened. One minute I am doing this (the show), I've finished at 9:45am, there's a car outside and I am like 'what's going on?'

"Straight down to Addenbrooke's Hospital and a few hours later... wallop. They open me up and stick a new liver in there. So I did have cancer in my liver and we suspected that for months to be honest, but they didn't want to go in and touch it and shake it up in case you could make it spread.

‌



Brazil continued: "First of all they said the perfect match came in, otherwise I might still be waiting and people will know what I am talking about who might be on the list. You can wait 18 months, you can go down there, get ready to have the op and they say 'it's not quite right, go away and come back and we will phone you later, maybe in a few weeks' and it can be murder.

"I was so lucky, I went down there and they said 'we've got one and it looks perfect so we are going to do it now'. They inject you all over and you have to sign a few forms, you get carried in there and it's like 'goodbye everyone', that's how bad it was. I thought 'see you later'. Wife's in tears, it was horrible.

View 2 Images Alan Brazil spoke about his operation

‌



"That was the stage where I had to get it done otherwise it was 'see you later'. I didn't realise it was that extreme but it was. They told me, another couple of weeks and you were gone. I had seven or eight hours on there, the fluid build-up I had was horrendous.

"They cut me open and there was a flood, it was that bad everywhere I had it. I did have a few complications, my heart stopped for 40 seconds. I said 'did you get the old jump-leads on?' He said 'no, no. It came back. We were about to take action but it came back."

The former Ipswich and Tottenham midfielder has called his surgery and recovery 'a miracle', praising the 'brilliant' team at Addenbrooke's in Cambridge for saving his life. "I can’t thank the people at Cambridge enough," he said.

Article continues below

He also said that he is currently on "massive medication," adding: "I am on these pills and my resistance levels are not good, so they said I have to stay out of the sun."

Sports.title: Inside Hector Bellerin's life – club ownership, dating Love Island star, Arsenal exit
Sports.content:
Inside Hector Bellerin's life – club ownership, dating Love Island star, Arsenal exit

Arsenal's latest pre-season outing sees them face Real Betis - and former defender Hector Bellerin, whose life both on and off the pitch remains as intriguing as ever

View 5 Images Ex-Arsenal star Hector Bellerin will line up against his former side on Wednesday (Image: Getty Images)

Hector Bellerin is far from your typical modern footballer. Once regarded as one of the fastest full backs in the Premier League during his time at Arsenal, the Spanish defender is now plying his trade in La Liga with Real Betis.

‌



While in north London, Bellerin became something of a cult hero, lifting three FA Cups and standing out for both his blistering pace and his football IQ. However, it's Bellerin's passions away from the pitch that truly set him apart.

‌



Known as one of the most stylish men in sports, his high-end fashion sense and runway appearances have turned heads for years. He is also a committed environmentalist and vegan, using his massive platform to promote sustainability - a passion that even led him to become a shareholder in a football club.

‌



With a personal life every bit as fascinating as his career, this article takes a closer look at Hector Bellerin - from his Arsenal exit and surprise move into club ownership to his relationship with a Love Island star.

Despite being raised in Barcelona's famed La Masia academy, Bellerin spent much of his formative years at Arsenal. He joined the club as a 16-year-old in 2011 and would end up spending over a decade in north London.

‌



After breaking into the first team in 2014, Bellerin would spend the next several years as the Gunners' first choice right back. But as one decade gave way to the next, the Spaniard began to feel it was time for a new challenge.

His agent, Albert Botines, later revealed that the isolation Bellerin experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic - cut off from his family in Spain - was a major factor behind his decision to leave both Arsenal and England.

"After 10 years, Hector had in his mind that it was the right time to change," Botines said. "But it wasn't only about Arsenal, it was also about the Premier League, about the country, about everything.

‌



View 5 Images Hector Bellerin spent 11 years at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

"He moved when he was 16 from Barca to Arsenal, from Spain to England. During the Covid-19 time without his family, he was so alone in north London. Only training, then going home. He had more time to think about it and he thought this was the right time to move on."

Bellerin spent the 2021/22 campaign on loan at Real Betis - his father's boyhood club - before returning to Barcelona on a free transfer after his Arsenal contract expired that summer.

‌



His second spell at the Nou Camp lasted just half a season before he joined Sporting CP. Six months later, he was on the move once more, returning to Real Betis, where he has finally found stability after several years of upheaval.

Club ownership

During the back-end of his Arsenal career, Bellerin took a surprise step into football club ownership. In 2020, the defender became the second-largest shareholder in Forest Green Rovers, widely recognised as one of the world's most environmentally friendly football club.

View 5 Images Bellerin is co-owner of Forest Green Rovers (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Bellerin's investment was driven by a shared ethos. Much like the club, which went entirely vegan in 2015 and boasts a carbon-neutral footprint, Bellerin is a passionate environmentalist. He famously pledged to plant thousands of trees in the Amazon rainforest for every Arsenal victory.

Teaming up with Forest Green's chairman, Dale Vince, Bellerin saw an opportunity to help push the sustainability agenda within the football industry. His continuous dedication to these causes was recently recognised when he was awarded the prestigious BBC Green Sport Award, proving his commitment goes far beyond a mere financial stake.

"I feel very grateful. It is totally unexpected," Bellerin said after receiving the award last year. "I've been doing this stuff for a very long time, talking about sustainability not just in sport but in our everyday life.

‌



"I really appreciate it because it means that all the work and effort behind the scenes, to promote a message that I think is really important, has been seen and appreciated."

Speaking about his environmental consciousness, the Spaniard revealed that he has been wearing second-hand clothes and shoes in an effort to live as sustainable a life as possible.

View 5 Images Bellerin is a proud environmentalist (Image: Getty)

‌



"I feel with power comes responsibility. Every time someone puts a microphone next to you, there's a chance to talk about issues, to generate conversation," he said.

"I've been consuming second-hand clothes and shoes for a really long time. I remember once it took me six months to decide to buy a pair of shoes I saw in a shop next to where I parked. I wear those shoes almost all the time. It's about giving what you consume a good life and, when you're done, giving it another life."

He added: "The sustainability of the environment and animal cruelty now motivate me just as much as health. The way I feel physically and mentally, knowing I’m doing the right things, makes me really happy to be a vegan."

‌



Dating Love Island star

View 5 Images Bellerin previously dated Love Island star Jasmine Muller (Image: ITV)

Bellerin's high-profile status has also seen his love life make headlines, particularly recently with the arrival of Jasmine Muller on the 2026 series of ITV's Love Island. The 27-year-old fashion business owner and the former Premier League star were reportedly an item between 2021 and 2022.

Despite the intense public scrutiny that comes with dating a top-flight footballer, Jasmine has insisted that there is no bad blood between her and her former partner. Speaking ahead of her entrance into the famous villa, she admitted they parted ways on "really good terms" and still have a lot of love for each other.

‌



"I have nothing bad to say about him and him the same for me," she said. "But it is so long ago that it’s not something I think about on a daily."

She added: "I had a very healthy and lovely relationship with him and everything is on good terms."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's dream Marcus Rashford replacement as Man Utd sign £60million star
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's dream Marcus Rashford replacement as Man Utd sign £60million star

Michael Carrick could go for an unorthodox approach in replacing Marcus Rashford at Manchester United

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford remains a Manchester United player - for now (Image: Getty)

The future of Marcus Rashford has once again been reignited. The Manchester United attacker remains on course for a return to Carrington after he completes his post-World Cup break.

‌



His reunion with the Red Devils was approved by United boss Michael Carrick despite not having played for the club since 2024. Loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona kept the 28-year-old away from Manchester, with many believing his career with his boyhood club had come to an end.

‌



However, Barcelona's decision to sign Anthony Gordon instead of paying the £26m option to acquire Rashford permanently left him in limbo. A meaningful offer to sign Rashford has yet to be received by United, but the wheels may be turning on his eventual departure from the Premier League giants.

‌



The Sun reports that Rashford is part of a three-man shortlist for Fenerbahce, including AC Milan forward Rafael Leao and Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr. They add that the Englishman's representatives have been contacted by the Turkish giants over a potential move.

If a move for Rashford to the Super Lig pans out, Carrick's plan of replacing the England star could revolve around Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall. Such an acquisition may sound baffling at first, but it could be quite the masterstroke from the United boss.

Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear READ MORE :

Patrick Dorgu became a key - and versatile - asset for United last season when fit, playing more games in left-midfield and left-wing than in his natural left-back position. With four goals and four assists to his name in the 25/26 campaign, the Danish international proved to be a legitimate option across United's attack.

‌



Matheus Cunha possesses Rashford's No. 10 shirt and his position on the left flank, with some suggesting Dorgu's go-to role this upcoming season will be playing back-up to the Brazilian.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is reportedly a top target for Manchester United (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



If that is the case, Carrick will only have Luke Shaw as his realistic option at left-back, thus opening the door to the arrival of Hall, who has emerged as a key target for United this summer.

The 21-year-old is reportedly considered as the long-term replacement to Shaw and United are said to be considering an initial bid of around £60m to prise him away from St James' Park. His departure would mark the fourth major exit from Newcastle this summer, following Gordon, Sandro Tonali, and boss Eddie Howe.

The England defender represents the present and future for United, with his versatility also proving to be a valuable asset. So far in his career, Hall has played 26 matches at left midfield, as per to transfermarkt.

‌



View 3 Images Patrick Dorgu was used in midfield and attack for much of last season (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

While he's keen to become an out-and-out first-choice left-back, reportedly blaming his World Cup omission on Howe's varied use of him in the second half of last season, he will slowly replace Shaw - now 31 - as United's starter.

Carrick will need such depth for what he'll hope is a much longer campaign than the last when United exited the domestic cup competitions early and had no European football. And if he could sell the long-term vision to Hall, then he'll have plenty of options to play with on the left side of the pitch.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola offer delay explained as PSG clear way with medical booked
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola offer delay explained as PSG clear way with medical booked

Things could be about to hot up for Liverpool in the transfer market as the push to sign PSG ace Bradley Barcola continues

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's primary transfer target (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's summer transfer business has been unusually subdued so far, but that may not be the case for much longer. While their Premier League rivals have spent freely, the Reds are still waiting to truly ignite the market, with the rest of the traditional 'Big Six' already splashing more than £800million on new signings.

‌



That cautious approach has raised eyebrows, particularly following the arrival of new head coach Andoni Iraola. The Spaniard has added just two players to his squad to date - Victor Munoz, who joined from Osasuna in a £34.5million deal, and Jeremy Jacquet, whose £55m move from Rennes was agreed back in February.

‌



However, Liverpool are expected to accelerate their recruitment before the window closes, with one or two marquee additions - particularly in attack - firmly on the agenda. With that in mind, here's a round-up of the latest transfer news from Anfield.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal READ MORE :

Barcola bid delay explained

Liverpool have identified PSG winger Bradley Barcola as their top transfer target as they search for the long-term successor to Mohamed Salah. Official talks between the clubs are understood to be underway, but the Reds have yet to submit a formal offer for the France international.

According to Sky Sports, that is a deliberate strategy. Liverpool want to establish what PSG would realistically accept before making their opening move, rather than launching a bid that is immediately rejected and risks negotiations becoming public.

‌



The French champions are thought to value Barcola at around £145m, while Liverpool hope a deal can be struck closer to the £100m mark, leaving a sizeable gap between the two clubs' valuations.

View 3 Images Barcola is reportedly keen to join Liverpool (Image: Dan Mullan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

PSG clearing way for Barcola exit

Liverpool and PSG may still be some distance apart on valuation, but there are growing signs the French champions are planning for a future without Barcola.

‌



According to reports, PSG have agreed a deal to sign Monaco star Maghnes Akliouche. The versatile attacker, who can operate as an attacking midfielder or out wide, is expected to undergo a medical ahead of a £42.8m move to the Parc des Princes.

View 3 Images Maghnes Akliouche is set for a medical at PSG

The Ligue 1 giants are also closing in on Ajax winger Mika Godts, with reports suggesting a deal worth around £50m is nearing completion. Should both arrivals be finalised, it would further fuel speculation that PSG are preparing to cash in on Barcola.

Article continues below

The 23-year-old has produced 34 goals and 28 assists across the past two seasons at club level, despite fierce competition for places from Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue. Barcola is understood to be keen on a move to Anfield, where he would be offered a more central role in Liverpool's attack and the prospect of regular first-team football.

Sports.content:
Slica Bay, Sea Suite and Ben Nevis line up for the Brighton Mile this afternoon, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Silca Bay and Sea Suite feature among a field of nine for the Sapporo Japanese Premium Lager Brighton Mile Challenge Handicap on the opening day of the Festival of Racing at Brighton.

6.40 Yarmouth - Dubai Charm and Dowman contest trappy nursery

Dubai Charm and Dowman contest a trappy edition of this Strawberry Fields Stud Nursery Handicap at Yarmouth.

Top weight Dubai Charm represents Richard Hughes and Neil Callan and looks to hold excellent claims. A dominant winner at this track and trip twenty-eight days ago, she looks capable of stepping up on that form and this daughter of Blackbeard might be tough to beat.

Dowman finished strongly when opening his account over this trip at Windsor back in June and has his first start having undergone a gelding operation. An opening mark of 73 looks fair and he can go well under Billy Loughnane, who is chasing winners as he attempts to land the jockeys' championship for the first time.

Beauty Box makes her handicap debut with a hood added, while Wait Geordie ran with credit in the Super Sprint Stakes at Newbury and cannot be ruled out.

Babzini and Minkaas complete the shortlist, with the latter hampered when going well on her first start for TJ Kent last time out.

Sports.title: Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane.

After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

When trailing 4-1, Draper sat down and spent the entire changeover crying, apparently uncontrollably.

The 24-year-old carried on and almost claimed a break before spiritedly holding serve one more time, before Atmane closed out victory in an hour and 52 minutes.

Draper had established himself as one of the biggest challengers to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's dominance of the men's game as he moved up to a career high No 4 ranking in June 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round match at the Canadian Open between Terence Atmane and Jack Draper.

It was around that time that Draper began suffering from a bone bruise in his left arm, an injury that has continued to hamper him ever since.

In 2026, he put together runs to the quarter-finals at Indian Wells in March and the semi-finals at Eastbourne in June, but has been unable to stay on the court consistently.

Sir Andy Murray has been part of Draper's coaching team since May, but Montreal was just the second tournament he has been able to play in during their partnership.

Draper has a wild card into next week's Cincinnati Open, but his defeat in Montreal is likely to raise fresh doubts over his participation there and at the US Open.

Sports.title: Brook stars as SunRisers thrash Spirit after setting record Hundred total
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds posted 241-2, the highest score in the history of The Hundred, before cruising to a comfortable victory over London Spirit.

Having been put into bat by Spirit at Headingley, SunRisers openers Mitchell Marsh and Ryan Rickelton put on a record stand of 148 for the first wicket from just 65 balls.

Harry Brook joined in on the fun once Marsh was out for 76 from 37 balls, with the England white-ball captain smashing 55 from just 18 deliveries.

Brook struck a six to bring up his half-century and take SunRisers past the previous highest Hundred total, the 226-4 set by Oval Invincibles against Welsh Fire last year.

After Brook was caught looking for one more boundary, Dan Lawrence added 10 from the final three deliveries, as Rickelton was left stranded six short a century after not finding his way back onto strike for the final eight balls of the innings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Harry Brook's incredible record-equalling 50, the joint fastest in Hundred history

Any hopes Spirit had of staging a remarkable fightback were quickly dampened by Johnny Bairstow getting caught behind by Rickleton from the bowling of Reece Topley with just the second ball of the innings.

Spirit captain Liam Livingstone got the scoreboard moving with 34 from 13 but saw Lhuan-dre Pretorius fall to Topley at the other end before losing his own wicket to Nathan Ellis.

James Coles and James Rew soon also departed to leave Spirit 56-5 from 26 balls, and with the game all but over.

From there, Matthew Revis (38 from 21), David Willey (83 not out from 46) and Jamie Overton (27 not out from 15) put up some resistance, but there was never a realistic prospect of Spirit chasing down the target.

Sports.title: The dangerous jobs of Callum Walsh – the making of a fighter
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh doesn’t shy away from danger. The unbeaten contender from Ireland is looking to break through into the highest echelons of the middleweight division.

On Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he fights former European champion Tyler Denny at the 3Arena in Dublin.

It will be a test for Walsh against a dangerous opponent, one that he welcomes.

"I'm ready for anybody. I love to challenge myself. I love to fight," Walsh told Sky Sports.

"Just tell me when. That's it."

The Irishman is returning to the 3Arena for his first fight in Dublin since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danny O'Donoghue from the Script looks ahead to Callum Walsh's fight in Dublin on the Zuffa Boxing 10 bill.

"It was one of the best nights of my life. Walking out in front of that crowd was insane," the 25-year-old said. "It looks like there was 20,000 people there and it felt like there was 20,000 people there.

"It was crazy. I can't even describe it."

He's come a long way from working on fishing boats as a teenager in Cork. That was a demanding profession with its own kind of dangers.

"I got this fishing job just randomly, I didn't want to work anywhere inside," Walsh remembered.

"It was seven days a week, it was hard work, it wasn't easy but the best job ever in the summer, when it's sunny and you can jump off the boat and swim. You start at four o'clock in the morning. It was very hard [work].

"The worst thing [was] the storms."

He'd haul crab and lobster pots on deck, rebait them and send them back to pulled down by their anchor.

"If you stack them in the wrong order, you're [in trouble]. The whole boat is going to go. Crazy. It's dangerous work," Walsh explained.

"If they're in the wrong order you're going to have rope all over the place, there's going to be stuff flying. You're going to get tangled up, you're going to get dragged overboard, dragged down with them. Even if it's four or five o'clock in the morning you have to be switched on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Walsh can't wait to fight on the Zuffa 10 card in Dublin and is predicting an electric atmosphere.

"[One time] I put them back in the wrong order, my leg got trapped on the side of the boat between the rope and the boat, but we were able to get the boat in reverse quick and I was able to get my leg out. Stuff like that is very dangerous if you don't know what you're doing."

All the while he was pursuing a highly decorated amateur career which saw him winning medals domestically and on the international scene.

But he chose to pursue professional boxing and found his way to Freddie Roach's famous Wild Card gym in LA. He had to prove himself straightaway. Roach threw the youngster into sparring on his first day.

"If you want to train here, you have to spar.' He [Roach] wanted to see if I was even worth being there. I sparred the first day and he told me to come back again tomorrow," Walsh said.

Image: Watch Callum Walsh live on Sky Sports on Saturday. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

"I was in there sparring everybody and anyone for a year and then I made my pro debut.

"Someone will come in [to the Wild Card] for sparring, you know that they're not really supposed to be there," Walsh continued.

"Freddie would tell you: 'Show this guy he's not supposed to be here.' I've knocked so many people out in that gym, I've seen so many people not come back. That's how it is. Freddie Roach's gym is known for being one of the best gyms in the world, known for tough sparring and Freddie he takes pride in that."

His experiences in California helped forge the fighter Walsh is today. "Coming from a massive amateur background, to learning the pro style and how aggressive his pro style is. I think it's the perfect combination," Walsh said.

"Being able to go over to Freddie and learn that aggressive pro style from someone who's had so much experience, I think it's the perfect mixture"

He is determined to show what he can do against Denny on Saturday. "I just believe in my own ability. I just believe if I've trained and prepared to my best I can beat anybody."
