Time-keeping was no longer the issue with Sancho. Now criticism came on his ability to change a game. Since signing for United, Sancho, who has never shown blistering pace, hasn’t hit 10 goals and assists in a single league season. A staggering statistic for a player who scored 50 goals and managed 64 assists in 137 games across four seasons in Germany.

Your browser does not support iframes.

At 20, Sancho was the ‘best young player on the planet bar none,’ Ferdinand claimed, and many other pundits were ready to back that up. At 26, Sancho has played for Manchester United, Chelsea and Aston Villa, gone back to Borussia Dortmund, and is now weighing up what the future holds, and whether that future is to be played out in the Middle East. There will be finger-pointing on all sides and the blame-game, in truth, should be split across the board. There should be no joy in the Sancho story, only sadness. It wasn’t meant to go like this.

Sports.title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar, 49, announces retirement as SummerSlam loss marks end of 26-year career
Sports.content:
WWE legend Brock Lesnar has called time on his 26-year career in the business following his defeat to Oba Femi at SummerSlam at the weekend.

Lesnar, a wrestling great and former MMA star, made the announcement during an appearance on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday.

Following his Hell in a Cell loss to Femi at SummerSlam in Minneapolis, the 10-time WWE champion confirmed the time has finally come for him to bow out.

'I’m here today to let the world know that I am retired and I wanted to say a big thank you to everybody,' he told WWE commentator McAfee and his co-host AJ Hawk. 'Saturday was a very emotional day for me.'

Lesnar, 49, has retired from wrestling and returned in the past, while he appeared to suggest the end was coming after leaving his gloves and boots in the center of the ring in an emotional moment after his WrestleMania 42 match against Femi earlier this year.

Yet despite having enough left to compete again at SummerSlam, he insists that defeat in Minneapolis will go down as his last in the business.

WWE icon Brock Lesnar has announced he is calling time on his 26-year career in the business

Lesnar, a 10-time WWE champion, made the announcement on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show

'I still had some fuel in the tank, but Saturday for Brock Lesnar, that's it. That's it for me in the squared circle and for everything else too,' Lesnar added.

'So I just wanted to give a shout-out to everybody in this universe that has followed me since I was a little kid, all the way till Saturday.'

Lesnar began life with the WWE back in 2002, following a successful college wrestling career that saw him a two-time NJCAA All-American and accrue a staggering 106-5 record over four years.

After signing with the wrestling promotion, he worked his way into the main roster and eventually became one of the biggest stars in the organization.

However, his first stint in the WWE would come to an end in 2004. Following a defeat at WrestleMania XX, he cited burnout, injuries and creative dissatisfaction as his reasons for walking away.

Lesnar returned to the promotion in 2012 and earned a number of WWE championship titles before seemingly retiring at WrestleMania 36.

That decision, however, was short-lived and he returned to the ring in 2021 rocking a new 'cowboy' look that featured a beard and ponytail.

The wrestling great has opted to bow out following his loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam

In 2023, Lesnar was named in a bombshell sex trafficking lawsuit against WWE co-founder Vince McMahon, filed by his former employee Janel Grant.

As a result of the lawsuit, he was removed from the WWE roster and wiped from their event plans. He would endure a two-year exile from the organization.

He returned at Summer Slam in August 2025, despite the Grant lawsuit remaining active at the time. He took part in a handful of fights between then and Sunday night, before officially retiring from the sport a year later.

Though he's best-known for his time in the squared circle, Lesnar also found success away from wrestling. After leaving WWE for the first time in 2004, he attempted to embark on a professional football career.

Lesnar participated in the NFL Scouting Combine at the time but later suffered a broken jaw and hand from a motorcycle accident which put his progress on hold.

Despite the injuries, a number of NFL teams still held an interest in Lesnar and, in July 2004, he signed with the Minnesota Vikings as a defensive tackle. However, his time with the franchise was short-lived and he was eventually released in August.

After his dreams of being on the gridiron came crashing down, he then decided to try his hand - literally - at mixed martial arts.

Lesnar also enjoyed success as an MMA star over the course of his extraordinary career

He began fighting for a promotion known as 'K-1', in April 2006, and won his first bout via submission in the first round - bring global attention to his MMA skills.

Lesnar would eventually sign with Dana White's UFC in 2008, which proved to be a massive success for the organization given his national star power.

Despite losing his first fight, UFC chief White stuck by Lesnar and offered him a multi-fight deal. Again, this proved to a wise call as Lesnar would later become the UFC heavyweight champion following a win over Randy Couture in November 2008.

In total, he had eight UFC fights, winning four of them and losing three - with the final bout being ruled as a no-contest after he tested positive for clomiphene.

Sports.title: NFL star is removed from practice after throwing a punch just weeks after landing $105m contract
Sports.content:
NFL star is removed from practice after throwing a punch just weeks after landing $105m contract

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice on Tuesday after throwing a punch early in a team drill.

As a result of the violent scenes, the All-Pro defensive tackle was forced to spend the rest of practice working on a side field with a strength coach.

First-year head coach Robert Saleh stopped practice after the incident, pulling his Titans together on the field for a reminder to spend the second session in pads working and not fighting.

'Our policy is if you throw a punch you're ejected in the game, same thing with practice,' Saleh said.

'If you throw punch, you're out of practice. But rather than going to the locker room, he went to the other field. He still got his work in. So the projected reps and the work that he would have gotten, he got in off to the side.'

Simmons, who got a very big extension in late June, also had a brief tussle Monday in the Titans' first day in pads.

Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice after throwing a punch

Simmons, who got a big extension in June, also had a brief tussle during Monday's practice

Robert Saleh stopped practice and sent his defensive star to practice on his own in Nashville

On Tuesday, Simmons and center Austin Schlottman scuffled after a play before he swung at right tackle JC Latham. Assistant defensive line coach Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons and took him down out of the scrum.

The Titans went 3-14 last season, and too many penalties for 1,011 yards didn't help.

Latham had the most with 14 penalties, including eight that stalled drives. Simmons ranked second with 12.

Saleh said he wants both lines playing with an edge up to toeing the line.

'We're always going to toe a line of being aggressive and call it instigating if you want,' Saleh said.

'It's just the nature of who we're going to be. But we've got to be disciplined enough to make sure that we always find our way back to the huddle without giving the other team freebies.'

In another concerning moment, left tackle Dan Moore Jr. walked off the field with a trainer.

Saleh had no immediate update after practice. Moore was one of the Titans' big free agent signees in 2025 and a key player for a line already looking for new starters at center and right guard.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward gave fans the play they had been hoping to see late in practice when he threw deep with Carnell Tate, the fourth overall draft pick, running under the ball in the end zone for a 65-yard touchdown.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah closes in on Turkey move: Trabzonspor confirm talks with former Liverpool star who will fly in TODAY ahead of signing a two-year contract
Sports.content:
Trabzonspor are closing in on a two-year deal with former Liverpool forward Mo Salah.

The Turkish club's rivals Besiktas were understood to be the Egyptian's first choice but talks with them stalled last week.

On Tuesday night, Trabzonspor shared a brief message with their 1.9million followers on X, with the club writing: 'Public Announcement: Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our Club.'

The club then posted: 'Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5.

'The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

'The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club's official communication channels during the day.'

Mohammed Salah is closing in on a move to Trabzonspor in Turkey

Trabzonspor also shared a 17-second AI video of a camera shot panning from pyramids over mountains to a view of their 41,000-seater stadium Papara Park.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023.

But Trabzonspor are now set to sign the winger, who fell out with Arne Slot at Anfield last term.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

His long-serving agent, Ramy Abbas, repeatedly insisted nothing had been decided and reaffirmed that stance during the World Cup.

But since returning from the competition in the US, talks have accelerated with interested parties.

Salah, pictured returning to Egypt after the World Cup, looks set to sign a two-year deal

Salah is renowned for his remarkable professionalism and will back himself to remain at a high level deep into his thirties.

Salah was the star man as Slot’s side won the Premier League in Slot's first season, the Egyptian's second English title, but his level dipped last term with just 10 goals last term compared to a staggering 34 when he spear-headed the 2024-25 title win.

Liverpool are yet to replace the player who was voted Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Players' Player of the Year three times at the club.

With the start of the season fast approaching, Bradley Barcola of PSG remains the most likely high-profile attacking signing.

But the 23-year-old, valued at £145million by his club, plays predominantly on the left and Jamie Carragher recently warned against buying him as a replacement for Salah.

Salah would be the most high-profile signing in Trabzonspor's history and if his expected move is confirmed, will join Man United loanee Andre Onana.

Ex-Man City defender Stefan Savic also plays for the Turkish side, who have won their domestic title seven times.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks as pressure continues to mount on the FIFA president.

It comes after Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused him of blackmail.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition – including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and CONCACAF – the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean – are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Jordan, meanwhile, are the first Asian nation to rebel against Infantino – taking the total to 91, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

In a statement Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks

Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein

‘There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time,’ Hussein said.

‘We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

‘First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets - which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‘Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‘This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

‘Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

Daily Mail Sport have contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open
Sports.content:
Jack Draper's torturous attempts to return to tennis continued as he wiped away tears during defeat in the first round of the Canadian Open.

Trailing Frenchman Terence Atmane 4-1 in the deciding set, the British former world No4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept.

It was a truly wretched sight and, while we must wait for the man himself to speak, it seems likely those tears were an indication that he is still feeling the pain of an arm injury which simply will not leave him alone.

Some natural ring-rust aside, there was nothing much wrong with Draper’s level in the first two sets, and when he won the second comfortably he looked well placed to take the match. But his serve began to subside dramatically and by the end he could do little more than just roll it over. The 24-year-old also, in apparent desperation, started to hit an increasing number of dropshots.

Atmane, in terrible form himself, won 6-3, 2-6, 6-2.

It has been well over 12 months now that Draper has struggled with bone bruising in the humerus of his left arm.

Jack Draper was in tears during the third set of his game against Terence Atmane in Montreal as he continues his return from injury 🎾 pic.twitter.com/ekhBse3Af3 — Sky Sports Tennis (@SkySportsTennis) August 4, 2026

Jack Draper was reduced to tears as he lost his comeback match following time out with injury

The British former world No 4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept in the final set

Due to play at Wimbledon, he pulled out the day before his match. Set to return in Washington, he withdrew citing a twinge in that arm.

The injury is clearly chronic and, if this is indeed yet another setback, it is not easy to see where Draper goes from here.

Draper said earlier this week: 'It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

'It's not as simple as 'rest and heal up and you'll come back and you'll be fine'.

Terribly sad to say, it is becoming increasingly likely we may never see the best of this beautifully, brutally brilliant player again.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours as medical completed for transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours as medical completed for transfer

There is plenty happening behind the scenes at Arsenal in terms of transfers

View Image Christian Norgaard travelled to Everton for his medical yesterday (Image: Getty )

More exciting transfer developments involving Arsenal are expected this week. Mikel Arteta’s side are currently preparing for the new campaign, where they will look to defend their Premier League title.

‌



The Gunners’ first official pre-season fixture against Girona ended in a thumping 4-1 victory on Saturday, where £34million summer signing Christos Tzolis was among the scorers. They face Real Betis on Wednesday afternoon, before returning to host Borussia Dortmund and Como at the Emirates.

‌



Aside from Tzolis, it's been a slow transfer window for the 2025/26 Champions League finalists, with sporting director Andrea Berta only otherwise managing to make Piero Hincapie’s move permanent and signing back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier as a free agent.

‌



But, according to The Athletic, Arsenal are now closing in on a complete agreement with Newcastle to sign Bruno Guimaraes, with there being a desire among all parties to bring the situation to a close. The deal is now on course for completion, with the 28-year-old awaiting Newcastle's permission to undergo his medical.

Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks READ MORE :

Berta has not been successful in selling players who are surplus to requirements yet, despite suitors being wanted for Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson and Gabriel Jesus. Yet, most of the Italian’s negotiation work has been conducted behind the scenes, with Arsenal hoping that bears fruit in the coming weeks, before the transfer window shuts on September 1.

‌



Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer stories involving the Gunners.

Christian Norgaard’s medical

Christian Norgaard completed a medical at Everton on Tuesday ahead of his permanent move away from Arsenal. The Danish midfielder was signed only a year ago from Brentford in a surprise deal worth an initial £10m plus £2m in add-ons.

Norgaard did not play as much as he would have liked last season, making just seven Premier League appearances - none of which were as a starter. Yet, the 32-year-old veteran was highly respected around the club for his leadership and role within the dressing room

‌



And he will leave north London as a Premier League champion ahead of his £7m transfer to Everton. Norgaard had been in Girona with the Arsenal squad last weekend for the 4-1 victory over the Spanish side but did not participate in the match as negotiations with Everton advanced. He was then given approval by the Gunners to complete all formalities ahead of signing a multi-year deal with the Toffees.

Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours

Bruno Guimaraes shared an image of himself joining Newcastle’s pre-season training camp on Monday amid reports of his impending move to Arsenal, before getting back to work on Tuesday. The Magpies captain has been at the centre of a long summer transfer saga, with the Gunners keen to land the midfielder.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Guimaraes is understood to have agreed personal terms with Arsenal, having told Newcastle of his desire to leave, but will not force through a move if an agreement isn’t reached between the two clubs. He showed that, and with it his professionalism as captain, by joining up with the rest of the Newcastle squad.

The 28-year-old Brazilian was initially meant to return from his extended post-World Cup break on Sunday but the club were happy for him to arrive 24 hours later. He did exactly that and posted an image of him in La Manga, where they are training in Spain, showing he is still a Newcastle player.

It was reported earlier this week that the Magpies rejected an opening official bid from Arsenal worth £75m. And the champions of England are expected to wrap up the deal shortly, following the latest reports surrounding the deal.

Sports.title: Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season
Sports.content:
Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season

UEFA has updated its regulations and made changes which will affect the nine English clubs playing in either the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League in the 2026-27 season

View 2 Images Qualifying for the 2026-27 Champions League has begun (Image: Kristian Skeie - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

UEFA have announced two rule changes ahead of this season's Champions League. Qualifying for the competition has already started, with the draw for the league phase not until late August.

‌



The same goes for UEFA's other primary competitions, the Conference League and Europa League. And the regulations for each competition have been updated, with two changes announced on Tuesday.

‌



Firstly, the yellow card threshold has been raised. A player will now need four yellow cards rather than three to pick up the first one-match ban.

‌



And secondly, UEFA have removed its long-standing regulation that prevented stadium clocks moving beyond 45 and 90 minutes. This change has been seen in the Premier League for the last two years.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement READ MORE :

The draw for the Champions League play-off round was made on Monday. Celtic are the only British club involved in the round and will face LASK of Austria in their bid to reach the league phase.

‌



Five English teams will play in the 2026-27 Champions League. Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool qualified through their league position.

In the Europa League, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland will feature. And in the Conference League, which Palace won last season, Brighton are the Premier League's sole representatives.

What do you make of the rule changes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Paris Saint-Germain will once again bid to defend their crown (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

UEFA has been in the headlines over the past week after its 55 member nations unanimously voted to pull out of FIFA competitions during an emergency virtual meeting on Friday. It comes after FIFA controversially unveiled plans to sell off its competitions to private investors.

In response, the European body said: "As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

‌



UEFA invited other confederations to follow their lead and reportedly believe that a number of Asian countries are also against the plan. "National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences," it added.

"This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation - an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits

Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr has been sent a clear message by Jose Mourinho as the Gunners await a final decision on his future

View 2 Images Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has revealed to Vinicius Jr what he expects of him (Image: (Photo by WOLFGANG JANNACH / APA / AFP via Getty Images))

Jose Mourinho has told Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr to enjoy himself, be positive and continue playing his style of football. The 25-year-old is back training in the Spanish capital after his break following Brazil's World Cup exit but the focus has instead been on his future amid significant interest from the Gunners.

‌



Vinicius has just one year remaining on his current contract and while there has not been a breakthrough in extension talks for some time, that could be about to change with new discussions set to take place on Wednesday.

‌



As such, Arsenal could be about to learn a definitive transfer outcome over his future with Real's stance clear that he either agrees to extend or is sold this summer.

‌



OPINION Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal by Fasika Zelealem

In the meantime, the forward has been putting in the hard yards alongside his Real team-mates under Mourinho's watchful eye.

In a video posted to Real's official social media channels, he lifted the lid on exactly what the new Los Blancos chief expects from him.

‌



The 26-year-old said: "He wants me to be just as I've always been - happy, positive and playing my own style of football."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



A large number of Real Madrid's recent posts have centred on his comeback, with a 'train with Vini Jr' montage shared on Monday.

In the latest clip, Vinicius goes on to discuss the training sessions he has taken part in so far and looks ahead to the forthcoming season — comments that strongly suggest he has no desire to leave.

Real chiefs appear to be the ones pushing for a departure, with the contract proposal that has been available for some time falling short of Vinicius' salary expectations. Since his return, there have been claims that an enhanced offer has been tabled which would see him earn approximately €22m (£18.9m) per year, though even that remains insufficient.

‌



Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta and head coach Mikel Arteta, who is now said to be heavily involved in negotiations, seem prepared to meet his financial requirements.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Andrea Berta are targeting a move for Vinicius Jr

Vinicius Jr stands as the club's primary attacking target, with Arteta eager to bolster his squad that may be somewhat depleted during the opening weeks of the 2026/27 campaign owing to the World Cup.

‌



Multiple midfielders could be absent for the initial fixtures, but the Premier League champions appear poised to secure an addition that will enhance Arteta's choices. Following his belated return to Newcastle United pre-season training, Arsenal are close to finalising a deal for Bruno Guimaraes.

Progress in that transfer situation comes after Everton launched a bid for Christian Norgaard, with that deal also anticipated to be concluded this week.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power

FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure to step down from his role over plans to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plan is rapidly falling apart (Image: DANIEL DUARTE/AFP via Getty Images)

Under-fire FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called his senior staff to a crisis meeting in a bid to cling to power. The desperate move comes after Arsene Wenger, FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, broke rank and criticised Infantino's controversial plan to sell off competitions including the World Cup.

‌



Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Monday saying that the withdrawal of Infantino's plan was 'absolutely necessary'. Meanwhile, Infantino's close allies are said to have been urging many of the 211 member associations to publicly back him after some withdrew their support for his re-election - while the president of one federation accused him of 'blackmail'.

‌



The Times report that Infantino has called staff to the Moroccan capital of Rabat for a crisis meeting. The Swiss chief is holed up in Morocco amid the swam of backlash.

‌



It's added that a group of senior staff within FIFA had a management meeting on Tuesday - without Infantino. All bar one reportedly opposed the plan to sell off FIFA's competitions.

Gianni Infantino accused of blackmail by Jordan FA chief in brutal FIFA criticism READ MORE :

Full list of Gianni Infantino's supporters and critics as FIFA president faces fight for job READ MORE :

Wenger's comments have also piled on pressure. " The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," the Frenchman said.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

‌



Even Infantino's No.2, FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, was revealed to have slammed the plan in a leaked email. " We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations." Grafstrom wrote.

Should Gianni Infantino step down? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger has broken rank and criticised the scheme (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



"A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure."

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back

The battle for ownership at West Ham United has intensified after Daniel Kretinsky responded to Amanda Staveley’s consortium agreeing a £150m deal with the family of David Gold

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley (Image: (Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Amanda Staveley has suffered a blow in her attempt to buy into West Ham United after Daniel Kretinsky agreed to sell just over 2% of his stake in the club to Jakub Havrlant.

‌



Within the last few days, Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, and others agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the Hammers, who were relegated to the Championship last season.

‌



Staveley’s consortium agreed a £150million deal with the family of the late David Gold on Saturday. But before Staveley can buy it, existing shareholders have first refusal at the price she agreed.

‌



However, Hammers co-chair Kretinsky sold just over 2% of his stake in the club to Czech businessman Havrlant on Tuesday, dealing a blow to Staveley and her consortium. As a result of the deal, BBC Sport explain Kretinsky can now buy Gold's 25.1% stake without his own stake exceeding 50%, which would otherwise force him to make an offer for the remainder of the club.

"I am delighted Jakub Havrlant has joined the West Ham ownership group as a shareholder, subject to the pre-emption process," Kretinsky said. "He brings exceptional experience as an investor and digital innovator and I have no doubt his involvement will strengthen our club."

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



While speaking on an episode of Bloomberg’s Leaders with Francine Lacqua recorded before West Ham confirmed her agreement with Gold on Saturday, Staveley revealed she is planning a 'big property play' in English football.

She said: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.

“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me. That’s where you get value uplift — when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

‌



View 2 Images West Ham United co-chair Daniel Kretinsky (c) looks on during the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023 (Image: (Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images))

Royal Mail owner Kretinsky bought 27% of West Ham in 2021 and for his plan he may need the help of the club’s third-largest shareholder, the American billionaire Albert Tripp Smith, who owns 8 per cent. While The Times are reporting that there are set to be two rounds of bidding.

In the first round, shareholders have 30 days to buy their entitlement, which is up to the same proportion as their present holding. And in the second round, any remaining Gold shares can be bought by shareholders who participated in the first round.

West Ham get their 2026/27 campaign underway on Saturday with a first round League Cup tie against Portsmouth at the London Stadium.

Sports.title: Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint
Sports.content:
Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint

Michael Carrick left out Radek Vitek for Manchester United's most recent pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid and the goalkeeper is now on the verge of sealing a move away

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is set to leave Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Middlesbrough over the sale of Radek Vitek. The goalkeeper has been in search of regular game time after an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season.

‌



Vitek, 22, started United's first two pre-season friendlies under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford. But Carrick left him on the bench for the Red Devils' 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Saturday in a hint at his impending departure.

‌



Now, Vitek is on the verge of completing a move to the Riverside. Multiple reports say that the Czech is close to signing for Middlesbrough on a permanent basis, adding that United will insert both a sell-on clause and a buy-back option into the deal. No fee has emerged at this stage.

‌



Having swept the end-of-season awards at Bristol City, Vitek found himself in high demand. The 22-year-old made it clear at the start of pre-season that he was 'ready' to leave.

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

"I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see," Vitek told reporters. "We will see what is going to happen.

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Vitek isn't the only United player who could be on the move in the coming days. Joshua Zirkzee has given the green light to join Juventus while Altay Bayindir is a target for Besiktas.

Who should Manchester United sign before the transfer window closes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Radek Vitek wants regular game time (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

As far as incomings go, United have made three signings this summer. Goalkeeper Karl Darlow was brought in on a free transfer to serve as backup to Senne Lammens, while midfield duo Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined for a combined £85million.

Carrick would like to add a third midfielder, particularly after Manuel Ugarte picked up a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will be ruled out for most of the season. However, the Red Devils hierarchy are weighing up whether to prioritise other areas instead.

Left-back is a position which United want to strengthen, with Luke Shaw's fitness always a concern and Patrick Dorgu being used further forward since Carrick was appointed. Newcastle's Lewis Hall is a target and he'd be open to the switch, but it'd likely take a huge fee to prise him away from a club who've already made big sales this summer.

Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino accused of blackmail by Jordan FA chief in brutal FIFA criticism

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been hit with a damning accusation of blackmail by Jordan football association president Prince Ali Al Hussein

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan's FA president Prince Ali Al Hussein (Image: (Photo by KARIM JAAFAR / AFP via Getty Images))

Jordan football association president Prince Ali Al Hussein has shockingly claimed he was told during the World Cup that his nation would benefit if he endorsed Gianni Infantino. The FIFA president has endured a whirlwind few weeks with his controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors scrapped following severe backlash.

‌



Several governing body's slammed his proposal and a member of one nation's FA that was at the World Cup has gone one step further by suggesting blackmail attempts were made. Prince Ali also revealed Jordan are yet to be paid for reaching the final of a FIFA event alongside several other issues.

‌



Part of his X post read: "For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters- until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‌



Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Arsene Wenger forced to break silence on Gianni Infantino's disastrous World Cup plan READ MORE :

"We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."

His full message stated: "There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time. We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

"First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted VISAS, even though they had tickets -which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Secondly, we are being taxed by the US govt through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‌



"This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

"Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been hit with serious accusations

‌



"The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve."

Infantino performed a hefty U-turn on his hopes for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) with all plans scrapped. Pressure on his job remains significant with FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom blasting him in a leaked email.

Arsene Wenger later issued a public statement, outlining the responsibilties of his role within FIFA in an attempt to distance himself from Infantino.

UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation spoke out against his proposal with the former also threatening legal action.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
