The Strategic Communication Adviser however alerted journalists and media managers to what he described as ongoing attempts by “desperate, highly ambitious but hopeless politicians” to fabricate allegations against the state government.

According to him, these individuals were seeking to use media platforms to make baseless claims with the aim of undermining the achievements recorded by the current administration.

“Kebbi State administration under Governor Nasir Idris has changed the narrative of the state’s development through the execution of high-quality infrastructure and programmes that have positively transformed the socio-economic fortunes of our people,” Zuru said.

“That is why the opposition has become hopeless in pursuing selfish political interests,” he added, stressing that the government remained focused on service delivery.

He further alleged that some of the politicians behind the campaign of calumny had previously served at the national level but failed to impact their communities, while instead accumulating questionable wealth now being investigated and prosecuted in various courts.

At IMS Online Television, the Managing Director, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar, thanked the team for the visit and commended the remarkable achievements of the Governor Nasir Idris administration.

He pledged that the station would continue to uphold the principles of justice, fairness, and the ethics of journalism in its reportage.

His counterpart at Skylight Television, Engineer Isiyaka Abdulaziz, also lauded the administration, saying the station identified with the “unprecedented and visible development” recorded by the Comrade Governor in the last three years.

The visit, according to the media team, forms part of efforts to strengthen collaboration between government and the media in promoting accurate information and developmental journalism in Kebbi State.

World.title: Aondoakaa Decries New Killings in Benue
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Benue State, Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, has condemned the latest attack on Abaashwa community in Mbaasar, Nzorov Council Ward of Guma Local Government Area of the state, where suspected armed herdsmen killed four people.

In a statement, yesterday, by his media aide, James Ian, the PDP governorship candidate described the attack as “barbaric, heartbreaking and yet another painful reminder of the worsening security situation in Benue State.”

While extending his condolences to the families, who lost their loved ones in the attack and praying for the speedy recovery of those currently receiving treatment for injuries sustained during the assault, Aondoakaa expressed deep concern over the deteriorating security situation in the state.

He stressed that the true test of effective security lay in preventing attacks rather than merely responding after lives had been lost.

“Recurring attacks on Benue communities have created an atmosphere of fear, forcing many farmers away from their ancestral lands and threatening the state’s agricultural economy,” he said.

Aondoakaa noted that the people of the state desired concrete security measures that would end the endless cycle of killings and displacement.

He appealed to the state government to appreciate that the protection of lives and property remained its foremost constitutional responsibility and should therefore command greater attention.

“Every available resource, every security architecture and every policy initiative should be directed towards achieving that sacred responsibility. Benue people deserve security, not endless condolences,” he said.

The governorship candidate also expressed concern over reports that some injured victims experienced delays in accessing prompt medical attention due to the ongoing industrial action by doctors in the state.

He, however, urged the authorities to make emergency arrangements to ensure that victims of violent attacks received immediate medical care capable of saving lives.

World.title: Osun State University College Provost, Prof Yusuf, Marks Era of Transformation as She Hands Over
World.content:
• Says 90 scholarships, educational grants, financial support awarded to students

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo





The immediate past Provost of Osun State University College of Education, Professor Florence Yusuf has made it clear that more than 90 scholarships, educational grants and financial support were awarded through collaborations with philanthropists and development partners to students of the college.

Professor Yusuf who stated this during the handling over ceremony which marks the era of transformation in the college said the idea was to ensure financial challenges did not become barriers to academic success.

According to her “After four transformative years at the helm of the affairs I had formally handed over leadership, leaving behind a legacy of unprecedented academic expansion, student welfare initiatives and institutional development that has repositioned the college as a beacon of teacher education in Nigeria.”

While presenting her stewardship report covering the 2022–2026 academic sessions, the outgoing Provost painted a picture of remarkable progress, highlighting the introduction of four new undergraduate programmes and the development of seven additional programmes now awaiting National Universities Commission verification.

She stressed that, “Throughout my tenure, I worked collaboratively with the university management, staff, students, alumni, and stakeholders to strengthen the academic, administrative, and professional standing of the College,’ Professor Yusuf stated during the handover ceremony.

“The College witnessed significant academic expansion with the introduction of B.Sc. (Ed). programmes in Business Education, Environmental Education, Adult and Continuing Education and Computer Education.

“Seven additional programmes, including Ph.D. offerings in English Language Education, Measurement and Evaluation, Curriculum Studies and Science Education, have been fully developed and prepared for NUC resource verification.”

Beyond the College, Professor Yusuf also provided leadership at the university level, serving as chairman of the Committee of Provosts, Deans and Directors for two terms.

Under her stewardship, the Committee recorded significant progress in policy harmonization, academic quality assurance, and inter-college collaboration, further strengthening the University’s governance structure and advancing its strategic objectives.

“Perhaps the most heartwarming achievement of the tenure was the unprecedented scholarship support extended to students.

“Under Professor Yusuf’s leadership, more than 90 scholarships, educational grants and financial support were awarded through collaborations with philanthropists and development partners, ensuring that financial challenges did not become barriers to academic success. “

“The scholarship initiative, which touched students across various academic levels and local government areas, represented one of the most extensive student support programmes in the College’s history.”

“In a move that significantly enhanced the College’s intellectual visibility, the administration successfully institutionalised the Annual Lecture Series, with four editions organised between 2022 and 2026. “

However, the events attracted distinguished scholars, policymakers, educationists and captains of industry, fostering meaningful discourse on contemporary educational issues.

“Similarly, three editions of the Annual Conference of Education brought together academics and researchers from various institutions, further cementing the College’s reputation at national and international levels. “

She posited that the College organised four Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) Induction Programmes during the tenure, enhancing the professional development of graduating education students and strengthening their professional identity as certified teachers.

She emphasized that recognising that human resources constitute the foundation of institutional excellence, the administration recruited 36 additional academic staff members and three Technologists, significantly improving teaching, research, and student support services.

Prof. Yusuf stressed the major milestone was the establishment of a functional College Resource Centre, made possible through donor generosity, which has improved access to academic and instructional resources while providing a conducive environment for teaching, learning, and research.

She also made it cleared that staff recognition and excellence awards were institutionalised, with the Vice-Chancellor receiving the Exemplary Leadership Award, while four dedicated staff members were honoured for their invaluable contributions to the College’s development.

She however, recommended that “the incoming administration pursue NUC resource verification for all newly developed programmes, sustain the flagship academic events, expand scholarship initiatives through stronger partnerships, and prioritise be infrastructure development.”

“I do so with gratitude, fulfilment, and confidence that the solid foundation laid during this administration will support even greater accomplishments in the years ahead,’ the outgoing Provost concluded.”

World.title: Another Nigeria is Possible: ActionAid, Social Movement Leaders Demand New Social Order at Cotonou Forum
World.content:
• Civil society groups rally West Africa against inequality, insecurity, poor governance, shrinking civic space

Michael Olugbode in Abuja





A coalition of leading civil society actors in Nigeria has renewed calls for a people-centred transformation of the country, declaring that a new Nigeria built on justice, accountability and inclusion is possible.

The call was made as the Steering Committee of the Nigeria Social Forum (NSF) and ActionAid Nigeria extended solidarity to the ongoing World Social Forum (WSF) in Cotonou, Benin, urging activists, social movements and democratic forces across the globe to unite against rising inequality, economic injustice, climate crises and threats to civic freedoms.

In a strongly worded statement on Monday, the organisations said the gathering in Cotonou represented a critical moment for citizens and movements to forge stronger alliances and develop practical solutions to challenges confronting millions of people.

“Another World Is Possible,” the groups declared, reaffirming the historic slogan of the World Social Forum, which since 2001 has served as a global platform for communities, workers, women, young people, indigenous groups and civil society organisations to advance alternatives to systems they describe as unjust and exclusionary.

The statement, signed by ActionAid Nigeria Country Director, Comrade Andrew Mamedu, NSF Chairman, Comrade Jaye Gaskia, and other prominent civil society leaders, said the ideals of the World Social Forum remain relevant as nations struggle with deepening social and economic inequalities.

The groups warned that Nigeria continues to face a combination of challenges, including widespread unemployment, insecurity, climate-related shocks, gender inequality, declining civic space and concerns over accountable governance.

“Today, these values are more urgent than ever,” the statement said, stressing that millions of Nigerians continue to experience hardship despite the country’s vast human and natural resources.

However, the civil society leaders noted that grassroots organisations and social movements have remained resilient by defending human rights, organising communities and amplifying the voices of vulnerable groups.

They argued that the challenges facing workers, women, youths, rural communities and persons living with disabilities are interconnected and require collective action rather than isolated interventions.

“When one voice is silenced, democracy grows weaker. When one community is left behind, the nation falls short of its promise. That is why solidarity is not optional; it is necessary,” the groups stated.

The coalition urged participants at the Cotonou forum to move beyond discussions by building cross-border partnerships capable of influencing policy and driving social change.

Among the key priorities outlined were strengthening alliances across West Africa and beyond, defending civic freedoms, advancing climate justice and demanding greater transparency and accountability from governments.

The organisations also called on civil society actors to ensure that resolutions from the forum translate into concrete actions within communities.

“We believe that another Nigeria is possible — a Nigeria where public institutions serve the people, where young people can realise their potential, where women participate equally in leadership, and where development leaves no one behind,” they stated.

The Nigeria Social Forum and ActionAid Nigeria reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of the World Social Forum Charter, including openness, pluralism, non-violence, solidarity and participatory democracy.

The statement was also endorsed by other members of the Steering Committee, including Comrade Otive Igbuzor, Comrade Eze Nwangu, Comrade Priscilia Achakpa, Comrade Abiola Akiyode Afolabi and Comrade Ene Obi.

The World Social Forum in Cotonou is bringing together civil society organisations, activists, social movements and community leaders from across Africa and other regions to deliberate on pathways towards a fairer, more inclusive and sustainable world.

For Nigeria’s civil society movement, the message from Cotonou is clear: without justice, inclusion and accountable leadership, development cannot be truly meaningful.

World.title: Orlando Pirates to refund fans locked out of stadium
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have apologised to supporters who were unable to enter Orlando Amstel Arena during last Saturday's Betway Premiership clash against Milford FC. Image: Orlando Pirates website

Orlando Pirates have apologised to supporters who were unable to enter Orlando Amstel Arena during last Saturday’s Betway Premiership clash against Milford FC after stadium gates were closed on safety grounds.

The Soweto giants confirmed that the decision to lock down the venue was taken by the Venue Operations Centre (VOC) during the match to protect the safety of spectators, players, officials and staff.

Counterfeit tickets blamed

According to the club, the lockdown was triggered by the activities of criminal syndicates operating in and around the stadium precinct.



Pirates said the groups were selling counterfeit match tickets and facilitating the unlawful entry of people without valid tickets, creating an unacceptable safety risk and compromising crowd management.

The club stressed that the decision to close the gates was beyond its control but acknowledged the frustration experienced by genuine supporters who were left outside despite holding valid tickets.

Refund process announced

To assist affected fans, Orlando Pirates have appointed Open Tickets to manage the refund process.

Supporters who purchased valid match tickets but were unable to gain entry because of the stadium lockdown can apply for a refund by contacting support@opentickets.co.za.

The club said only supporters who held valid tickets and were prevented from entering due to the lockdown would qualify for refunds.

Commitment to improve security

Orlando Pirates said they remain committed to working with the Premier Soccer League, stadium management, law enforcement agencies and other stakeholders to strengthen matchday operations and combat criminal activity around the stadium.



The Buccaneers added that the aim is to ensure a safe, secure and enjoyable matchday experience for all supporters while preventing the sale of counterfeit tickets and unlawful access to future fixtures.

Orlando Pirates kicked off their defence of the Betway Premiership title with a 2-0 win over Milford FC.

Orlando Pirates will next be in action in a home MTN8 quarter-final against Durban City on Saturday, 8 August at 15:00.

The Buccaneers’ next league assignment will be away from home against AmaZulu on Wednesday, 12 August at 19:30.

World.title: Daily Snow Report: Forecasters monitor major snow system
World.content:
Calm conditions across most of South Africa today, with forecasters watching what comes next: Image ChatGPT

South Africa is enjoying another largely calm winter’s day on Wednesday, 5 August, with no widespread weather warnings in place as forecasters continue to monitor the possibility of a significant snow event later this week.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued only a Yellow Level 1 warning for damaging winds and waves between Table Bay and Cape Agulhas, valid from Wednesday afternoon until Thursday morning.

An extremely high fire danger warning also remains in place for the eastern parts of the Northern Cape.



Mostly fine conditions across the country

According to SAWS, most provinces can expect fine and cool to warm conditions throughout the day.

Gauteng will remain fine and cool, while Mpumalanga is expected to experience morning frost over the Highveld before warming up across the Lowveld later in the day.

Elsewhere, conditions will remain mostly dry, although partly cloudy skies with isolated rain and showers are possible in some areas.

Apart from the coastal wind and wave warning and the fire danger alert, no additional impact-based weather warnings have been issued.

Attention turns to next week’s snow threat

While conditions remain settled for now, weather forecasters are closely watching a developing system that could bring widespread snowfall to South Africa between 9 and 11 August.

Early forecast models indicate the potential for a multi-day snow event affecting every province, including areas that do not typically experience snowfall.



However, meteorologists have cautioned that the forecast remains at an early stage and is likely to change over the coming days as newer weather data becomes available.

Should the system develop as currently projected, it could bring significant snowfall to several parts of the country and disrupt travel on major routes.

For now, South Africans can expect another relatively quiet winter’s day before attention shifts to what could become one of the season’s most notable weather events.

I’ll be keeping a close eye on how that forecast evolves as the weekend approaches, since a nationwide snow event would be a genuinely rare sight.

Are you hoping the cold holds off a little longer, or are you ready for another snowy weekend?

World.title: Why Africa continues to back Gianni Infantino despite growing FIFA opposition
World.content:
Africa could play a decisive role in Infantino's future. Image via X@mauritaniefoot

African football leaders are once again emerging as some of FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s strongest allies, even as football officials in Europe, Asia and North and Central America question his leadership.

According to Reuters, influential football administrators from Morocco, Egypt, Niger, Mauritania and the Democratic Republic of Congo have publicly backed Infantino following his decision to abandon a controversial proposal to sell a stake in future FIFA World Cup revenues.

The statements come at a critical time for the FIFA president ahead of next year’s presidential election, with Africa’s 54 member associations representing one of the largest voting blocs within world football.



Why Africa continues to back Infantino

Many African football associations depend on FIFA development funding to supplement limited commercial revenue, sponsorship and broadcasting income.

Since taking office in 2016, Gianni Infantino has overseen a significant expansion of the FIFA Forward Programme, increasing financial support for member associations to fund football infrastructure, administration, competitions, youth development and women’s football.

For many African federations, these funds have helped finance stadium renovations, training facilities, grassroots programmes and operational costs that would otherwise be difficult to sustain.

Speaking to Reuters, Comoros Football Federation president Saïd Ali Athouman said financial support remains one of African football’s biggest priorities.

“Our problem is how to obtain money. Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete?” he said.

He added that wealthier football nations enjoy better infrastructure and resources, making it difficult for smaller associations to compete internationally.



The importance of FIFA funding was also highlighted by Football Association of Malawi president Fleetwood Haiya.

“Malawi needs money. Malawi needs stadiums,” Haiya told Reuters.

Under FIFA’s current funding model, each of its 211 member associations is guaranteed baseline funding of US$8 million over a four-year cycle.

In recent years, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) has also introduced annual grants for its member associations, providing an additional financial boost.

For many smaller football nations, these resources remain essential to improving infrastructure, organising domestic competitions and supporting national teams.

CAF yet to take an official position on Infantino

Despite individual expressions of support, CAF itself has not officially endorsed Infantino.

The continental governing body is expected to discuss the matter during its Executive Committee meeting on Thursday after the FIFA president withdrew his controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal under pressure.

Reuters reported that the proposal sought to raise about US$4.2 billion through a new commercial rights company linked to future World Cup revenues but faced significant resistance from several football confederations.

CAF had previously indicated it would study the proposal before Infantino abandoned the plan.

Africa could play a decisive role in Infantino’s future

While football authorities in Europe, Asia and the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) have reportedly expressed declining confidence in Infantino’s leadership, Africa’s position could prove crucial ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next March.

With 54 voting member associations, Africa remains one of the most influential blocs in FIFA politics.

For many African football leaders, continued access to development funding and investment remains a central consideration, helping explain why support for Infantino has remained stronger on the continent than elsewhere.

Although CAF has yet to announce a collective position, the public backing from several senior African football officials suggests Infantino can still count on significant support from a continent that has been instrumental to his leadership since his election in 2016.

World.title: Club Med shock: Worker named, released on bail over teen rape allegations
World.content:
Club Med French employee granted on bail over rape allegation. Image via Instagram @clubmedsa

A French employee working at Club Med Tinley Manor in KwaZulu-Natal has been released on bail after being accused of raping a teenage guest.

CLUB MED FRENCH WORKER RELEASED ON BAIL OVER RAPE ALLEGATION

A French worker, 35-year-old Guy Marchandier, at the new Club Med Tinley Manor in KwaZulu-Natal has been released on bail after being accused of raping a teenage guest at the resort.

The incident reportedly took place over the weekend of 3 to 4 August, when a 17-year-old guest alleged that she had been sexually assaulted.



The matter was immediately reported to the South African Police Service, who arrested the suspect and opened a case of rape.

The accused appeared in the KwaDukuza Magistrate’s Court on Monday 4 August.

Despite the seriousness of the charges, the court granted the accused bail of R5 000.

As part of his bail conditions, he must remain in South Africa until the case is finalised and comply with restrictions set by the court. He is expected to return later this month for further proceedings.

Police have confirmed that the investigation is ongoing.

CONCERN OVER SAFETY

The case has drawn attention to the new resort, raising questions about guest safety and the protection of minors.



The incident has caused shock in Tinley Manor and across the province with parents and community members voicing concern about the vulnerability of young guests at resorts.

Many have called for stricter supervision and accountability, urging hospitality venues to strengthen safeguarding policies and staff vetting processes.

This case also comes at a time when South Africa is facing growing scrutiny over safety in tourism and hospitality spaces.

Incidents like this highlight the importance of clear safeguarding measures and the need for resorts to prioritise the protection of minors.

Siya Kolisi’s “girlfriend” Rachel John recently visited this resort, which she described as “not bad”.

World.title: Cape Town set to experience 15-hour water supply disruption from Friday
World.content:
The City of Cape Town has confirmed that some areas will experience a 15-hour water supply disruption on Friday, 7 August.

The Water and Sanitation Directorate said the planned maintenance forms part of ongoing efforts to upgrade critical infrastructure and improve water supply across the city.

CAPE TOWN AREAS SET TO EXPERIENCE 15-HOUR WATER SUPPLY DISRUPTION

The City of Cape Town said planned maintenance work, including pipe and valve installations, repairs, and replacements, will result in water supply disruption to these areas:



Century City, Tygerhof, Brooklyn, Koeberg, Ysterplaat, Summer Greens, Milnerton, Kensington, Factreton, Maitland, Goodwood, Athlone, Langa, WP Showgrounds, Pinelands, Thornton, Parow, Ruyterwacht and GrandWest.

The water supply to these areas will be temporarily disrupted from 19:00 on Friday, 7 August, until 10:00 on Saturday, 8 August, and again from 19:00 on Saturday, 8 August, until 10:00 on Sunday, 9 August. This will enable the City of Cape Town’s Bulk Water Operations team to conduct acoustic leak detection testing on a critical bulk water pipeline as part of a broader condition assessment programme aimed at assessing the condition and reliability of the City’s water infrastructure. The municipality said water tankers will be made available where required to provide water for essential domestic use as and where required.

Myhof Road, Claremont

The City will shut off the water supply to Myhof Road, Claremont and surrounding roads on Wednesday, 5 August, from 09:00 until 18:00 to enable the appointed contractor to complete a new water connection. The affected area includes Myhof Road between Warrington Road and the Access Park entrance in Myhof Road.

RSE TUNNEL MAINTENANCE

Planned National Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS) RSE tunnel maintenance shutdown

The City of Cape Town said the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS) has notified all affected water users that the Theewaterskloof Dam to Riviersonderend (RSE) Berg River Tunnel will be shut down from 10 to 26 August 2026 to allow for essential inspection and maintenance work on the tunnel infrastructure.



“This shutdown will significantly reduce the availability of raw water during this period. To ensure that sufficient raw water remains available for the production of potable water at Blackheath Water Treatment Plant throughout the shutdown period, the City of Cape Town’s Water and Sanitation Directorate will close the supply from the RSE Tunnel to the Faure RSE raw water pipeline. Residents are requested to reduce their water consumption during this period,” the municipality said.

World.title: Woman in Home Affairs video speaks: ‘Do not tolerate corruption!’
World.content:
A Port Elizabeth woman has claimed in a video that has gone viral that Home Affairs approached her to pay a bribe in exchange for accelerated services.

The incident took place at her local branch.

WOMAN CLAIMS HOME AFFAIRS OFFICIALS WANTED BRIBE

In a video posted on social media, a woman named Amanda Shaw was seen causing a commotion at her local Home Affairs branch in Port Elizabeth.



Shaw, wearing a white dress, stood on a chair as she explained that she had been approached by officials who asked her to pay R150 to skip the queue.

“I’m phoning the police!”, she exclaimed in the video.

In a Facebook post, the woman shared that she visited the branch to apply for her children’s passports. She felt compelled to speak out against corruption.

She shared: “I climbed onto a chair in Home Affairs and rebelled against their corruption! For R150, you can get your ID or passport pick-up card in 10 minutes. Or in 20 min you can have your new ID card done and dusted.

“As I pulled up to Home Affairs in my BMW X4. I was approached with an offer to pay R150, and I will be helped in 10 minutes. I decline the offer….I watched closely as customers who arrived after me were helped.

She added, “No way, Home Affairs. I will not pay you!.



The woman added that she had tried to call authorities to report the incident but was unsuccessful.

‘EVERY CROOKED OFFICIAL WILL BE CAUGHT’

While the Department of Home Affairs has not officially responded to the video, Minister Leon Schreiber has previously sent a stark warning to employees who engage in illegal behaviour.

Speaking out after the arrest of another two officials involved in fraud and corruption in May, the Minister said: “We are now securing dismissals, arrests and prosecutions on a near-weekly basis as Home Affairs ramps up our cleanup operation.

Every crooked official and complicit member of the public must know that it is now only a matter of time until their turn arrives.

“As our crackdown accelerates, the days of sleeping soundly are over for the corrupt. They now need to spend every moment wondering when it will be their turn. My answer to them is simple: sooner than you think. We will not rest until we have rid Home Affairs of every single rotten apple through this combination of dismissals and criminal convictions.”

World.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day smashes South African box office records
World.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has officially become the biggest opening weekend release in South African box office history. Image: Sony Pictures

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has officially become the biggest opening weekend release in South African box office history, earning R44 million during its debut weekend in cinemas.

Sony Pictures South Africa confirmed the record-breaking performance, with the latest instalment in the Marvel Cinematic Universe surpassing every previous local cinema opening and providing another major boost for the country’s recovering film industry.

🇿🇦 Thank You, South Africa!



You've made history.



Celebrating the biggest opening weekend in South African cinema history, with an incredible R44+ million at the South African box office.#ThankYouSouthAfrica #BoxOfficeHistory #SpidermanBrandNewDay #SonyPicturesSA pic.twitter.com/vdqX0O4AwO  August 3, 2026

Biggest opening ever in South Africa

The superhero blockbuster drew packed cinemas across the country, with social media flooded by spoiler-free reactions, fan theories and videos of enthusiastic audiences.

Many viewers praised the film’s emotional storyline, spectacular action sequences and the return of Tom Holland as Peter Parker following the dramatic events of Spider-Man: No Way Home.

The film currently holds an impressive 98% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, reflecting overwhelmingly positive fan reception.

For South African exhibitors, the record-breaking debut is another sign that audiences continue to embrace the big-screen experience for major blockbuster releases.

Breaking records worldwide

The success hasn’t been limited to South Africa.

Internationally, Spider-Man: Brand New Day opened to an estimated $932 million (approximately R17 billion) worldwide, including around $360 million from North America alone.



The domestic opening was enough to edge past Avengers: Endgame as the biggest opening weekend in North American box office history, although Endgame still retains the record for the largest global opening weekend with $1.2 billion.

The latest Spider-Man adventure has also set new industry benchmarks for:

Biggest Thursday preview screenings

Biggest opening day

Sony Pictures’ biggest film launch ever

With final figures still being compiled, the film has already established itself as the biggest cinema release of 2026 so far.

Strong competition at the box office

The Marvel blockbuster arrived just two weeks after Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, which itself enjoyed an impressive worldwide opening of $264.1 million and broke several box office records.

However, Brand New Day has comfortably eclipsed those figures and now appears firmly on course to become one of the year’s highest-grossing films.

Marvel’s next major challenge will come later this year with the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which analysts expect to become one of 2026’s biggest global releases.

Peter Parker returns

The latest chapter follows the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, where Peter Parker sacrificed his identity by having the world forget who Spider-Man really was.

Living in isolation and attempting to rebuild his life, Peter tries to reconnect with MJ and his best friend Ned before a dangerous new threat forces him back into action to protect New York City.

The film stars: Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, Mark Ruffalo, Florence Pugh and Jon Bernthal.

With a record-breaking South African debut and massive international earnings, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has firmly established itself as the must-see blockbuster of 2026, with both local and global box office records already tumbling.

Have you seen Spider-Man: Brand New Day?
