World.title: Copper  Queens dare Malawi at WAFCON  ‎ ‎
World.content:
The Copper Queens are confident ahead of Wednesday night’s decisive Group C match against Malawi at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Rabat.

‎

‎Kick off is 22h00 at Al Madina Stadium. Zambia must beat Group C leaders Malawi to advance to the quarterfinals, while Malawi will only need a draw to finish top of the group.

‎

‎Zambia opened the tournament with a 6-0 win over Egypt before a 1-0 loss to Nigeria.

‎

‎Coach Nora Häuptle said the team’s quarter-final destiny remains in their own hands and the squad is approaching the game with positivity.

‎

‎“We are in a good position, all in our hands. For me, it’s a privilege to be in this situation. To play the last game in this group and to be in the situation where it’s in our hands. We don’t need to rely on other results but what we face; that’s not pressure,” Häuptle said.

‎

‎The Swiss trainer said Zambia will focus on performance rather than qualification permutations.

‎

‎“We don’t go out and calculate tomorrow on the pitch. We go out and focus on our performance, as always. We have a clear approach to how we want to face Malawi. I think we played three very good halftimes out of the last four, and we want to build on this stable approach,” Häuptle said.

‎

‎She predicted a tough match, noting both teams are evenly matched and know each other well.

‎

‎“Tactic-wise, there are not so many secrets, I would say, in this game, but again, we bounce back to us,”_ she added.

‎

‎Goalkeeper Hazel Nali said the team is ready for the challenge.

‎

‎“We know exactly what we want and we know exactly what’s on the table. Our main focus is to work extra hard because football is played on the pitch. What we want as a team is to fight and give our all for the country.”

‎

‎Nali said the team is working on containing Malawi’s speed and is not dwelling on past results.

‎

‎The top four semi-finalists at WAFCON will qualify automatically for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

Zambia is aiming to better its 2022 bronze medal won under the late coach Bruce Mwape.

World.title: Mporokoso Praises ECZ Ballot Handling Professionalism
World.content:
Political stakeholders in Mporokoso District have commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for the professional manner in which they have handled the receipt and offloading of ballot papers ahead of the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

The stakeholders say the Commission has demonstrated transparency and professionalism by addressing concerns raised by political party representatives throughout the process.

They explained that although the ballot papers for Mporokoso Constituency arrived at 21:50 hours on August 3, 2026, the ECZ remained professional in advising that they could not be offloaded at night in line with the Commission’s guidelines, a decision that was unanimously accepted by all stakeholders.

And the United Party for National Development (UPND) representative Patrick Mulenga praised the Commission for adhering to established procedures, describing the level of professionalism exhibited by ECZ officials as commendable.

Meanwhile, National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) representative Chrispine Kachusha expressed satisfaction with the manner in which the process was conducted, stating that the Commission met the expectations of all stakeholders through a transparent and orderly exercise.

The ballot papers were successfully offloaded today, August 4, 2026, at 07:50 hours in the presence of political party representatives and other election stakeholders.

The ballot papers arrived in Mporokoso District yesterday in preparation for the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

World.title: Five Lusaka Residents Jailed Five Years for Possession of Pangolin
World.content:
The Lusaka Magistrates Court has sentenced five people to five years imprisonment each with hard labour for illegal possession of a live ground pangolin.

Handing down judgment on 28th July, 2026, Magistrate Mutinta Mwenya convicted Lutangu Namushi, 35, Melody Mwangala, 39, Abigail Sitali, 22, and Nawa Pelekelo, 33, after a full trial.

Peter Mukela, 32, had earlier changed his plea to guilty on 15th May, 2026 and was also sentenced to five years with hard labour.

According to the Department of National Parks and Wildlife (DNPW) the five were arrested on 1st February, 2026 at Novare Mall in Lusaka during an intelligence-led operation where officers found them in possession of a live ground pangolin weighing about seven kilograms.

Investigations established that the pangolin was sourced from Kalabo District in Western Province and transported to Lusaka where it was allegedly intended for sale to foreign buyers.

All five were initially charged with illegal possession of a protected species under the Zambia Wildlife Act.

DNPW has described the successful prosecution as evidence that intelligence-led operations are working to disrupt wildlife trafficking networks.

“Pangolins are protected under the Zambia Wildlife Act and are among the most heavily trafficked mammals globally due to demand for their scales and meat,” DNPW stated.

“Removing them from the wild not only threatens the survival of the species but also undermines the health of ecosystems in which they play an essential role, DNPW said.

The Department urged members of the public to help protect pangolins by refusing to buy, sell or keep them, and to report any suspicious activity to the nearest police station or DNPW office.

The conviction comes as Government and conservation partners intensify efforts to combat wildlife trafficking and safeguard Zambia’s biodiversity for tourism and ecosystem health.

World.title: President Hichilema Orders Jobs for Mufulira Volunteers
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has directed that all volunteer nurses and teachers in Mufulira District be employed.

Speaking during a community engagement meeting in Mufulira District, President Hichilema instructed the United Party for National Development (UPND) aspiring Members of Parliament candidates to compile a list of the names of volunteers for employment.

The President reiterated his commitment to continue creating more jobs for youths, highlighting that in the last four years, his government has employed 45,000 teachers,20,000 health workers and many more officers in the army, Zambia National Service,and Police.

“I Hakainde Hichilema,umubomfi wenu (your servant) have made a decision that all volunteer teachers and nurses will be employed, “the President said.

“God works through people and today He has used me to employ you,” Mr Hichilema added.

Meanwhile, the President urged Mufulira residents to vote for the UPND in order to enable them complete the various infrastructural projects being undertaken in the district.

“Vote for us so that we complete the Mufulira-Ndola Road, Mufulira-Mokambo Road, Kamuchanga Modern Market, and the Mufulira District Hospital,” Mr Hichilema said.

He stated that once re-elected, the UPND will continue with the social cash transfer programme, the cash for work Programme and the free education.

“In the Patriotic Front government children were failing to go to school due to lack of school fees, but due to our free education policy,2.5 million children have gone back to school, “he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Hichilema said he wants youths to conduct mining activities safely and legally.

Mr Hichilema said he is in the process of facilitating for youths to legally and safely mine at dump sites urging them to be patient and desist from illegal mining activities.

“No responsible parent would want their children to go and mine in where they can die, Bally is a responsible parent and I want youths to mine safely, no guns and no violence, “the President said.

President Hichilema said his government will also embark on the construction of Township Roads in Mufulira.

Meanwhile former Copperbelt Minister, Elisha Matambo highlighted some of the achievements of the New Dawn government.

Mr Matambo said the UPND government has constructed 6 level one hospitals, and also commenced construction of Mufulira District Hospital which had stalled for several years.

“Hospitals had no equipment and no drugs but under our government we bought equipment and medicines are now available,” he said.

Mr Matambo said the UPND have made several scores including resuscitating Mopani Copper Mine and Konkola Copper mine, the Free Education and building up of government reserves.

World.title: President Hichilema Salutes Dr Monze’s Exemplary Public Service
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has described late Southern Province Permanent Secretary Namani Monze as a dependable public servant who served the Zambian people with integrity, commitment and humility during his tenure in public office.

Dr Monze was laid to rest at his family farm in Bwacha Ward of Choma District, where mourners gathered to pay their final respects, with First Lady Mutinta Hichilema among those in attendance.

The President, in a speech read on his behalf by Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa, said Dr Monze distinguished himself through dedicated service across key sectors including health, education and infrastructure development.

“He was a dependable public servant who served with integrity, commitment and humility,” he said

President Hichilema further paid tribute to Dr Monze’s calm leadership style, noting that he was a civil servant who avoided controversy and instead focused on delivering results for the people.

He said such qualities were rare and worthy of emulation by those currently serving in government.

” Dr Monze understood public office and executed his duties with diligence, his death was a profound loss to the public service and the nation at large”, he said.

He also emphasized that government would remember Dr Monze not only for his professional contributions but also for his ability to work with communities and traditional leaders in fostering development at the grassroots level.

The President said his spirit of collaboration had helped strengthen service delivery in Southern Province.

The Head of State further extended his condolences to the bereaved family, urging them to take comfort in the legacy of service and respect that Dr Monze left behind.

“I encourage you to remain strong, as the nation stands with you during this difficult period of mourning”, he reiterated.

And Chief Hamusonde, speaking on behalf of other traditional leaders in Southern Province, praised Dr Monze for his responsiveness and inclusive leadership style.

“He was always prompt in responding to the needs of the people and made it easy for chiefdoms to work with government,” he said.

The Chief remarkably commended Dr Monze ‘s humility saying that his genuine interest in people knew no social status.

The chief also urged family members to continue comforting the widow and the children and warned against property grabbing.

The church, represented by Dr Vanny Munyumbwe, offered words of comfort to the bereaved family, urging them to remain strong and anchored in faith during the period of mourning.

“He was a dedicated Christian who supported the church and lived a life guided by faith and service,” she said.

And widow, late Dr Monze’s wife, Joleha Monze, described her late husband as a loving and respectful man who valued family and treated everyone with kindness.

“He was a caring man who showered me with love and respect and always put his family first,” she said.

The children remembered their father as a joyful and principled man who instilled values of integrity and humility in the family.

“My father was a cheerful man who lived with integrity and humility and always encouraged us to do what is right,” she said.

Family members, including his sister Kabanga Malekwa, described Dr Monze as a pillar of strength whose leadership extended beyond his professional life into the wider community.

“He was a pillar of strength to our family and a man who united everyone around him,” she said.

Though Dr Namani Monze has been laid to rest, mourners said his legacy of humility, dedication and service to the people of Southern Province will continue to inspire future generations.

The burial was also attended by former Southern Province Minister Credo Nanjuwa and, former Minister of Information and Media Cornelius Mweetwa.

Others who attended the burial include Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo kawana, Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe and other senior government and UPND officials.

Dr Monze 52, died on 28th July 2026, and he is survived by a wife and four children.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 5, 2026
World.content:
Tinubu Approves Up to 80% Pay Rise for Nigerian Troops

President Bola Tinubu has approved a salary increase of between 30% and 80% for about 250,000 members of Nigeria's Armed Forces, effective from 1 September. The move is expected to increase the military's annual wage bill by N264 billion, from N660 billion to N924 billion. Junior soldiers, from private to staff sergeant, will receive the highest increase of 80%, while personnel from colonel to warrant officer will get 50%, and senior officers above colonel will receive 30%. The government said the pay rise is part of broader efforts to improve troop welfare and strengthen military operations as security forces continue to combat insurgency, banditry and kidnapping across the country. Tinubu said the increase recognises the sacrifices of military personnel and reaffirmed his administration's commitment to equipping the armed forces with the resources needed to tackle Nigeria's security challenges.

Eight Years On, Zimbabwe Yet to Deliver Justice for 2018 Victims

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Eight years after Zimbabwe's security forces killed six people and injured 35 during the 1 August 2018 post-election protests, no one has been held accountable, according to Human Rights Watch. The rights group said President Emmerson Mnangagwa has failed to implement key recommendations of the Motlanthe Commission of Inquiry, despite initially pledging that those responsible would face justice. Human Rights Watch said no security personnel have been arrested or prosecuted, victims have not been compensated, and the lack of accountability has fuelled further abuses, including the deadly crackdown on January 2019 protests. The organisation urged Zimbabwean authorities to implement the commission's recommendations and end what it described as a cycle of impunity and human rights violations.

Funerals Held After Ethiopia Monastery Landslide Kills 14

Funerals have been held for some of the 14 people killed after a landslide struck the Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St Mary Monastery in Ethiopia's Amhara region during an overnight prayer service. The hillside collapsed after hours of heavy rain, burying worshippers gathered for a holy water cleansing ritual. Seven others were injured, five seriously. Rescue efforts have now ended, with 11 victims buried at the monastery and others returned to their hometowns. Landslides are a recurring hazard during Ethiopia's rainy season. Scientists have warned that climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall across East Africa.

Pesticide Poisoning Suspected in Deaths of 15 Kenya Elephants

The deaths of 15 elephants outside Kenya's Amboseli National Park have sparked concern. The Kenya Wildlife Service said preliminary findings suggest they may have been poisoned by cyanide-containing pesticides used on nearby tomato farms. Wildlife officials found traces of cyanide in samples from some elephants and said the animals showed signs consistent with poisoning. Investigations are continuing, and deliberate poisoning has not been ruled out. Conservationists and local farmers have questioned the pesticide theory. They said that elephants would have had to consume large quantities and that other wildlife sharing the same habitat was unaffected. The incident has also renewed concerns over illegal agrochemicals, weak enforcement of pesticide regulations and growing human-wildlife conflict as farming expands into elephant migration corridors.

Close 

Cameroon's Biya Makes Military Changes From Geneva

Cameroon President Paul Biya, 93, has reshuffled the country's military while remaining in Geneva, Switzerland. He has been in Geneva for nearly two months on what his office describes as a private visit. In the signed decrees, Biya appointed officials to key military posts and promoted five colonels to brigadier general, including the reappointment of Raymond Jean Charles Beko'o Abondo as head of the elite presidential guard. The move comes amid growing speculation over Biya's health and prolonged absence. Critics have warned of an institutional vacuum; however, the government insists he remains in charge and will return to Cameroon soon.

World.title: South Africa: Govt Vows to Intensify Health Corruption Fight - South African News Briefs - August 5, 2026
World.content:
South Africa Vows to Intensify Health Sector Anti-Corruption Drive

President Cyril Ramaphosa has said that the fight against corruption in South Africa's health sector is far from over, despite progress in recovering stolen public funds and prosecuting suspects, reports EWN. Speaking at the opening of the R1.6 billion King Nyabela Hospital in Mpumalanga, Ramaphosa also revealed that plans to build 11 new public hospitals are now before the National Treasury as government explores innovative ways to fund the projects. Ramaphosa said rooting out corruption will remain central to the government’s efforts to strengthen the public health system and restore public confidence in State healthcare.

Madlanga Inquiry Resumes Corruption Probe

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Madlanga Commission of Inquiry is set to resume its hearings, continuing its examination of the Investigative Directorate Against Corruption's handling of the fraud and corruption case, reports SABC News. The commission has been examining the investigation and prosecution of Crime Intelligence Head Dumisani Khumalo and six other officials from the unit. The inquiry is expected to hear from a new witness as it scrutinises the investigation, evidence assessment and legal processes that led to the arrests.

Impeachment Committee Appeals Ruling Halting Ramaphosa Inquiry

South Africa's Parliamentary Impeachment Committee has joined an application to appeal directly to the Constitutional Court against a Western Cape High Court ruling that temporarily halted its inquiry into allegations of misconduct against President Cyril Ramaphosa, reports EWN. The committee argues the judgment undermines Parliament's constitutional oversight role and accountability, saying the interdict has far-reaching implications for the separation of powers.

World.title: Mozambique: Government Concerned At New Wave of Fuel Shortage
World.content:
Maputo — The Mozambican government has expressed its concern at the new wave of fuel shortage in several parts of the country, following the crisis that affected the country last April and May.

The previous fuel shortage caused long queues of vehicles at filling stations in Maputo and other cities. According to the authorities, the crisis was influenced by the US-Israel aggression war against Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which is responsible for the daily flow of almost 20 percent of the world's oil sales.

About 80 per cent of Mozambique's fuel imports pass through routes connected to the Strait of Hormuz, which means that the impact of the war in the Middle East is potentially disastrous for the country's economy.

This situation forced the government to increase, at the beginning of this May, the prices of the main liquid fuels by up to 45, 5 percent.

The authorities also pointed out the bankruptcy of fuel distributors and the shortage of foreign currency (particularly US dollars) as the main cause of the crisis.

The wave of fuel shortage has returned. According to government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration, Inocêncio Impissa, speaking to reporters on Tuesday after a meeting of the Council of Ministers (cabinet), the government is assessing the causes of the new crisis.

"We are still assessing the situation to understand what is actually happening, so that we can solve the problem. The government is gathering information to find the causes of the problem so that something must be done", he said.

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Approves Up to 80% Salary Increase for Nigerian Soldiers
World.content:
Junior soldiers, who make up much of the military's frontline fighting force, received the largest percentage increase, suggesting the government is directing the biggest pay improvements to personnel most actively engaged in combat operations.

President Bola Tinubu has approved a salary increase of between 30 and 80 per cent for members of Nigeria's Armed Forces, a move expected to raise the federal government's annual military wage bill by N264 billion as the country continues to battle terrorism, banditry and kidnapping.

This was disclosed in a Tuesday statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga who noted that the pay review will take effect from 1 September.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The presidency said about 250,000 personnel would benefit from the salary review. While it did not explain the figure, it likely refers to active members of the Nigerian Armed Forces currently on the federal payroll across the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force.

The military's total strength is not officially disclosed, although public estimates have Nigeria's active military strength at about 230,000 personnel.

Percentage increase by rank

Under the new salary structure, officers above the rank of colonel--including brigadier generals, major generals, lieutenant generals and generals--will receive a 30 per cent salary increase.

Personnel from colonel to warrant officer will receive a 50 per cent increase, while soldiers from private to staff sergeant will receive the highest adjustment of 80 per cent.

The presidency said the revised package would increase the armed forces' annual salary bill from N660 billion to N924 billion, representing an additional N264 billion in personnel expenditure.

The increase amounts to an overall rise of 40 per cent in the military wage bill, although the actual increase for individual personnel varies by rank.

Junior soldiers, who make up much of the military's frontline fighting force, received the largest percentage increase, suggesting the government is directing the biggest pay improvements to personnel most actively engaged in combat operations.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that troops fighting across the country's frontlines have lamented about poor welfare.

While the presidency has yet to release the revised salary table, Defence Minister Christopher Musa had earlier said the minimum monthly salary for the lowest-ranked soldier was increased from N49,000 to N100,000 under the Tinubu administration. It is not immediately clear whether that increase forms part of the newly approved salary review or was implemented separately. The presidency has also not disclosed the new salary figures that will result from the latest adjustment, which takes effect on 1 September.

The announcement comes as Nigerian troops remain deployed in sustained counter-insurgency and internal security operations across the country, including the North-east, North-west and North-central, where they continue to confront Boko Haram, ISWAP, armed bandit groups and kidnappers.

The salary adjustment also forms part of the Tinubu administration's broader efforts to improve troop welfare alongside investments in military equipment, weapons procurement and technology aimed at strengthening operational effectiveness.

Announcing the decision, Mr Onanuga explained that President Tinubu said members of the armed forces deserved greater support in recognition of their sacrifices.

"The men and women who help to keep us safe in our homes must be supported and appreciated in the course of their duties to our nation," Mr Tinubu was quoted as saying.

Close 

The president said his administration would continue to prioritise troop welfare while modernising the armed forces with the weapons and technological tools required to confront security threats.

"Our administration believes that no nation can achieve greatness without security. We therefore remain resolute in mobilising all military and law enforcement assets to eliminate security threats and protect the lives and property of all Nigerians," he added.

Mr Tinubu urged military personnel to regard the salary increase as a demonstration of the government's appreciation for their service, expressing confidence that the armed forces would prevail against groups threatening the country's security.

World.title: Zimbabwe: U.S. Disputes Zimbabwean Govt's Recent Account On $365 Million Health Deal
World.content:
THE United States Embassy in Harare has disputed recent claims by Information Minister Zhemu Soda on the US$365 million health deal Zimbabwe rejected late last year.

Zhemu told Parliament that the US government sought to collect private health data for medical research which they were not sure would benefit Zimbabweans.

"As the Government, we felt we could not put the lives of our people at risk because we did not know the intention," said Soda.

According to a US Embassy spokesperson who spoke to NewZimbabwe.com this does not make sense as Zimbabwe has benefited from America's medical research through treatment and vaccines for decades.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The US government through PEPFAR has spearheaded Zimbabwe's fight against HIV/Aids by providing most of the country's ARVs and condoms.

"We reject the recent mischaracterisation of the terms of the Health Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) made by a high-level Government of Zimbabwe official, which described the MOU as a threat when, in fact, it would have provided $365 million in lifesaving assistance over five years for Zimbabwean health programs, including HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, maternal and child health, laboratories, and outbreak response," said th US Embassy spokesperson.

"The MOU required very reasonable conditions: that the Zimbabwean government co-invest, assuring sustainability of the programs; provide financial accountability and transparency to guarantee funds benefit the people and communities of Zimbabwe; and share specimens when outbreaks occur, which is a long-standing global practice to quickly develop solutions.

"Assertions that the United States was seeking personal/private data of Zimbabweans are categorically false. Any suggestion that Zimbabweans would not have benefitted from American medical research is disproven by decades of U.S. assistance, through which Zimbabweans have received US treatments and vaccines."

The same programme has been successfully presented to 34 countries with a total of US$14.3 billion in health funding.

World.title: Uganda: Opposition Politician Tortured, Faces Abusive Charges
World.content:
Nairobi — Investigate Ill-Treatment Allegations; Drop Charges

The Ugandan authorities have brought abusive criminal charges against an opposition politician, Muwanga Kivumbi, apparently based on his criticism of the president's son, who is head of the armed forces, Human Rights Watch said today.

On July 29, 2026, the authorities charged Kivumbi, a deputy president of the National Unity Platform (NUP) Uganda's main opposition party, with "inciting violence" and "managing an unlawful society," after unlawfully detaining him for 19 days in an unrevealed location the day after he was released on bail for separate politically related charges. Kivumbi is one of several government critics that the military has in recent weeks arbitrarily seized, held incommunicado, and handed over to courts for abusive prosecutions.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Ugandan authorities are weaponizing the justice system to harass and target its critics and opposition," said Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. "The government needs to end these malicious prosecutions, and instead ensure accountability for the numerous rights abuses and scaling up of human rights violations in the country."

On July 10, armed plainclothes and uniformed soldiers dragged him from his car at a police roadblock and drove off with him to an unrevealed location. On the morning of July 19, the soldiers left him at a police station in Kampala, media reported.

The police took him 66 kilometers away to a magistrate's court in Butambala later that day, where they brought new charges against him. Based on the charge sheet, Kivumbi's charges arise from a speech he made to his supporters at a public gathering in Butambala on the day of his initial release.

The authorities did not specify the basis for the charges in the charge sheet. But in a video of this speech, seen by Human Rights Watch, Kivumbi criticized President Museveni's son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the chief of the Uganda Peoples' Defence Force, for engaging in politics as a military officer.

During the July 29 court hearing, Kivumbi said that the security officers who abducted him blindfolded him and took him to a location he could not identify, where they held him for days in a small room, and kicked and beat him until he bled from his head. A witness who saw Kivumbi upon his release told Human Rights Watch that he had scars on his head, arms, legs, and back, apparently from the beatings.

The authorities had initially arrested Kivumbi on January 22, alongside scores of other National Unity Platform supporters around Uganda's contested general elections on January 15, holding him until he was released on bail in July. Kivumbi had been running for a parliamentary seat during the elections which he lost.

The authorities who arrested Kivumbi in January accused him of orchestrating "a violent attack on Kibibi Police Station and Butambala Electoral Commission Tally Centre," and causing "serious damage to sections of the Butambala-Gomba road" and multiple vehicles that "directly resulted into the deaths of seven people" on the days before and after election day. Kivumbi had rejected the allegation, saying security forces had raided his home on election day and shot and killed several members of his campaign team who were there.

The Agora Centre for Research, a Ugandan organization, reported that the armed forces killed at least seven people at Kivumbi's home, including election officials, who had run into a garage for safety during the raid.

The Ugandan authorities should urgently and impartially investigate the circumstances of those killings and hold the those responsible to account, Human Rights Watch said.

Although Uganda's Constitution guarantees the right to bail and prohibits arbitrary arrests and detention, security agencies frequently re-arrest people after courts have granted them bail, and courts have denied bail to other political opponents, extending their pretrial detention beyond maximum periods under Ugandan and international law.

In another such case, on July 29, a former presidential candidate, Kizza Besigye, who is on trial for treason and has been imprisoned since November 2024, collapsed during a court hearing and was hospitalized. The courts have previously denied him bail, despite requests by his family to have him released to allow him to receive private medical treatment.

On July 15, soldiers seized and unlawfully detained one of Besigye's lawyers, Elias Lukwago, then sent him to pretrial detention on treason-related charges. The authorities later deported another of Besigye's lawyers, Martha Karua, to Kenya on July 22. On July 30, the High Court denied Lukwago bail, which he had sought to receive medical treatment.

Close 

International human rights law requires any pretrial restrictions on criminal suspects to be consistent with the right to liberty, the presumption of innocence, and the right to equality under the law. The UN Human Rights Committee, the international body that provides authoritative analysis of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, has stated that pretrial detention imposed on suspects as punishment, among other reasons, is inconsistent with those rights.

Ugandan law criminalizes torture under the Prevention and Prohibition of Torture Act 2012, and the Human Rights (Enforcement) Act 2019 provides for personal liability for public officers who commit human rights violations.

"Kivumbi's charges are only the latest in Uganda's intensifying clampdown on critics of the government," Budoo-Scholtz said. "The authorities should drop all criminal charges against him and ensure that all security officials implicated in his ill-treatment and enforced disappearance are held to account."

World.title: Mali: Journalist in Mali Sentenced to a Year in Prison
World.content:
Quash Charges and Release Chahana Takiou

A prominent Malian journalist was convicted under Mali's cybercrime legislation for criticizing the use of that same law to silence another journalist. The verdict marks the latest escalation in the military junta's widening assault on freedom of expression in the country.

On August 3, the national cybercrime court in Bamako, Mali's capital, sentenced Chahana Takiou, editor of the biweekly 22 Septembre, to one year in prison.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Security forces arrested Takiou on June 8 after he publicly criticized the authorities for prosecuting a fellow journalist, Youssouf Sissoko, under the cybercrime law rather than Mali's press laws. Sissoko was sentenced to two years in prison in June after he published an article critical of the military ruler of neighboring Niger.

Prosecutors charged Takiou with "undermining the credibility of the state through the judicial institution" and placed him in pretrial detention. Takiou's lawyers, citing his diabetes and cardiovascular disease, requested provisional release on medical grounds, but the prosecutor rejected the request.

The day after Takiou's arrest, the authorities arrested another journalist, Abdramane Keïta, director of the newspaper Le Témoin (The Witness), after he said on a television program that the Al-Qaeda-linked armed group Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wa al-Muslimeen (Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims, JNIM) controlled the northern city of Kidal. JNIM and allied Tuareg fighters recaptured Kidal in April following a three-year presence of Malian forces and Russian mercenaries. The authorities charged Keïta with "offense of a regionalist nature undermining national unity and the credibility of the state" and detained him pending a trial on August 17.

Takiou's prosecution fits a broader pattern in Mali of using fabricated or politically motivated criminal charges to silence journalists, activists, opposition figures, and human rights defenders. Since seizing power in 2020, Mali's military junta has steadily dismantled civic space. The authorities have banned media outlets, dissolved civil society organizations, abolished multiparty politics, and targeted dissidents through arbitrary arrests and enforced disappearances.

No one should face prison for peacefully expressing an opinion. Mali's authorities should immediately release Takiou and Keïta, quash Takiou's conviction, and drop all charges stemming solely from the peaceful exercise of freedom of expression. They should also do what Takiou suggested: end the misuse of cybercrime legislation to silence independent voices.

Close 

Ilaria Allegrozzi, Senior Sahel Researcher

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: New Ebola Vaccine Trial Launches As Outbreak Spreads in DR Congo
World.content:
Results may be months away, but efforts are advancing towards enhanced treatment and the world's first vaccine for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday as deaths and cases rise in the largest ever outbreak on record in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Key points

3,748 cases, including 1,657 deaths and 708 recoveries, as of 1 August, according to WHO

While Ebola vaccines exist, trials for the first ever Bundibugyo species-specific candidate vaccine began in the UK on 24 July, with a second starting in Canada this week

Clinical trials of medicine and treatment options are rolling out in Ituri province, the restive epicentre of the current outbreak

A new 100-bed treatment centre was inaugurated in Bunia, capital of Ituri

Searching for solutions

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Compared to previous Ebola outbreaks, trials started more quickly this time as protocols had been written before the current one was declared in DRC in mid-May, said Vasee Moorthy, acting lead of WHO's R&D Blueprint, a global platform for research and development collaboration to respond to epidemics and pandemics.

Despite ongoing efforts, there are still no proven safe and efficacious treatment, preventive or vaccination options for the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus, Dr. Moorthy told reporters in Geneva.

However, it would likely still be several months before more definite conclusions could be drawn from the ongoing trials, he said.

Vaccine trials

A vaccine trial in the United Kingdom entered phase one on 24 July, with another to begin in Canada in coming days, Dr. Moorthy said.

Both trials are being conducted on ferrets and monkeys, after which results would be analysed by WHO before deciding on whether to move to the subsequent phase.

New data has also emerged in animal studies on the licensed vaccine Ervebo, targeting a different Ebola strain, according to WHO.

The UN health agency's technical advisory group convened last Friday and is expected to publish recommendations later this week.

New clinical trials

A clinical trial of a potential post-exposure prophylaxis - or preventative - medicine is underway in Ituri province.

Led by the DRC's National Institute for Biomedical Research with an international consortium of research and outbreak-response partners, the trial has enrolled over 25 patients to evaluate whether an oral medicine given for 10 days to confirmed high risk contacts could prevent onset of disease.

Close 

Since the outbreak was declared, three testing sites have opened in Ituri province and a fourth is set to open later this week where patients can enrol in trials and be monitored in safe conditions to see if the medicines are effective, Dr. Moorthy said.

"We are trying to ramp up the enrolment," he said. "Because they're a clinical trial, we have to have safe, monitoring of the people that are enrolled in the trial. And that does take time to have more and more teams and more sites enrolling."

The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, is supporting screening, infection prevention, risk communication and provision of essential hygiene items

At the DRC-Uganda border, a mobile lab supported by WHO and the World Food Programme (WFP) delivers Ebola test results in around one hour , cutting delays and bringing lifesaving diagnostics closer to more than 94,000 people

, cutting delays and bringing lifesaving diagnostics closer to more than 94,000 people The UN Children's Fund (UNICEF) operates nurseries for youngsters of Ebola-affected families

for youngsters of Ebola-affected families The MONUSCO peacekeeping mission in DRC protects civilians, conducts information campaigns for local communities and has increased presence around medical facilities to support WHO teams and partners

World.title: Trump warns Iran will be hit 'really hard' if nuclear negotiations collapse again
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

President Donald Trump renewed his warning to Iran on Tuesday, saying the U.S. could strike the country "really hard" if negotiations between Washington and Tehran collapse again.

"If they back out again, they're going to get hit really hard," Trump told Fox News' Trace Gallagher. "They know that. They understand that. I have no choice. They can't have a nuclear weapon. It's very simple."

Trump said military action remained an option if diplomacy fails.

TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

"The hard hit is yet to come, and hopefully we won't have to use it," he said during the interview.

Trump’s comments came days after he held off on a planned military strike on Iran that he said would have been the largest since World War II after Tehran and several Middle Eastern countries requested more time to negotiate over reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing Iran’s nuclear program.

"We were going to a tremendous attack, the biggest since World War II, and they called me and said very politely, 'Please, can we talk? Can we talk?' And I said, 'Yes, we can talk. Let's get it done,'" Trump said.

Earlier this week, Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and curb Iran's nuclear program was "imminent."

TRUMP SAYS IRAN DEAL ‘LARGELY NEGOTIATED’ AS 84-DAY WAR NEARS POSSIBLE END

Iranian officials have denied holding direct talks with the United States, saying negotiations are taking place through mediators in Oman. The Associated Press reported Tuesday that Iranian and Omani officials had made significant progress toward a potential agreement to reopen the strait, though negotiations remained ongoing.

US OFFICIAL SAYS JD VANCE MADE 'GREAT PROGRESS' IN IRAN TALKS, CALLS SNUB REPORTS 'FOREIGN PROPAGANDA'

Trump described Tuesday’s negotiations as "very good," despite Iran’s repeated public denials that direct talks were underway.

"They don't like to admit that, but, well, you know, it's a little bit disconcerting," he said.

"It's just such a lie," Trump added.

"But it doesn't matter. That's talk. The only thing that matters is action. And they want to make a deal. We'll see what happens. If they don't make a deal, it's going to be too bad."

When asked at what point the U.S. might abandon talks with Iran after negotiations repeatedly collapsed, Trump said he was not in a rush to walk away from diplomacy.

"I have plenty of time," he said.

Trump argued that previous administrations failed to resolve the issue and again criticized the nuclear agreement negotiated under former President Barack Obama.

TRUMP RECALLS NETANYAHU'S FAILED PUSH TO KILL OBAMA IRAN DEAL, SAYS HE FINISHED THE JOB

"It should have been done by many presidents over many years, and it wasn't, and I'm doing it," Trump said. "Obama was taken to the cleaners."

Trump has previously called the latest round of negotiations Iran’s "last chance" to avoid an escalation of US military action. He has said negotiators will initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz before addressing Tehran’s nuclear program.

Fox News Digital's Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

Brazilian lawmakers preparing to conduct official business found themselves sharing the halls of a state legislature with several uninvited — but unusually relaxed — guests.

Video recorded by legislative staffer Nayara Bueno showed the animals moving calmly through the entrance while workers sought to steer them outside.

BLACK BEAR CAUGHT ON VIDEO WANDERING INTO CALIFORNIA WATER DISTRICT OFFICE AFTER PUSHING OPEN FRONT DOOR

"They show up here quite often, so we’ve gotten used to seeing them," Bueno told The Associated Press.

The rodents' guest appearance did not cause any damage to the Mato Grosso state legislature, according to officials.

The legislature borders a park that is home to wildlife, giving the animals easy access to the surrounding government complex.

Native to South America, capybaras are semiaquatic mammals commonly found around wetlands and other bodies of water. They are highly social, generally travel in groups and can reach weights of about 175 pounds.

World.title: Socialist tenant organizer who blasted 'sell-out Democrats' loses Midwest primary
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Jordan Herrera, an attorney, Air Force veteran and former Missouri assistant attorney general, won the Democratic nomination Tuesday in Missouri’s newly redrawn 4th Congressional District, defeating better-funded democratic socialist Hartzell Gray in a seven-way primary.

Herrera prevailed over Gray, the 33-year-old former Kansas City radio host and tenant organizer who drew national attention after appearing on Hasan Piker’s Twitch livestream and blasting "sell-out Democrats."

The result puts a more conventional Democrat on the November ballot against Republican Rep. Mark Alford in the GOP-leaning district, rather than Gray, who had framed his campaign as a left-wing challenge to the party establishment.

RNC AND NRCC FILE LAWSUIT DEFENDING MISSOURI'S NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAP AGAINST DEMOCRATIC CHALLENGES

The new 4th District takes in part of Kansas City before extending south through a broad swath of suburban and rural Missouri. While the map made Alford’s district less Republican than it had been, it remains a solidly GOP seat.

Gray emerged as the clear financial leader in the Democratic field. FEC records showed his campaign had raised about $250,000 through mid-July — more than six times the roughly $40,000 raised by Herrera and far more than Cass, the 2024 Democratic nominee who again sought the seat.

The Kansas City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America said its backing of Gray marked its first endorsement in a federal race. The group praised Gray’s refusal to take money from corporations, developers and lobbying groups, while pointing to his support for universal health care, tenant protections and more progressive taxation.

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

Gray, who has also called for rent controls, Medicare for All and ending the Supreme Court’s Citizens United decision, has framed his campaign as a rebuke of a Democratic Party he argues has become too closely tied to wealthy donors and corporate interests. The 2010 ruling allowed corporations and unions to spend unlimited sums independently to influence elections.

His appearance on Piker’s show helped turn an otherwise low-profile Missouri primary into a small test case for the party’s socialist left, which has increasingly relied on social media personalities, small-dollar donors and activist networks to build support outside traditional party structures.

HASAN PIKER MAKES AOC HIS 2028 PICK FOR PRESIDENT, SAYS IT'S 'NOT EVEN A QUESTION’

Gray’s campaign said viewers gave more than $30,000 after the Piker appearance. He later appeared on The Majority Report , another left-leaning online program, as his campaign sought to translate national attention into turnout in Kansas City.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The primary also included former Democratic nominee Jeanette Cass, attorney and Air Force veteran Herrera, radio host Randy Miller, Ashleigh Rogers, Wayne Russell and G. Rick.

Gray’s nomination is a win for a local Democratic Socialists of America chapter that had not previously backed a federal candidate. But the general election will test whether the kind of coalition that powered him through a fractured Democratic primary can compete in a district intentionally drawn to favor Republicans.

World.title: Dems rally behind Michigan prosecutor to champion party in crucial House race

Christina Hines, a prosecutor and Democratic candidate for Congress in Michigan's 10th Congressional District, secured her party's nomination in a primary election on Tuesday evening.

Democrats will count on Hines' messaging on affordability and her story as as a special victims prosecutor to flip the district and chip away the GOP’s slim majority in the U.S. House of Representatives.

"My work was a different kind of chaos. Protecting families from predators isn't just a job for me. It's a mission. Now families like ours are getting screwed by a system that only works for the rich," Hines said in a campaign video.

SOCIALIST-BACKED MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL CALLS AMERICAN POLITICS A 'DISEASE' AFTER PROFESSING LOVE FOR US

In recent years, the district has leaned Republican but remains largely competitive.

Incumbent Rep. John James, R-Mich., last won re-election in 2024 in a 51.1% to 45.0% victory over Democratic challenger Carl Marlinga, a judge and former prosecutor.

The cycle before that, James beat out Marlinga by a narrow 48.8% to 48.3% win in 2022.

But now, James, who enjoyed the benefit of incumbency, announced he would vacate the seat and instead pursue a gubernatorial bid, calling it a way to secure Michigan’s prosperity to future generations.

"My family, like countless others, came to our great state for the better opportunities our manufacturing and automotive industries offered and to live the American dream," James said in a statement.

TWIN COURT RULINGS RESHAPE HOUSE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS FIGHT UPHILL REDISTRICTING BATTLE

With an open seat in play, Hines has pitched her candidacy as a way to protect the country from what she characterized as an overzealous administration and institutional corruption.

In her career as a prosecutor, Hines described her work as helping victims of sexual abuse and human trafficking, according to her website. She has also prosecuted cases involving homicide, torture and hate crimes.

On her website, Hines listed priorities like reducing the cost of living by pushing back against what she identified as "price gouging" and increasing the minimum wage, investing in technical educations and protecting federal programs against cuts from the Trump administration like Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy strikes evidence deal as fingerprint gap opens trial debate, expert says

Lindsay Clancy spoke directly in court Tuesday, repeatedly answering, "Yes, Your Honor," as she agreed to let prosecutors treat certain forensic facts as established hours before a state police trooper testified that investigators recovered no usable fingerprints from a knife or three exercise bands.

The developments narrowed the Massachusetts mother’s murder trial toward its central dispute: whether Clancy was criminally responsible when her three children were killed inside the family’s Duxbury home.

Before jurors entered the courtroom, Judge William Sullivan questioned Clancy about a stipulation covering certain evidence.

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

"You understand that by signing the stipulation, you’re agreeing that the Commonwealth does not have to prove these certain facts that are contained in the stipulation," Sullivan said. "Do you understand that?"

"Yes, Your Honor," Clancy replied.

Asked whether anyone had forced or threatened her to accept the agreement, Clancy said, "No, Your Honor."

Sullivan found that Clancy was competent and had entered the stipulation "knowingly, intelligently, voluntarily and willingly."

LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS PILL USE AS EXPERT SAYS EVIDENCE COULD SHAPE MURDER TRIAL

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington said the agreement would prevent prosecutors from calling dozens of witnesses solely to establish the chain of custody for blood, bodily fluids, exercise bands and DNA evidence.

The stipulation is not a guilty plea or an admission that Clancy was criminally responsible for the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

"The legal strategy behind the move by the defense is to steer the jury’s focus away from the horrific nature of the acts and to that central issue of criminal intent, or what we would call mens rea," McLean told Fox News Digital.

McLean said Clancy’s measured responses Tuesday should not be taken as evidence of her mental condition on Jan. 24, 2023.

"She sounded rational. She understands what she’s doing," McLean said. "But remember, the Commonwealth’s burden of proof is to prove that she was sane beyond a reasonable doubt at the time the crimes were committed -- not today, not two weeks ago."

World.title: Tarik Skubal's Dodgers debut ends in decisive 5-1 loss to Cubs as LA drops fifth straight game
World.content:
The Los Angeles Dodgers ruined baseball this past weekend when they attempted to make their team better, an unforgivable crime in the world of modern online baseball fandom.

With Shohei Ohtani nursing a nagging knee injury, injuries to Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, and inconsistent performance from some of the team's other starting pitching options, the Dodgers used some of their impressive outfield prospect depth to acquire reigning American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers.

This set off a firestorm of criticism from fans online, who announced they were quitting the sport, that the season should be canceled, that owners should lock players out indefinitely until players agree to allow billionaire owners to keep 99.9% of revenue, or that the outcome of the 2035 World Series was already determined or something.

SENDING ACE PITCHER TARIK SKUBAL TO THE LOS ANGELES DODGERS WOULD OFFICIALLY RUIN BASEBALL

Well, Skubal made his Dodgers debut Tuesday night in Chicago, facing the Cubs at Wrigley Field. The Dodgers lost their fifth straight game, 5-1, falling to 3-7 in their last 10 games. Baseball is ruined.

Skubal, for his part, pitched well, allowing two runs on four hits over six innings while striking out six and walking two. His first run allowed came on a Dansby Swanson home run in the third inning, with the second coming on an unlucky break.

After striking out Pete Crow-Armstrong to start the sixth, he walked Seiya Suzuki, before Alex Bregman hit a ball to right field that Kyle Tucker wasn't able to make the play on. The Dodgers got Suzuki at home on a Michael Busch grounder, before Nico Hoerner hit a swinging bunt that bounced too high for anyone to make a play on, bringing in Bregman.

The Dodgers offense never got much going against Cubs starter Javier Assad, outside of a Kyle Tucker home run, then did even less against their bullpen. On the rare inning with a baserunner, a Dodger hitter would work tirelessly to hit into an immediate double play.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The LA bullpen, however, was extremely accommodating. Chicago added two runs in the seventh inning when Pete Crow-Armstrong threw his bat at the ball to drive in Swanson, then Seiya Suzuki blooped another single in to bring in the fourth run of the game. Nico Hoerner homered off Edwin Diaz in the ninth to cement the win.

With baseball ruined, the Dodgers will look to avoid their second consecutive series loss via the sweep on Wednesday, sending superstar starter Eric Lauer to the mound against Shota Imanaga.

This game, and this series, is a microcosm of the absurdities of online baseball discussion. Skubal, arguably one of the best two pitchers in baseball, was outpitched by Javier Assad, a 29-year-old with such mediocre stuff that he's struck out just 51 hitters in 75.1 innings this year. The Cubs are so terrified of starting Assad in a postseason game that they traded for two starting pitchers at the deadline in hopes of avoiding it. Dansby Swanson entered the series on an 0-21 streak, only to go 5-8 with a home run in the first two games.

Meanwhile, Pete Crow-Armstrong's reality defying streak continues, with a .415 batting average on balls put in play since the start of June, an impossible number when league average is around .300. But therein lies the problem with ruining baseball and predicting the World Series in August. You just don't know who will be hot, cold, or underperforming when October rolls around.

A baseball season of 162 games gets compressed into a best-of-five or best-of-seven, the definition of a small sample size, that does quite literally nothing to determine the better team. Good teams often slump. Bad teams sweep good teams.

Since the start of June, the Dodgers have the seventh highest winning percentage in baseball, worse than the Cubs, Red Sox, Astros, Brewers, Tigers, and the... Miami Marlins. That's not in a postseason series, that's over a two month sample. You can't ruin baseball because the gaps between teams are so small. Even now.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Edwin Diaz has now allowed nine runs in 8.2 innings, with a whopping 20 baserunners. Kyle Tucker's been a league average hitter. Mookie Betts, for all his prior accolades, is hitting .223 with a .280 on base percentage and .390 slugging percentage. His OPS has dropped nearly 200 points from 2024. LA's bullpen since the start of July has an ERA of around 5, and the 27th best FIP in MLB. Ruining baseball indeed.

The far-left insurgency within the Democratic Party scored another victory on Tuesday night, with a co-founder of the progressive Sunrise Movement trouncing two establishment-backed Democrats in a contentious Michigan primary.

William Lawrence defeated former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink and former Navy SEAL Matt Maasdam to win the Democratic nomination for Michigan's 7th Congressional District, anchored in Lansing.

Lawrence will now go on to face Rep. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., a military veteran who is seeking a second term in Congress this November.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN, WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

Barrett ran unopposed in the Republican primary after winning the seat in an open race in 2024. It was previously held by Democrat Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who vacated it when she successfully ran for Senate that year.

Lawrence's victory is a commanding win in the wider civil war for the soul of the Democratic Party, with battles being waged across the country.

Mike Marinella, spokesman for House Republicans’ campaign arm the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), told Fox News Digital after Lawrence’s victory, "The Democrats' path to the House majority is evaporating in real time. Every embarrassing defeat leaves them with a radical socialist nominee, an emptier bank account, and another must-win seat off the board."

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

The establishment left's main opponent has been the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which has not endorsed a candidate in this race.

But Lawrence does have backing from Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., his fellow Michigan Democrat and a prominent DSA member who's stirred controversy for her comments about Israel.

He was also endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., a self-described democratic socialist.

The Sunrise Movement, which Lawrence co-founded in 2017, began as a youth-focused climate activist group that pushed the Green New Deal alongside progressives in Congress.

HOUSE PROGRESSIVES REVIVE GREEN NEW DEAL FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS AS DEM CIVIL WAR EMPOWERS FAR LEFT

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Since then, its non-climate policy platform has included calls to get Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) out of U.S. cities and abolishing police, according to its website.

Lawrence's victory is likely the best outcome for Republicans, who are fighting a nationwide uphill battle to keep control of the House of Representatives.

World.title: Progressive activist wins Democratic primary in one of the country’s biggest House races
World.content:
Democrat William Lawrence, a co-founder of the progressive Sunrise Movement, has won his party’s primary in Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, NBC News projects — a big victory for the insurgent left that also sets up a dramatic general election contrast with Republicans in a crucial battleground seat.

Voters in five states participated in primaries Tuesday, including several with major battleground districts up for grabs in November. And few are more hotly contested than this Michigan district, where Lawrence bested two prominent Democratic rivals with national security backgrounds after having differentiated himself as the more liberal candidate and as an aggressive critic of data centers.

Meanwhile, the battle between his two Democratic opponents, former Ambassador Bridget Brink and retired Navy SEAL Matt Maasdam, became increasingly bitter as the race drew to a close, and the two candidates ultimately appear to have split the more moderate wing of the party.

Lawrence will take on GOP Rep. Tom Barrett in one of the most tightly divided swing seats in the country. President Donald Trump carried the district by just 1 percentage point in 2024, and super PACs and other outside groups have reserved more ad spending there than in all but one other House race in the country.

Lawrence won support from an array of prominent progressives and outside groups, and a mysterious super PAC spent more than $1 million in the race’s final weeks to boost him and tear Maasdam down. The spending raised concerns among some Democrats that Republicans might be boosting Lawrence because they think he’ll be easier to beat in the general election.

Michigan voters are also cementing other key battleground House races Tuesday, albeit with less fanfare.

In Michigan’s 4th District, Republican Rep. Bill Huizenga will face off against Democratic state Sen. Sean McCann in the Kalamazoo-area district. Huizenga had Trump’s backing, while McCann was endorsed by top Democrats in the state like Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson.

Republicans are still waiting to find out who will be their nominee against Democratic Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet. And in the 10th District in suburban Detroit, which is being left open by GOP Rep. John James and his run for governor, Trump-endorsed military veteran Mike Bouchard will run against Democrat Christina Hines, a former special victims prosecutor.

In Virginia, the matchups are set in four districts expected to fit into the battleground puzzle in different ways this fall.

In the Norfolk area, Republican Rep. Jen Kiggans and Democratic former Rep. Elaine Luria head to a rematch of the 2022 2nd District election, which Kiggans won. In the Richmond-area 1st District, Republican Rep. Rob Wittman will face Henrico County Commonwealth’s Attorney Shannon Taylor in a district that could be competitive this fall — one that Trump won by 5 points in 2024.

Farther out on the battlefield, Democratic Rep. Eugene Vindman will face off against Republican Doug Ollivant, a retired Army lieutenant colonel, in the Fredericksburg-area 7th District, a race in which Vindman will start with a significant resource advantage. And Republican Rep. John McGuire will run against Democratic former Rep. Tom Perriello in a district Trump won by 12 points in 2024.

Missouri is home to one of Republicans’ best opportunities to gain a seat this fall after the GOP-controlled state Legislature redrew the congressional map to put Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver into a seat Trump won by 18 points in 2024.

Republican Rick Brattin, a state senator backed by Gov. Mike Kehoe and the Club for Growth, is projected to win the nomination there, with Trump having weighed in for him in the race’s final days.

In Washington state, Republicans are targeting Democratic Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez in a district Trump won by 3 points in 2024. She will face state Senate Republican leader John Braun, who has Trump’s endorsement, this fall.

Meanwhile, two Democratic incumbents faced serious primary challenges Tuesday. One, Rep. Wesley Bell of Missouri, is projected to win his primary, a rematch against former Rep. Cori Bush, whom he defeated in 2024. The other, Rep. Shri Thanedar of Michigan, is narrowly leading state Rep. Donavan McKinney in a race that has not yet been called.

Voters in a handful of safe seats are also picking nominees who are all but certain to win this fall.

In Michigan’s Oakland County, state Senate Democratic leader Jeremy Moss cruised to victory in Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens’ district, with Stevens running for the Senate.

In Missouri, Salem Radio Network host Chris Stigall won the Republican primary in the seat from which GOP Rep. Sam Graves is retiring.

And in Washington’s 4th District, Trump-backed Yakima County Commission member Amanda McKinney will move on to face retired Air Force Maj. John Duresky, a Democrat, in a red seat Trump won by about 20 points in 2024.

GOP Rep. Dan Newhouse, one of the last remaining House Republicans who voted to impeach Trump in 2021, is retiring.

World.title: Rep. Wesley Bell defeats former Rep. Cori Bush in a Missouri Democratic primary rematch
World.content:
ST. LOUIS — Rep. Wesley Bell defeated former Rep. Cori Bush in a Democratic primary rematch, NBC News projects, in the latest chapter of a long-term fight over a deep-blue St. Louis-based district.

Bell overwhelmed Bush on the airwaves, fending off her push to make the race a referendum on his support for U.S. aid to Israel.

In total, Bell’s campaign and outside allies outspent Bush by a staggering 27-to-1 ratio, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking service. United Democracy Project — the super PAC linked to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the pro-Israel advocacy group known as AIPAC — spent $2 million to support Bell, largely through negative ads attacking Bush. One such ad slammed Bush for being critical of former Vice President Kamala Harris.

It was a reference to Bush’s criticizing the Biden-Harris administration for supporting Israel amid what she deemed a genocide in Gaza. She endorsed Harris in the 2024 election.

As Bell cast his vote Tuesday, he criticized Bush for focusing on Israel and talking “over and over ... about an issue that is not impacting folks right here in St. Louis.”

“And while we take those issues seriously, you know, the M in Missouri doesn’t stand for Middle East,” Bell told NBC News. “It stands for Missouri.”

At a campaign stop later Tuesday, Bush hit back at Bell’s claims and said Missourians “are not happy” that he filled his “campaign coffers” with money from outside groups.

“Why are they meddling in our primaries?” she asked. “Why does he allow that?”

AIPAC loomed large in the race after it helped Bell oust Bush two years ago. United Democracy Project poured $9.3 million into ads in that primary, according to AdImpact, accounting for nearly half of the spending in the race.

Sidney Clark, a Democratic candidate for state representative currently serving in local government, said he supported Bell in 2024 but was voting for Bush this cycle because Bell, in his view, has “been paid for.”

“There are people out there who are using their money and financial influence to buy candidates, and I think that’s the wrong direction for our country,” Clark said after having voted at a St. Louis polling place.

Airest Wilson, another Democratic voter, told NBC News that candidates who take corporate money cross a red line for him — even if they are otherwise aligned with his political views.

“They don’t get that money for free,” he said. “You got to represent their interests. You can’t represent the constituents freely.”

“Cori, it took a lot of courage, but she rejected dark money. So that’s why I support Cori,” Wilson added.

This year, Bush ran two TV ads in the primary, each touching on multiple issues. But both linked Bell to AIPAC and cast him as more interested in sending money to Israel than Missourians, including those suffering from the aftermath of last year’s tornado.

Bell presented himself as a fighter against President Donald Trump, saying of Bush in one of his ads: “She fights Kamala Harris, Joe Biden and other Democrats.”

Bush said Tuesday that if she were to lose, it would not be a setback for the progressive movement.

“If there is a loss, then that just means that there is more work for us to do,” she said.

Asked whether she could see herself voting for Bell if he wins the primary, Bush told NBC News: “See myself voting for a Republican? Oh, I don’t think that’s on the ballot for me.”

World.title: GOP’s Ty Masterson and Democrat Cindy Holscher to meet in Kansas governor’s race
World.content:
Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson will face Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher in Kansas’ election for governor this fall, NBC News projects, setting up a contest that represents the GOP’s best gubernatorial pickup opportunity this year.

Both candidates won their respective primaries on Tuesday. Masterson rode an endorsement from President Donald Trump to emerge from a crowded GOP field, while Holscher focused on a progressive, anti-establishment message to defeat a fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was backed by term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly.

Holscher pitched herself in ads as someone who “gets that working people are tired of being sold out by both parties.” She also made her support for a proposed moratorium on new data center construction a big part of her message.

Corson massively outspent Holscher in the primary, and leaned heavily on his support from Kelly, who won two terms in a state Trump won by double digits in the past three presidential contests.

One of his recent TV ads featured Kelly praising him as someone who can “stand up to Trump and ICE” and has the “strength and judgement and backbone” for the state’s top job. Another ad, run by a pro-Corson PAC called Heartland Priorities, showed Kelly lauding Corson for having a “record of standing up for Kansas values” and for “stepping up and fighting back” against Trump.

Kelly, who has maintained strong job approval ratings, told the Kansas City Star in a recent interview that Corson was the only Democrat in the race capable of winning the support of the state’s “extraordinarily moderate” Republican and independent voters in November. She said that, “if he’s not elected, I’m very concerned about the direction Kansas will go in,” while also suggesting that Holscher was an “extremist.”

Meanwhile, on the GOP side, Masterson and his allies were outspent on the airwaves by his opponents, but his support from the president put him over the top.

In a tele-rally last week, Trump lauded Masterson as a “fighter,” a “winner” and as someone who has “done a fantastic job — throughout life, actually.”

“We love each other, we love that state,” Trump said.

In Kansas, registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats nearly 2 to 1. The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter has rated the general election contest as “lean Republican.”

World.title: Missouri voters block GOP-led effort to raise bar to pass constitutional amendments
World.content:
Missouri voters blocked a Republican-led effort to raise the bar for passing citizen-led constitutional amendments, NBC News projects.

Under current state law, such ballot measures require a simple statewide majority for passage, a process that has been used in recent years to grant abortion rights, expand Medicaid and legalize marijuana.

But Amendment 4 would have required citizen-led ballot initiatives to win a majority in each of Missouri’s congressional districts, boundaries that are drawn by state lawmakers. Other ballot measures, like those referred from the Legislature, would not have been subject to this higher bar.

It would have created “the strictest passage threshold in the country for citizen-initiated ballot measures only,” according to Hannah Ledford, the deputy director of the Fairness Project, a group that supports citizen initiative processes. She added it could have left Missouri’s direct democracy process “functionally dead.”

Missouri is one of 26 states that allows voters to legislate directly by petitioning to place a constitutional amendment on the ballot.

The amendment was first proposed by Republican state Rep. Ed Lewis, after Missouri voters used the method to advance a spate of progressive priorities in a state where the GOP has full control of government. Many recent amendments would have failed under the stricter standard proposed by Amendment 4.

“This amendment is really an amendment to protect our Constitution,” Lewis said on a radio program earlier this month. “We have the absolute lowest and weakest process and that’s why we’ve had six initiative petitions passed in the last eight years that have really done real harm to our state and to our Constitution.”

The state’s Republican-controlled Legislature has repealed or limited some changes made through ballot initiatives, including repealing paid sick leave.

Opponents of the proposal heavily outspent its supporters, pouring more than $6 million into broadcast ads, according to data from the tracking firm AdImpact. The measure’s backers did not air any broadcast ads, AdImpact’s data shows.

The more-moneyed campaign against Amendment 5, a proposal to end income taxes and expand sales taxes, also included arguments against Amendment 4 in their ads.

The effort to change the constitutional amendment process also came after Republican lawmakers redrew the state’s congressional map last year to carve up the lone Democratic-held district. Earlier Tuesday, Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins said that a referendum that sought to undo the new map would not appear on the state’s ballot, arguing the effort was unconstitutional.

Missouri isn’t the only state where Republicans have sought to make it more difficult for citizen-led constitutional amendments to pass. In November, North Dakota and South Dakota voters will decide whether to bump the threshold up from a statewide majority to 60%. And in Utah, there will be a similar measure on the fall ballot specifically related to tax increases.

World.title: Senate Republicans advance Todd Blanche nomination after ‘anti-weaponization’ fund holdup
World.content:
Republicans on the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday advanced Todd Blanche’s attorney general nomination after it had been delayed over concerns from two GOP members on the panel.

Blanche’s path to confirmation had been on hold after Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — both of whom are leaving Congress in January — raised concerns about the “anti-weaponization” fund that the Trump administration tried to establish in May to give taxpayer-funded payments to Trump allies, potentially including Jan. 6 rioters the president pardoned on his first day back in office.

Blanche said Sunday that he had reached a deal to amend the settlement that Cornyn and Tillis later said satisfied their concerns. Trump had recently defended the fund and said he would revive it if Blanche’s nomination was blocked.

The nomination will now advance to a vote before the full Senate, where Republicans hold 53 seats.

Kicking off Tuesday’s hearing, Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, said that the demands from Tillis and Cornyn about the IRS settlement were “common sense.”

Speaking in front of the committee before the vote, Cornyn thanked Blanche for “being willing to work with us.”

“I’m glad we could address these issues here in committee, so that this nomination can move forward,” he said.

Blanche, who served on Trump’s legal defense team during his hush money trial, was confirmed as deputy attorney general last year. He was nominated for the top position after Trump fired Pam Bondi in April amid reports that he was frustrated with her for not pursuing legal action against his political foes more aggressively.

The fund would have been established with a symbolic $1.776 billion in connection with a lawsuit Trump and his family members brought against the government he controls over the leak of his tax returns.

Even with the carveouts in the Blanche documents that would block the “anti-weaponization” fund from moving forward, the Justice Department has ways to make payouts to Trump allies through the long-established Judgment Fund.

Hundreds of pardoned Jan. 6 rioters have made claims against the government and it’s not clear how the Justice Department will handle those claims moving forward, even though the government would have an easy method to get them dismissed because they weren’t filed in a timely manner. The Justice Department moved to dismiss one of the lawsuits Monday.

Democrats at Tuesday’s hearing also brought up the possibility that Trump could move to enforce the original settlement deal since only Blanche signed the order amending it.

“To state the obvious, Mr. Blanche’s statement on the slush fund and the IRS immunity agreement are not signed by the parties to the settlement agreement and are therefore unenforceable,” said Sen. Dick Durbin of Illinois, the top Democrat of the panel. “The parties could still sue to enforce the agreement, and the cop beaters fund can easily be revived with a new order from the Department of Justice 15 minutes after Mr. Blanche is confirmed as attorney general.”

“Indeed, the president himself has loudly telegraphed that’s his plan,” Durbin added.

Speaking to reporters during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, Trump said the anti-weaponization fund “is dead, but you know, I wish it weren’t.” During an Oval Office event Monday, Trump said that he viewed the fund “as a positive, and a lot of Republicans do too.”

“These people were treated horribly, and this fund could have given them some solace,” the president added. He also noted that he “didn’t look at” Blanche’s agreement dissolving the fund. “All I know is that Todd Blanche is great,” he said.

Durbin issued a warning to Republicans ahead of the vote Tuesday.

“To my Republican colleagues, you gave Mr. Blanche the benefit of the doubt when you supported his nomination to be deputy attorney general,” Durbin said. “Seventeen months later, there is no doubt where his loyalty will lie.”

World.title: Suspect arrested in connection to devastating Spokane wildfire
World.content: A man with a previous manslaughter conviction was arrested in Spokane, WA and had his first appearance in court today. Authorities say he is responsible for the fire that has reduced hundreds of homes to rubble and forced thousands of people to evacuate. NBC News’ Morgan Chesky reports.Aug. 4, 2026

World.title: SpaceX hit by surging AI costs as insiders prepare to sell their shares
World.content:
For a rocket company, SpaceX is spending a lot of money to build out its AI capacities.

Too much, according to investors.

The company reported revenue in its first quarterly update as a public company that surpassed analysts’ expectations. Most of its revenue came from its Starlink satellite offering.

But investor focus turned to capital expenditures related to its xAI unit, which runs the Grok AI service. Those hit $15.8 billion, higher than expectations of $13.09 billion, according to Bloomberg News data, and about double the previous quarter. The AI spending also accounted for most of SpaceX’s overall $18.4 billion quarterly spending on capital expenditures.

The report caused SpaceX shares to reverse a healthy run-up during regular trading hours Tuesday. The stock fell 6.5% in trading after the closing bell, after having surged 9%.

Musk at Tesla's Gigafactory in Grünheide, Germany, in March 2022. Patrick Pleul / AFP via Getty Images file
