World.title: Iraq in talks with Iran to facilitate vessel transit through Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that discussions are taking place with Iran regarding the transit of oil tankers via the Strait of Hormuz, with an anticipated agreement in the near future.

In a statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair stated that the economic and political discussions held during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran addressed approaches to expand cooperation and resulted in signing several agreements.

The Iraqi delegation held talks with Iranian counterparts to ensure the safe transit of vessels across the Strait of Hormuz and protect oil shipments, according to Khudair.

The oil minister stressed that the policy of the Iraqi government is based on building communication channels and partnerships with neighboring countries to support the national economy.

The two parties’ discussions aim to avert future interruptions to Iraqi oil exports amid growing regional maritime concerns.

As Baghdad depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz, it seeks to secure a deal for the safe passage of oil shipments through the waterway.

While Iran has previously shown a willingness to make exceptions for friendly or non-hostile neighbors, practical implementation and approval processes remain a primary focus of continuing discussions.

World.title: Iraq’s liquidity crisis causes delays in paying public servants
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is experiencing a serious financial and liquidity problem, causing delays in paying state employees.

The fall in income from oil, due to the difficulties of exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, has put the Finance Ministry of Iraq in a deficit by trillions of dinars.

The Iraqi government is considering home loans to finance its enormous monthly salaries.

Crude oil exports, which account for approximately 90 percent of Iraq’s federal income, fell dramatically because of the military operations in the region and maritime shipping difficulties.

Iraq requires between 8 and 11 trillion Iraqi dinars ($6.1 billion to $8.4 billion) every month to pay millions of governmental staff and pensioners.

The country’s income fell significantly below expenditure demands, resulting in a large monthly shortfall and an acute cash crisis.

Payrolls have experienced extraordinary delays, causing public concern and reducing local economic activity.

Financing shortfalls have put a burden on government-owned enterprises, particularly drug delivery in the health sector.

Authorities aim to engage in temporary local borrowing to avoid incurring further international debt, as well as long-term calls for diversified state resources.

World.title: Dana Gas, Crescent Petroleum supply Baghdad with gas for electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum said on Tuesday that they started supplying the electricity ministry with natural gas from the Khor Mor field in Iraqi Kurdistan under an agreement to support the country’s electricity output.

An agreement was reached last December between the Electricity Ministry and the two companies to supply 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Khor Mor facility to the Taza gas-fired power plant in Kirkuk province for a period of one year.

The step took place after a project to increase the production capacity of the Khor Mor gas field to 750 million cubic feet per day was completed.

The completion of the expansion project increased the availability of additional gas quantities to local markets through the pipeline network, as reported by Shafaq News.

Majid Jafar, CEO of Crescent Petroleum and Managing Director of Dana Gas, stated that the gas transfer to the Electricity Ministry in Baghdad marks an important milestone in Iraqi Kurdistan’s gas sector growth.

Jafar explained that this development will address the growing demand for electricity and enhance the services offered to residents.

Richard Hall, CEO of Dana Gas Group, described the deal as an important step reflecting the outcomes of the production growth program.

According to Hall, the agreement paves the way for enhanced collaboration within Iraq’s energy sector, strengthens energy security, and contributes to the stability of the electricity grid.

The Khor Mor gas project provides the fuel required to produce more than 80 percent of the energy in Iraqi Kurdistan, which supplies power to over eight million people.

World.title: Iraq unveils tourism vision 2035 to attract 10 million visitors
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has unveiled an ambitious long-term strategy to transform its tourism sector, aiming to attract 10 million visitors by 2035 through infrastructure upgrades, workforce development, and the preservation of the country’s rich historical, cultural, and religious heritage.

The Iraqi Tourism Authority announced on Tuesday that it has finalized the Iraq Tourism Vision 2035, a roadmap launched under the slogan “A Prosperous and Competitive Iraq.” The initiative is designed to position Iraq as a leading tourism destination in the region while supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

Ali Yassin, spokesperson for the Tourism Authority, said the agency will begin organizing workshops in Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, Karbala, and Erbil to present the vision’s objectives and implementation mechanisms to stakeholders across the country.

The workshops aim to engage local governments, tourism professionals, and investors in executing the strategy over the coming decade.

According to the authority, the plan seeks to attract 10 million tourists by 2035, with a focus on promoting Iraq’s archaeological, cultural, religious, and natural attractions.

Officials said achieving the target will require significant investment in tourism infrastructure, including improving transportation, accommodation, visitor services, and restoring key heritage sites across the country.

The strategy also calls for the rehabilitation and maintenance of archaeological landmarks, museums, religious sites, and other destinations that showcase Iraq’s diverse historical legacy.

The Tourism Vision 2035 is built around three strategic pillars: integration, sustainability, and quality.

Officials said these principles will guide efforts to create a more competitive tourism industry while ensuring long-term preservation of Iraq’s cultural and natural resources.

The plan also emphasizes improving coordination among government institutions and the private sector to encourage investment and strengthen the country’s tourism ecosystem.

In addition to infrastructure projects, the Tourism Authority highlighted the importance of developing skilled professionals capable of supporting the industry’s growth.

The vision includes programs to strengthen the capabilities of workers in the tourism sector through training and capacity-building initiatives, recognizing that qualified personnel are essential to delivering high-quality visitor experiences.

The Tourism Authority said the long-term strategy reflects its commitment to restoring Iraq’s position as a prominent international tourism destination.

By combining investment in infrastructure, heritage preservation, sustainability, and workforce development, officials hope the plan will contribute to economic growth while showcasing Iraq’s unique cultural and historical assets to visitors from around the world.

World.title: Iraq liquidity crisis does not mean bankruptcy, says government financial adviser
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq liquidity crisis should not be interpreted as a sign that the country is running out of money or facing bankruptcy, according to government financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Salih. He emphasized that the Iraqi government retains sufficient financial and administrative tools to continue paying salaries and meeting its core obligations despite ongoing cash flow pressures.

Speaking to Shafaq News on Tuesday, Salih explained that the current challenge stems from timing mismatches between oil revenues entering the treasury and the government’s monthly expenditure commitments, particularly public sector salaries.

Salih stressed that Iraq’s financial pressures are primarily linked to liquidity management rather than a shortage of national wealth.

According to him, the government’s current challenges include:

Timing differences between oil revenue receipts and monthly spending obligations.

High levels of public expenditure.

Continued expansion of public sector employment.

Weak non-oil revenues.

Regional tensions affecting trade and oil exports.

He said these factors have created temporary liquidity pressures but do not indicate a severe financial crisis.

The financial adviser said the government can continue paying salaries and maintaining essential public services through several financial management tools.

These include:

Efficient liquidity management.

Prioritizing essential expenditures such as salaries.

Rescheduling non-urgent investment projects when necessary.

Improving tax and fee collection.

Reducing financial waste.

Increasing non-oil government revenues.

Salih also noted that domestic or external borrowing remains available if required, provided borrowing remains within safe public debt limits and supports financial stability.

Looking ahead, Salih said Iraq must accelerate long-term economic reforms to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

He highlighted several priorities:

Diversifying oil export routes.

Developing transportation and energy infrastructure.

Expanding non-oil revenue sources.

Building a more resilient economy capable of absorbing regional and global shocks.

He concluded that sustainable financial stability cannot rely solely on oil income and will require broader economic diversification and structural reforms.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports surpass 1.25 million bpd in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July 2026 by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June, according to Attaqa News.

Despite this partial recovery, Iraqi shipments remain significantly lower than pre-war levels, reflecting a 63 percent decline from the July 2025 figure of 3.38 million barrels per day.

With the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad’s major marine trade route, strains on the state budget are increasing due to declining oil earnings.

The decrease in revenue from oil exports has driven the Iraqi government to accelerate its search for alternative land routes to export crude oil via neighboring countries.

In July, Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports reached one million barrels per day for the first time since March 2026, marking the end of a steep fall.

The country’s oil exports totaled 3.31 million barrels per day in January, 3.34 million barrels per day in February, 542,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, 98,000 barrels per day in May, 493,000 barrels per day in June, and 1.25 million barrels per day in July.

The figures show that Iraq’s average offshore oil exports fell by 60 percent between January and July 2026, hitting 1.31 million barrels per day compared to 3.33 million barrels per day during the same period in 2025.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Iraq clarifies role in oil tanker transit through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has clarified that it is not responsible for the movement of crude oil tankers after they leave Iraqi export terminals, emphasizing that buyers assume full responsibility for transporting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The statement comes as Iraq continues to navigate regional security challenges affecting energy exports, while officials report gradual improvements in crude oil sales in recent months.

Oil Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said Iraq continues to sell crude oil under the Free on Board (FOB) system, meaning ownership and responsibility for the cargo transfer to the buyer once the shipment is loaded at Iraqi ports.

According to Al-Rikabi, tankers carrying Iraqi crude continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz after departing export terminals. However, he stressed that the ministry is not responsible for the vessels’ navigation routes or for securing the necessary transit approvals.

“The ministry sells crude oil at the port, after which the buyer assumes responsibility for transporting and managing the shipment,” Al-Rikabi said.

He added that the ministry neither owns the tankers nor oversees their operations once they leave Iraqi waters.

Despite transferring responsibility to buyers, Al-Rikabi said the Oil Ministry continues monitoring tanker movements through international vessel-tracking systems.

He noted that Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) follows shipments until they reach their destination refineries, allowing authorities to track export deliveries without directly managing vessel operations.

Some tankers transporting Iraqi crude carry cargoes of up to 2 million barrels, according to the ministry.

Al-Rikabi also indicated that Iraq’s oil export performance has improved steadily in recent months despite disruptions linked to the regional security situation and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said sales last month exceeded those recorded in the previous month, continuing a gradual recovery following earlier export challenges caused by tensions affecting maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes, carrying a significant share of global crude exports, making uninterrupted transit critical for Iraq’s energy sector and international oil markets.

World.title: Iraq launches 3,000-cubic-meter gas storage facility in Najaf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated a gas storage project as part of the Oil Ministry’s efforts to raise storage capacity in line with current operations to boost gas output.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry revealed Monday the start of trial operations at a new gas storage facility in the central Iraqi province of Najaf.

Undersecretary for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber said in a statement that the new gas depot has a storage capacity of 3,000 cubic meters and is part of efforts to boost production and storage capabilities, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The step also reflects the ministry’s efforts to develop the transportation, storage, and distribution systems of liquefied gas, according to Saber.

The Iraqi official explained that the inauguration of the depot at the trial operation stage is certainly an important milestone in improving the capacity of strategic reserves and increasing the flexibility of the supply system.

The initiative will ensure that the requirements for liquefied gas in the central provinces and other cities are adequately met.

The delivery of liquefied gas to the new depot via pipelines, as opposed to tanker trucks, will adhere to safety standards and enhance the stability of supplies.

World.title: 'Tread carefully': SC calls for restraint, dialogue in dealing with student protesters
World.content:

World.title: ‘Vile, abusive’: Bombay HC orders takedown of fake posts targeting Gadkari over E20 ethanol row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday granted interim relief to Union minister

, directing social media intermediaries, including Meta, to take down defamatory deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts linking him and his family to the government's E20 ethanol-blending programme.

The court described the flagged material as âvile and abusiveâ.

Granting interim relief, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed intermediaries, including Meta, to take down deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts falsely linking Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and his family to the E20 fuel controversy, describing the content as "vile and abusive."

The order was passed by Justice Arif Doctor on Wednesday in Gadkari's suit against Meta Platforms, X, Google/YouTube, the Union ministry of electronics and information technology, the department of telecommunications and unidentified users.

The court observed that the material cited by Gadkari was âabsolutely vileâ and abusive, and said such content should not be available on public platforms accessible to young people.

"One such transcript appears on instagram reel. There are other content. The material which plaintiff seeks to pull down, I can only say that the same is absolutely vile abusive. Such material should have no place on public platform, which is accessible to everyone including young," the court said in its interim order, as reported by Bar & Bench.





The court said Gadkari had made out a case for ad interim relief. Meta and Google, which appeared before the court, agreed to remove the material identified in Exhibit C of the plaint. âTheir statement is accepted,â the court said.

The case concerns posts, reels and videos that Gadkari alleged contained manipulated images and videos, including AI-generated âdefamatory contentâ and âdeep fake contentâ. The material allegedly attributed personal responsibility to the Union minister for the E20 programme and suggested that he and his family had derived âundue pecuniary benefitsâ from ethanol blending.

According to the plea, some posts referred to Gadkari's son, Nikhil Gadkari, and his association with CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure Limited, which is involved in manufacturing ethanol and other products. The allegations sought to link that association to purported financial benefits from the E20 programme.

Gadkari has denied the allegations.

The suit also referred to social media content blaming the minister for introducing or mandating E20 petrol and alleging that ethanol-blended fuel had caused damage to vehicles.

Gadkari argued that the posts insinuated corruption, conflict of interest and abuse of office.

The court's interim directions apply to the material identified in the proceedings, rather than constituting a blanket finding on all online criticism of the minister.

The matter will come up for further hearing after four weeks, when the court is expected to consider the case further.

World.title: 'I'm Kalaignar's grandson, M K Stalin's son': Udhayanidhi hits back after release, shares photo
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Senior

leader and Tamil Nadu Leader of the Opposition

on Tuesday hit out at the ruling TVK government after being released from police custody, saying he was not intimidated by his arrest and would continue to fight for farmers and the people.

Sharing a photograph with his father and former chief minister M K Stalin on X, Udhayanidhi invoked his political lineage and accused the government of trying to suppress the opposition.

"I am the grandson of Kalaignar and the son of M K Stalin. I am a cadre of the DMK. We do not fear these tactics. If it means getting arrested while fighting for farmers, not just once - I will get arrested even 100 times. Your repression will never stop our service to the people for even a single day!" he wrote.

'I'm M K Stalin's son': Udhayanidhi shares photo with father after release

Udhayanidhi was briefly arrested on Tuesday morning, a day after his remarks during a protest in Thanjavur over the

with Karnataka sparked a political controversy. During his speech, he was interrupted by chants of "Trisha, Trisha" from the audience. The ruling TVK alleged that his response carried a vulgar double meaning and accused him of lowering the standards of political discourse and insulting the dignity of women.





After being questioned by the police, Udhayanidhi was released later in the day.

Targeting the TVK government after his release, he alleged that the action against him was aimed at diverting attention from farmers' issues.

"The #SofaModel government, which is incapable of wiping away the sorrows of farmers, has arrested me to divert attention from the issues. Using the ruling party's Abusive warriors, they spread defamation against me claiming that I used unnecessary words during the Thanjavur protest.

They registered false cases, thinking they could harass me by dragging me from Chennai to Thanjavur, and tried to satisfy someone," he said.

"Even after arresting me, I looked at the media and said that I view this arrest as a comedy, and only then came along. I did not run away in fear after seeing the police," he added.

Udhayanidhi also referred to the Karur stampede in which 41 people died, accusing the chief minister of avoiding accountability.

"The whole country knows that today's Chief Minister, even when 41 people died in Karur, without meeting their families and without facing the media, fled head over heels in fear that he might be arrested."

"Even after so many lives were lost in Karur - this is the same person who went to Malaysia within the next one month for a film promotion and danced around. The Chief Minister may fear arrest if he wants. I am not afraid of any of that," he said.

The DMK leader also thanked party workers, alliance partners and other political leaders who condemned his arrest and participated in protests demanding his release.

"I express my gratitude to the leaders of various political parties, including friendly movements, who condemned my arrest, and to the party comrades across Tamil Nadu who showed unity in support of me," he said.

World.title: Day 12 of Jharkhand students' protest: Hemant Soren says govt taking exam row 'very seriously'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister

on Wednesday said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity," assuring students that justice would be delivered within the constitutional and legal framework.

Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations.

"This is a sensitive government that believes in delivering justice. Whenever we take up an issue, we remain committed to resolving it. Our young people will certainly get justice within the ambit of the Constitution and the law," Soren said while speaking to reporters after a programme in Ramgarh district's Nemra village on the first death anniversary of Dishom Guru Shibu Soren.

"I cannot tear open my chest to show how serious we are, but the government is taking this matter very seriously. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.

The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were underway and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter.





"We are waiting for the findings and conclusions of the investigating agencies. The people of the state will soon be informed in detail about the matter. Students will receive full support in accordance with constitutional and legal provisions," he said.

Soren said the government was closely monitoring developments and that administrative processes were continuing at all levels. He added that the probe agencies were actively investigating the allegations and that the government's final decision would be announced after all facts and findings were available.

Meanwhile, students protesting at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi entered the 12th day of their agitation on Wednesday. They are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI and ED probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations, disclosure of OMR sheets, main examination answer scripts and category-wise cut-off marks, blacklisting of controversial examination agencies, and comprehensive reforms in the state's recruitment bodies.

World.title: Govt distances itself from Hasina event but Dhaka not convinced
World.content:
Ahead of former Bangladesh PM

's media address, the Indian government sought to distance itself from the event saying that India doesn't endorse the views that may be expressed at the event.

However, Dhaka, which had raised the issue with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Monday, remains unconvinced as diplomatic sources said allowing Hasina to make a political speech might rock an already unsteady relationship.

Hasina, who has announced she plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite the death sentence awarded to her, is scheduled to virtually address a media event at the foreign correspondents' club on Wednesday evening.

This would be Hasina's first media address since she fled to India after being deposed on August 5, 2024.

The MEA said that the interaction was being organized by a private media entity. âThe government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,â said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. The ministry recently told a Parliamentary committee that while providing refuge to Hasina, India had strictly adhered to the principle that no political activity is directed against any other country from Indian soil.





The Indian government also for the first time confirmed that Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman had been invited by India for the

summit that it will host in September. While PM Narendra Modi had earlier invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit, the government said that the invitation on this occasion is for a BRICS outreach session and in Rahman's capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While Bangladesh aspires for BRICS membership and has already received support from Russia and China for its candidature, Rahman will likely be wary of any domestic fallout of travelling to India amid the unresolved Hasina extradition issue.

Jamaat-e-Islami's ascendancy as the primary opposition party may also restrict Rahman from soft-pedalling the Hasina issue. Dhaka has not yet formally accepted or declined the invitation that was extended by Modi to Rahman for BRICS.

âYou would be aware that a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to the Bangladesh PM upon his assumption of office in Feb 2026. As far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh PM in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi,â said the spokesperson.

âThe invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner,â he added.

World.title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Dismissing reports of fuel quality issues at outlets, govt Tuesday said additional checks have been introduced by oil marketing companies (OMCs) to detect fuel contamination and adulteration.

In a post on X, the petroleum ministry said OMCs were regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination, and that only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far.

"In addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing 8-12 times a day at over 87,000 outlets. Over 2,000 samples have also been tested for chloride/sulphide.

Only two cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately," ministry said.

It added that oil companies had been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination across the fuel supply chain, and strict action would be taken if contamination or adulteration was found at any retail outlet.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Through a series of infographics on X, ministry said there was "zero compromise" on quality benchmarks and that 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026 for failing quality standards.





It added that ethanol used for blending must comply with BIS IS 15464, have a minimum purity of 99.6% and be accompanied by a certified quality report. The ministry said ethanol is stored in dedicated facilities to prevent contamination, its quality is monitored regularly to ensure consistency and every tanker is sampled from both the top and bottom before being accepted.

Separately, govt has so far approved Rs 4,687 crore as interest subsidy for eligible ethanol projects under its various support schemes, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament Monday. Under the schemes, govt bears an interest subvention of 6% or 50% of the interest rate charged by lenders, whichever is lower, for five years on loans taken to set up new distilleries or expand existing ethanol production capacity.

It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds, report Dipak Dash & Aabhas Sharma.Late evening, SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns, which were based on investigations of failure of vehicle parts.Some numbers quoted in the communication need authentication through collection of elaborate data from various regions across the country followed by a comprehensive consultation with our member OEMs. MoPNG has also instituted 3ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into petrol supply chain, SIAM clarified late Tuesday.âAll of these steps fully meet the needs of the automobile industry. Further, we understand from OMCs that checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets,â it added. In the letter sent to ministry, SIAM had said investigations of failure of vehicle parts revealed that these were due to âcorrosion or wear caused by high chloride presence traced to the fuel usedâ.It had urged the govt to âinclude chloride parameterâ in E20 fuel specifications and its control by oil marketing companies and retail fuel outlets.SIAM said chloride was highly detrimental to engine parts as its presence or accumulation in the fuel system can lead to corrosion, which can further result in âpermanent damageâ to engine parts immediately or over time. âHence, it is imperative to include the chloride limits in fuel specifications and implement quality control to avoid chloride related failures in the customer vehicles,â the letter had noted.

World.title: West Bengal to fast-track land acquisition to take trains close to Doklam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for expediting a new railway line to boost connectivity to the border area near the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction, West Bengal govt has given its go ahead for fast-tracking acquisition of around 380 hectares of land.

With this, work on the 20-km Chalsa-Naxak new line project that was originally sanctioned in 2011-12 is likely to get speeded up.

TOI has learnt that the new section, a vital component of the New Jalpaiguri-Siliguri-New Bongaigaon gauge conversion project was placed in abeyance in Sept 2019 due to non-cooperation from the earlier Trinamool govt in the state. Official records show that railways "de-freezed" (revived) the project in Jan along with five others after a six year hiatus but again failed to make any progress with the lack of support from the state govt's side.

They added that soon after BJP formed govt all projects pending for years are being expedited. "Soon after Suvendu Adhikari took charge, railway minister Ashwini Vashnaw visited the state where all pending projects were reviewed and state govt has given the go ahead, including for this strategically important project," Siliguri MP Raju Bista told TOI.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Earlier in the day, in a social media post, Bista said, "Happy to share that the ministry of railways has sanctioned around Rs 272 crore for a new 17-km line to Jaldhaka.





The route originates from Khunia More near Chalsa, and passes through Jalpaiguri and Kalimpong forest divisions." He added that the rail link will improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhuta trijunction and boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta area.

Bista said, "The railways and Bengal forest department will carry out a joint survey after the monsoon for the proposed new line." It will connect Jaldhaka region, on the border of the river originating from a place close to Doklam tri-junction of India, Bhutan, China.

World.title: CJP will go to Jharkhand to back students protesting against JPSC, JSSC exam ‘irregularities': Dipke
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) said they will go to Jharkhand in support of the students protesting there over alleged irregularities in the State public service examination and other recruitment tests.

Speaking to reporters ahead of the CJP's core team meeting in his hometown Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra, Mr. Dipke also said their youth movement will function as a "pressure group" for now, as that is what India needs at the moment.

He said the meeting will focus on the dwindling trust of people in institutions like the media and judiciary and also take up issues like ethanol-blended fuel and rising unemployment.

A large number of job aspirants have been staging an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi since July 29, demanding that the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and other recruitment examinations be investigated by an independent panel of retired HC judges from outside Jharkhand.

Asked whether he will support the protest in Jharkhand, Mr. Dipke said, "We will definitely go to Jharkhand, we will stand with them and support their every demand in the agitation."

On whether the CJP will enter politics, Mr. Dipke said the media seemed more excited than the outfit.

"People have lost faith in the judiciary, politics, media and Election Commission of India. Our agitation received nationwide support. As the agitation grew, the support was not merely limited to education issues, it was also about these institutions. Hence, to bring accountability in these institutions, there is a need for a public pressure group," he said.

The condition of political parties is "very bad". People vote for one side in the morning, but by evening a government is formed by someone else, he noted.

"For now, CJP will be a pressure group, as what India needs now is a pressure group," Mr. Dipke asserted.

On the CJP’s core team meeting, Mr. Dipke said, “The agitation at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi drew a nationwide response. The responsibility on us has increased, and people’s expectations from us have grown. In this meeting, we will decide how the organisation should grow and also outline a rough road map for the future."

CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said environmentalist and education activist Sonam Wangchuk will continue to be their mentor and they will seek advice from him.

He further said they will push for withdrawal of FIRs against students who took part in the recent protests led by the CJP against the NEET paper leak and other exam irregularities. "We are talking with government representatives on this issue," he said.

Mr. Das also said they are working to provide legal and medical help to protesters injured in the recent students' agitations across the country.

The CJP core team meeting later commenced its meeting and it will continue on Thursday as well. "We will inform about the decisions by tomorrow," Mr. Dipke said.

CJP representatives Ashutosh Ranka, Ratna Singh and others are also attending the meeting.

The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi concluded on July 25. Thousands of student activists, joined by Mr. Wangchuk during his 26-day hunger strike, mobilised to express public anger over the alleged widespread competitive examination paper leaks.

Mr. Dipke returned to India from the U.S. in June to lead an agitation against the NEET-UG paper ‘leak’ that saw youth from different parts of the country converge in Delhi to demand reforms and resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union education minister.

The movement, which received an enthusiastic response across the country, led to Mr. Pradhan's resignation last week.

The CJP's movement spread across various cities in the country, but demonstrations turned violent, with the police cracking down on student agitators in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and in Bihar, registering cases against them.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir — the elusive quest for Statehood
World.content:
August 5 marks seven years since Jammu and Kashmir (J&K)’s special status (Article 370) was revoked by the Narendra Modi administration; a few days hence, August 9 will mark seven years of J&K’s loss of Statehood. Both actions were accompanied by the most dubious lockdown in India’s history. Thousands of troops were flown in, over 5,000 political leaders and cadre were detained, and curfew was imposed together with a communications blockade.

These were emergency measures, yet no emergency was either visible or declared. The Modi administration argued that its measures were temporary and would lead to a violence-free region in which economic growth would be unleashed. Instead, and predictably, violence has continued, as last year’s terrorist attacks in Kashmir’s Pahalgam (April) and Delhi’s Red Fort (November) attest; indeed, it has spread to areas that were relatively dormant, such as Poonch-Rajouri, and from there to adjoining districts of J&K.

Economically, the region continues to suffer. According to the J&K Economic Survey 2025-2026, the ratio of the region’s per capita income to the national average is 76.6%, whereas it was 79.9% in 2013-14, a fall of 3.3 percentage points. Unemployment remains close to twice that of the national average; graduate unemployment is as high as 23.9%.

Lockdowns and summons

Kashmiri response to the Pahalgam attack was a wholehearted rejection of violence, expressed in peace marches and candlelit demonstrations. It offered the Modi administration an opportunity for peacebuilding on the ground, beginning with the restoration of Statehood. Instead, the Union Home Ministry chose an even more heavy-handed security response. This year’s Amarnath yatra is the most militarised in the history of J&K. Citizens are routinely charged under the draconian Jammu and Kashmir Public Safety Act (PSA) and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act on the flimsiest of grounds; mass summons are common — over 2,000 were called in for questioning after Constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi was shot on July 22 this year — curfews are more often in place than not; and the Union Territory has had the highest number of Internet and communications shutdowns in the country since 2019.

At the time, few recognised how momentous the Modi administration’s actions were, not only in what they did but also in how they did it. Article 370 was hollowed out by executive fiat — a Governor who later said he was ‘ordered’ to sign by the Union Home Minister. Statehood was removed by legislative fiat, via a Parliament which did not even consider consulting J&K’s people or political leaders. No Indian State had been stripped of its Statehood since Delhi lost its Statehood in 1956.

Together, the two actions comprised a breathtaking violation of India’s constitutional principles and the basic structure of the Union. They should have been seen as the second major salvo against India’s democracy — the first being the re-communalisation of the Indian polity through state-sanctioned attacks on Muslims and Christians — but instead they were hived off as specific to conflict-ridden Jammu and Kashmir.

The belief that draconian measures are justified in a conflict-ridden region is fundamentally flawed both morally and pragmatically, as India knows from its own colonial past. Morally, the argument that subjugation is a means towards a desirable end masks the point that subjugation is a repugnant end per se, never a means. Pragmatically, as India knows from its more recent past, subjugation only breeds disaffection which will likely express itself in violence when peaceful means of expression are disallowed.

Editorial | ​Fulfil the promise: On restoring Statehood to Jammu and Kashmir

Yet, the deployment of the argument has allowed the Modi administration to get away with direct rule for seven years. The Supreme Court of India let Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta parrot the argument for four years before weakly advising that Statehood be restored as soon as possible.

Three more years have passed since then, without the Court hearing petitions seeking a timeline for restoration. At no point did the Court question the Union on the utility of its measures on constitutionally moral, or even merely pragmatic, grounds.

Lieutenant-Governor holds power

The Constitution limited the imposition of emergency conditions to six months. Yet, in J&K, emergency conditions have not been lifted for seven years. Though the J&K High Court has repeatedly and increasingly lamented the misuse of draconian laws by the J&K police, its strictures do not appear to have led to reform. J&K held elections two years ago, but the elected administration has few powers. It is the Lieutenant-Governor who controls the administration, the police and government prosecutors under the 2024 Transaction of Business Rules; he has now been granted emergency powers over telecommunications. As an appointee rather than an elected representative, the Lieutenant-Governor is not accountable to the people.

Accountability through democracy

Thanks to India’s young, who so joyfully turned the derogatory ‘cockroach’ into an assertion of strength, accountability has acquired a salience that it had been stripped of over the past decade. Fortuitously, J&K’s ruling National Conference party had already decided to renew a campaign for the restoration of Statehood that the Congress party had launched two years ago but persisted with only fitfully. Now the campaign for Statehood must couch itself in the name of accountability.

As the Constitution clearly recognised, an elected administration is the only way to provide for accountability. Though accountability needs guarantees by an independent legislature, oversight and autonomous institutions and a free media, these too require an elected administration to develop. At base, civil society acquires some space to push for reform under an elected administration, which it lacks under an appointed administration.

Over the past decade, J&K has acquired a number of ugly firsts. It was the first State to undergo wide use of the semi-lethal pellet guns in 2016. (Ironically, pellet guns were developed partly as a less lethal response to the stone-pelting agitation in 2010. Our Interlocutors report had criticised their induction.) It was the first State to lose its special status and its Statehood in 2019. It was the first State to undergo a communal delimitation in which Jammu’s demography was altered by the creation of additional Hindu-majority constituencies, some of them with populations below 50,000, in 2022.

Is it not time for J&K to experience some positive firsts instead of suffering only ugly ones? After all, it was the first State to overcome communal gerrymandering when the 2024 elections yielded a majority for the pluralist National Conference-Congress alliance. It is only fitting that it also be the first State to regain the Statehood that has been withheld for so long.

Radha Kumar is a former Member, Group of Interlocutors for Jammu and Kashmir, and the author of the book, The Republic Relearnt: Renewing Indian Democracy, 1947-2024

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates: Finance Minister Marie Wilson announces one-sovereign gold coin for brides in TVK-led govt.'s maiden Budget

World.title: NEET-UG protests: Listen to Gen Zs, don’t repress them, Supreme Court advices
World.content:
The Supreme Court of India on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) struck a parental tone, saying reasoning with students, youths and organisers involved in the NEET-UG paper leaks protests would be a better option than taking an aggressive tone with them.

“A better way is to counsel them, pacify them… The most powerful resource is reasoning. To listen to them. The government knows how to deal with it,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said.

The court was hearing a petition filed by a retired Air Force officer, Manish Kumar Solanki, who said the government was on the “backfoot” bringing the “so-called organisers” of the Cockroach Janta Party-linked (CJP) demonstration against the paper leak and the ensuing police crackdown and violence which rocked the national capital on July 20.

The counsel for Mr. Solanki said 15 days have passed since the July 20 incident, but there has been no move to make the organisers accountable. He said the CJP was not even a registered organisation.

“The government is bending backwards to accommodate them. Violence, meanwhile, is continuing. A youth died in Rajasthan. In society, everybody is important, including the farmers who had agitated and the protestors of Shaheen Bagh… If the government is on the backfoot, society and the institutions of law cannot be seen to be on the backfoot,” advocate Rizwan Ahmed, appearing for the petitioner, submitted.

He asked why the nation and the society should tolerate a “dangerous precedent”.

“Stone-pelters cannot be allowed to go scot-free just because the government is on the back foot. Tomorrow, Generation Alpha, Beta, Gamma may come… Farmers will take tractors to the Parliament, the temple of democracy,” Mr. Ahmed argued.

He said the NEET-UG protest organisers were continuing to fan the fires, “moving from channel to channel who give them time on a silver platter”. The petitioner suggested that the “young boys and girls” should be asked to do seven days of community service.

But the Chief Justice advised conciliation, counselling and peace.

“Youngsters are required to be pacified, even if some among them are involved in stone-pelting. They need a lot of advice and counselling. Any aggression will only unnecessarily aggravate the situation and lead to further violations. That needs to be avoided,” Chief Justice Kant said.

The Chief Justice said restraint on the part of the law enforcement agencies was better than the use of force while dealing with the young generation. A peaceful agitation could turn violent; it was up to the government to ensure the situation did not spiral out of control.

“In a democratic movement, what starts with a peaceful objective, and then some incident takes place, forces need to have a lot of restraint to ensure that the situation does not go out of hand,” Chief Justice Kant noted.

The court said continuing incidents of violence involving youths must be dealt with carefully to avoid them snowballing into another violent confrontation.

“Stray incidents, wherever they are happening, authorities need to step carefully to avoid any further violence… " A better way is to counsel and pacify them,” the Chief Justice reiterated the message to soothe rather than agitate Gen Z.

The court tagged the petition with a bunch of pleas dealing with the NEET-UG protests to be heard along with them on August 18.

World.title: Home at last: Coimbatore mother reunites with son rescued from bonded labour in Punjab
World.content:
R Sundari is curled up on a mat inside her tile-roofed home at Neelambur in the outskirts of Coimbatore. She is exhausted. Only last week, she undertook the journey of a lifetime. The 68-year-old travelled to Punjab to bring home her 41-year-old son R Prakash, who was rescued from bonded labour from Jasraur village in Amritsar, after he went missing 23 years ago.

When Prakash sits down to eat his lunch of rice and brinjal curry, she is on her feet, fussing over him, asking if he would like some curd. Prakash’s rescue is nothing short of a miracle and Sundari still cannot believe he is back.

“He was 16 when he ran away from home,” she recalls, settling on her front porch that she shares with a calf and a cow she is raising. She and her late husband Ramamoorthy, who moved to Coimbatore from Poomalaipatti village in Virudhunagar district for a better life after marriage, were construction labourers then.

“We’d just bought a bike for our sons,” she says. Prakash, all of 16, angered that he had to share it with his younger brother Prabhu, ran away from home after a heated argument. Initially, the couple assumed their son would be back in a few days once he cooled down. But when he didn’t, they started searching for him. “We were worried about him, but I kept telling myself that he was old enough to take care of himself and that he will be fine,” she says.

Prakash called a neighbour’s grocery store two months later from Chennai. “But he didn’t share his address,” she says. That was the last time she heard from him. When weeks ran into months, she realised she may never see her son again. “I would look for him everywhere. Every time I saw someone sleeping on the streetside, I would run to see their face,” she says, as Prakash sits down next to her. “I have even hopped off buses too peer into the face of someone on the roadside. What if he was my son?”

Sundari had given up all hope of finding Prakash. “When Corona happened, I thought my son too might have been among the many people who died when they caught the infection,” she says. But everything changed when a relative in their native village received a phone call about a Tamil boy in Punjab.

This was possible because of a journalist who just wouldn’t give up. T Muthaiah, a reporter who covers Palladam and Tiruppur for Afternoon News, tracked down Sundari. He heard from his cousin brother that Apna Farz Sewa Society, an NGO based in Lachkani village in Patiala, had rescued a Tamilian who was chained to his bed as a bonded labourer in Jasraur, a village near the India – Pakistan border in Punjab.

Former Haryana Legislative Assembly Secretary Subhash Chander happened to notice Prakash during his visit to the NGO. “I have been volunteering at shelters for destitutes and people who have been rescued from bonded labour since 2018,” says Subhash, who has so far reunited 2,300 people with their families.

Subhash alerted Muthiah’s cousin S Balakrishnan who works as the Deputy Secretary at the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Secretariat. “Prakash was rescued in 2022 and was brought to the shelter. But back then he couldn’t recall much about his hometown,” says Muthaiah.

In 2023, Prakash was able to recall his old neighbourhood near Kavundampalayam from his childhood. “But there was only a burial ground in the place he pointed to,” says Muthaiah. “His family had moved elsewhere.” He finally managed to locate Prakash’s mother in Neelambur.

Muthaiah travelled to Punjab twice by train last month. Once with Prakash’s brother and an interpreter and then with Sundari herself. “On my first visit, the NGO refused to send Prakash with us saying they needed official documents to support our claim,” he says.

Sundari had an old ration card with Prakash’s name at home. Thanks to the support of Coimbatore district collector Pavankumar G Giriyappanavar whom she reached out to at a grievance meeting, she was able to gather the required documents.

She sold two of her cows to be able to undertake the trip. “We finally boarded a train to Punjab on July 26 armed with these documents,” says Muthaiah. It is a journey he will never forget. “I was anxious about Sundari,” he says. “She refused to eat. She kept asking when we would reach; she was very emotional.”

It was in Punjab that Muthaiah was witness to the spirit of Tamil brotherhood. “About 50 people from the Tamil Sangam in Chandigarh accompanied us to the shelter on the morning of July 28,” he says. “They all stood by us with unshakable determination.”

After a tearful reunion of mother and son, they were brought back home by another Salem-based NGO that booked flight tickets for them. “We got to experience the kindness of so many people,” Muthaiah recalls.

Seated with her son at home, Sundari says her late husband would keep telling her that their son would come home one day. “He would say Prakash’s light would lead us to him.”

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget: TVK-led government announces India’s first AI and innovation city ‘Arivagam’
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) said since assuming office, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led State government has signed seven memoranda of understanding (MoUs) worth ₹35,062 crore, with the potential to create 14,790 direct and indirect employment opportunities.

Presenting the Revised Budget for 2026-27 in the Assembly, Mr. Wilson said India’s first dedicated AI and innovation city, named ‘Arivagam’, will be established for artificial intelligence and deep-tech development, with facilities including an AI university, an international skill development centre, a semiconductor hardware testing lab, multi-domain innovation incubators, and modern residential infrastructure. A feasibility study for the project will be undertaken at an estimated cost of ₹5 crore.

Tamil Nadu Budget 2026 LIVE updates: Finance Minister Marie Wilson announces one-sovereign gold coin for brides in TVK-led govt.’s maiden Budget

To encourage large-scale investments and accelerate industrial growth, the State government will strive to establish more Multi Modal Logistics Parks (MMLPs) and Dry Ports at strategic locations, establish petrochemical and ancillary industries, and explore the possibility of setting up new ports in Tamil Nadu.

Space tech boost

According to the Minister, Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli will be declared a ‘Space Industrial Investment Zone’, anchored by the strategic significance of the spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam. To provide infrastructure and technological support to private enterprises, startups, and research organisations, the State government, in collaboration with IN-SPACe, will establish an advanced ‘Space Vehicle Common Technical Facility’.

A new Tamil Nadu Industrial Policy will be released to strengthen the State’s industrial and economic growth. The policy will foster innovation and technology-driven growth, support emerging industry sectors, drive sustainable development, and export promotion. The State government will also create the Tamil Nadu Industrial Capability Directory, a comprehensive digital platform listing the State’s manufacturing and supply capabilities, Mr. Wilson said.

To enhance Tamil Nadu’s competitiveness, the State will introduce an AI-powered investment service system called ‘Guidance 3.0’, making all requisite information, clearances, and services available on a single platform for investors. As part of this initiative, the ‘Tamil Nadu Single Window Portal 3.0’ will be upgraded to enable all statutory approvals, clearances, and no-objection certificates required for establishing industries and investment projects to be obtained through a unified interface, he said.

Besides, a ‘Non-Resident Tamil Investment Facilitation Desk’ will be established within Guidance to facilitate and promote investment by the global Tamil diaspora in the State.

New industrial parks

To ensure balanced and equitable industrial development across all regions of Tamil Nadu, SIPCOT will establish new industrial parks in industrially backward districts based on district-specific industrial development plans and sectoral strengths. These parks will be developed with state-of-the-art infrastructure at an estimated cost of approximately ₹3,200 crore over the next five years, the Finance Minister said.

The Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department has been allocated ₹4,414 crore in the Budget.

World.title: Delhi witnesses widespread rainfall; waterlogging, traffic snarls in several areas
World.content:
Widespread rainfall lashed Delhi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), leading to traffic snarls and waterlogging in many areas, while the weather office issued yellow and orange alerts for various parts of the city, warning of moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorm activity.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), between 8.30 a.m. and 11.30 a.m. on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), Safdarjung, the city's base station, recorded 15.4 mm of rainfall, while Lodhi Road received 26 mm. Ridge recorded trace rainfall during the period.

Areas including Vijay Chowk, Jantar Mantar, Kartavya Path, ITO, Mathura Road, Sangam Vihar, C R Park, Lodhi Road and several other localities recorded heavy rainfall.

Many commuters took to social media to complain about waterlogging in areas such as CR Park, Sangam Vihar, Lodhi Road and several other localities following the rain.

Traffic congestion was reported from several parts of the city, including the ITO-Mathura Road stretch, Safdarjung Enclave and the Nizamuddin-Ashram corridor, following the rain.

In the 24-hour period ending at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), Safdarjung recorded 10.8 mm of rainfall, Palam 8.3 mm, Lodhi Road 3.9 mm, Ridge 3 mm and Ayanagar 49.3 mm, the IMD said.

The IMD has forecast moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds in parts of Delhi between Wednesday (August 5, 2026) and Thursday (August 6, 2026).

World.title: Railway Ministry reiterates bedroll kit directive for RAC passengers after repeated complaints
World.content:
The Railway Ministry has reiterated its directive to provide linen and blankets to passengers travelling on Reservation Against Cancellation status after receiving repeated complaints from almost all zones.

Under the RAC system, two passengers are accommodated on a single berth.

"Complaints regarding the non-provision or inadequate provision of bedroll kits to RAC passengers are still being received through various channels," the Ministry said in a letter dated August 4.

It added, "In view of the above, it is reiterated that the Railway Board's instructions must be strictly followed to ensure that every RAC passenger travelling in AC coaches (except AC Chair Car) is provided with a complete bedroll kit at par with other bona fide passengers travelling in the coach."

World.title: Pakistan, US hold counterterrorism dialogue, reaffirm commitment to combating terrorist groups
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States and Pakistan on Tuesday held the fourth counterterrorism dialogue in Washington, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorist groups and strengthening security cooperation at a time when regional tensions remain high.

The talks were led by US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Ambassador Gregory LoGerfo and Foreign Ministry Special Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir, a joint statement released by the US State Department said.

“The dialogue underscored shared interests in the US-Pakistan counterterrorism partnership and the two countries’ determination to confront terrorism,” the joint statement said.

“Delegations exchanged views on the current threat environment, explored avenues to enhance collaboration, and discussed steps to strengthen border security and disrupt terrorist facilitation networks,” it added.

The statement specifically named ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K), Al Qaeda, the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its affiliates among organisations that both governments said posed threats to regional security.

“The US and Pakistan affirmed their joint resolve to confront terrorist organisations that endanger the safety of their citizens and the stability of the region,” the statement said.

“The two governments committed to ensuring their counterterrorism collaboration to keep both of their nations safe and secure, and as part of an enduring vision of regional peace, prosperity, and stability,” it said.

Meanwhile, the Foreign Office said that the two sides held “extensive deliberations on the regional and global terrorist threat and pledged to deepen counterterrorism collaboration both bilaterally and at multilateral fora”.

The renewed engagement marks a shift from the difficult period in US-Pakistan relations following the withdrawal of American forces from Afghanistan in 2021. Washington had expressed concerns over terrorists sanctuaries in the region, while Islamabad repeatedly highlighted the security challenges it faced from cross-border militancy and instability in Afghanistan.

In recent years, both countries have sought to focus on areas of mutual interest, including counterterrorism, trade, investment, climate cooperation, and regional stability.

Pakistan’s strategic location and longstanding diplomatic links with neighbouring countries have also increased its importance in regional diplomacy. The country’s diplomatic role also gained renewed attention during the US-Iran conflict, as Islamabad has mediated between the two sides.

The improved engagement with the US also comes as Pakistan continues to face serious internal security challenges. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

Pakistan, US look to finalise reciprocal trade framework

While representatives from the US and Pakistan held counter-terrorism discussions in Washington, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a virtual meeting with United States Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer from Islamabad.

The meeting was held to review the progress of ongoing negotiations, which are focused on strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the US, a statement released by the finance ministry said.

The engagement took place roughly three weeks after the finance minister visited Washington, where he held talks with senior American officials on trade, tariffs, investment and economic cooperation.

During his visit, Mr Aurangzeb held meetings with officials from the Office of the Trade Representative, the US Export-Import Bank (Exim), the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and the International Monetary Fund.

The discussions focused on a possible bilateral trade agreement covering tariffs, market access, investment opportunities and wider economic cooperation. Separate talks with the Exim Bank and the DFC explored financing for infrastructure, energy and private-sector investment projects in Pakistan.

During the meeting on Wednesday, he recalled his recent discussions in Washington and “welcomed the steady progress made by the respective negotiating teams and appreciated the constructive engagement that has characterised the dialogue over time”, the finance ministry said.

It added that both sides noted that negotiations on the proposed reciprocal trade framework had advanced significantly and reaffirmed their shared commitment to conclude the agreement at the earliest.

“The finance minister highlighted the importance of maintaining the momentum of negotiations in view of Pakistan’s economic priorities.

“He emphasised that a strengthened trade and investment partnership with the United States would contribute to Pakistan’s export-led growth strategy, support economic resilience, and create greater commercial opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the statement read.

It further said that Auragzeb also underlined the importance of continued collaboration with the Exim Bank to facilitate bilateral trade and investment.

According to the finance ministry, Ambassador Greer acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement throughout the negotiations.

He reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to “sustaining the positive trajectory of bilateral trade discussions and expressed confidence that the remaining issues could be resolved through continued technical engagement”, the finance ministry said.

It added that Aurangzeb also emphasised the importance of maintaining close coordination and accelerating technical-level discussions to build on the progress already achieved.

“Both sides expressed satisfaction with the progress achieved and agreed to continue working closely to finalise the remaining elements of the framework and agreed to continue regular engagement with a view to concluding the reciprocal trade framework soon, further strengthening the longstanding economic partnership between Pakistan and the United States,” the ministry’s statement read.

It added that Greer also “appreciated the progress made on labour and regulatory reforms, including measures relating to forced labour compliance”.

Pakistan is among the 60 countries on which the US imposed new import tariffs last month over what Washington said was their failure to effectively prohibit imports of goods produced with forced labour.

Pakistan was placed in the lower 10 per cent tariff category, alongside countries that had either adopted forced labour import prohibitions, committed to doing so under reciprocal trade arrangements, or had partial enforcement regimes.

The finance ministry said that Pakistan’s Federal Secretary for Commerce Jawad Paul and senior team members of the USTR also joined Wednesday’s meeting.

World.title: Trump warns Iran to open Strait of Hormuz or get 'hit very hard'
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come as soon as Wednesday but warned Iran it would get “hit very hard” if negotiations fell through.

Transit of the waterway, a key conduit for global oil and gas supplies, has been a sticking point in talks and led to renewed fighting following an April ceasefire.

Iran has tightened its grip on Hormuz and wants to control the strait and charge tolls — powers it did not exercise before the war began on February 28.

Trump said on Tuesday a deal with Iran to reopen Hormuz could happen “tomorrow or the next day,” telling reporters in California that negotiators “had a very good day”.

Earlier, he struck a more threatening tone.

“The strait is going to be open very soon, or they’re going to get hit very hard — and then the strait’s going to be open,” Trump said in an interview with Fox News.

“All you can do is fight your way out.”

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC earlier “there is a chance we may have a deal” by Wednesday or Thursday.

Underlining the volatile situation, one crew member was listed missing Tuesday on a merchant ship hit by a projectile in Hormuz, while an Indian ship in the Red Sea sank following an unattributed attack.

In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran “very hard”, potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back, hinting a deal was near.

Iran’s foreign ministry has denied negotiations with Washington, even as Trump insisted they were happening.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that the US was involved in negotiations between Oman and Iran on increasing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

News outlet Axios reported on Tuesday that the US, Iran and Oman were nearing an interim deal to reopen the strait, which Washington was hoping to announce on Wednesday.

Axios, citing unnamed regional officials and a US official, said the deal on the table would be a 60-day arrangement for safe passage in the strait between Iran and Oman.

Deal or surrender

Qatar, which has been mediating negotiations, said that diplomatic efforts were ongoing but that no direct Iran-US talks were planned.

Its leader, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani, spoke with Trump by phone on Tuesday, with Doha saying they discussed “efforts to de-escalate tensions.”

Trump had previously said he expected to know by Tuesday how the talks were going, “one way or the other”, but insisted “it’s not very complex”.

Washington’s diplomatic goals include reopening Hormuz and the denuclearisation of Iran, which Trump accepted could “take a little while.”

The president previously called Tehran “duplicitous” for saying it was not negotiating, adding that a US counter-blockade of Iranian ports would remain “unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished”.

More than five months into a war that has cost Washington billions of dollars, Iran remains able to fire missiles and drones at US and allied targets in the region, as well as at commercial shipping.

Early on Tuesday, Britain’s maritime security agency UKMTO said an unnamed cargo vessel had been struck by an “unknown projectile” in the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman.

Iran continues to impose an effective blockade on the strait and insists ships coordinate crossings with it.

Red Sea attack

The disruptions in Hormuz have only placed greater importance on shipping lanes through the Red Sea, where Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu has enabled it to keep up shipments to global markets by circumventing Hormuz entirely.

But since the Houthis announced their blockade, they have claimed attacks on multiple ships they say are in violation.

On Tuesday, the Indian ship MSV Faize Noore Oliya sank in the Red Sea off Yemen following an unattributed attack, with all of its crew rescued.

The Red Sea is a gateway to the Suez Canal, and a previous campaign of Houthi attacks on commercial vessels during the Gaza war forced shippers to instead take lengthy detours around the southern tip of Africa.

World.title: Youm-i-Istehsal: Pakistan says lasting peace in South Asia linked to peaceful resolution of Kashmir dispute
World.content:
The military and civilian leadership on Wednesday said just and lasting peace in South Asia was closely linked to the peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute as the country marked Youm-i-Istehsal (Exploitation Day) to mark the anniversary of India revoking the occupied region’s special autonomy in 2019.

President Asif Ali Zardari said that Youm-i-Istehsal was being observed to “reaffirm our unwavering solidarity” with the people of occupied Kashmir.

“We pay tribute to their courage, resilience and commitment to their just struggle for the realisation of their inalienable right to self-determination,” he said.

The president said that seven years have passed since India’s “illegal and unilateral actions” of August 5, 2019, when it revoked the region’s special autonomy.

“These actions cannot change the legal status of the dispute, nor can they weaken the resolve of the Kashmiri people,” he said.

“For seven years, millions of Kashmiris have continued to live under severe restrictions that have affected every aspect of daily life. Families have endured uncertainty, young people have seen their opportunities constrained and entire communities have continued to bear the burden of prolonged conflict and instability. Despite these hardships, the people of Jammu and Kashmir have remained steadfast in their pursuit of justice and their legitimate right to determine their own future,” President Zardari said.

He said that Pakistan remained unwavering in its moral, political and diplomatic support for the people of occupied Kashmir.

“We will continue to raise our voice at every international forum until the Jammu and Kashmir dispute is resolved in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people,” he said.

The president said that just and lasting peace in South Asia was closely linked to the peaceful resolution of Kashmir dispute, urging the international community to play its role in addressing the human rights situation in the occupied valley.

“To my Kashmiri brothers and sisters, I say: Pakistan stands firmly with you. Your courage in the face of adversity inspires us. You are not alone. The people of Pakistan will continue to stand by you until your legitimate right to self-determination is realised,” he said.

In his message, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the people and the government of Pakistan “stand in unwavering solidarity with our Kashmiri brothers and sisters”.

He said that seven years later, India’s unlawful measures had neither changed the legal status of occupied Kashmir nor diminished the legitimate aspiration of its people.

“Instead, they have deepened repression, undermined fundamental freedom, and accelerated attempts to alter the demographic composition of the occupied territory through unlawful legislative and administrative measures. The continued suppression of the genuine Kashmiri political leadership, restrictions on civil liberties, and curbs on independent media, remain a matter of serious concern,” he said.

“Despite these challenges, the courage, resilience and steadfastness of the Kashmiri people remain unshaken. Their peaceful and just struggle for the realization of their unalienable right to self-determination continues to inspire generations and commands the respect and support of all those who believe in justice, human dignity and the rule of international law,” he added.

The premier said that the Kashmir dispute remained the “principal unresolved issue affecting peace and stability in South Asia”.

“Lasting peace in the region cannot be achieved by coercion or unilateral action, but only through a peaceful settlement of the dispute in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the relevant UNSC resolutions. The international community must move beyond expressions of concern and play its rightful role in advancing a just and durable resolution of the dispute,” he said.

He reaffirmed that a peaceful and just resolution of the dispute remained a cornerstone of Pakistan’s foreign policy, adding that Pakistan would continue to “extend its diplomatic, political and moral support and raise the voice of the Kashmiri people at every regional and international forum”.

PM Shehbaz said that Pakistan called upon the international community to urge India to end its human rights violations in occupied Kashmir, reverse its “illegal and unilateral measures” introduced since August 2019, repeal the draconian laws imposed upon the people and create conducive environment to enable the peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute, through the exercise of the right to self-determination by the Kashmiri people in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in his message on the occasion, called on the international community to fulfil its “long-overdue responsibility” for the peaceful resolution of the dispute.

DPM Dar said India’s actions in occupied Kashmir on August 5, 2019, presented a “grave challenge” to the established international framework and expressed solidarity with the people of the region.

“We reaffirm our unwavering support for their fundamental rights, as enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations and reflected in the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he said, adding that events of August 5, 2019 remained a “matter of deep concern”.

He continued: “These steps have further complicated efforts to promote peace and stability in South Asia and have adversely impacted the lives, rights, and freedoms of the Kashmiri people.”

At this, the DPM urged the international community to play a role in ensuring respect for international law, international humanitarian law, human rights and commitments made under the UN.

Dar also called on India to halt all actions aimed at undermining the disputed status of occupied Kashmir and “take steps conducive to creating an environment for the peaceful resolution of the dispute”.

“We reiterate that lasting peace and stability in South Asia can only be achieved through the resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he said, adding that Pakistan will continue to raise its voice on international forums for a “just and peaceful settlement of the dispute”.

Concluding his statement, Dar paid tribute to the “resilience, courage, and sacrifices” of the Kashmiri people.

“Pakistan stands in steadfast solidarity with them and will continue to extend its unwavering moral, political, and diplomatic support to their just struggle for the realisation of their legitimate right to self- determination.”

He called upon the international community, particularly the UN, to “fulfil its long-overdue responsibilities and make meaningful efforts for a peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute”.

Separately, foreign ministry officials, led by the foreign secretary, participated in a solidarity walk on Islamabad’s Constitution Avenue to “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Kashmiri people”, a statement on the ministry’s X said.

It said Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam addressed the rally and reiterated Pakistan’s “steadfast political, diplomatic and moral support for the just struggle of the Kashmiri people and their inalienable right to self-determination, in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation resolutions”.

Armed forces reaffirm solidarity with Kashmiris

Separately, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf and Chief of Air Staff Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu reaffirm their unwavering solidarity with the resilient and courageous people of occupied Kashmir.

A statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations said, “The armed forces of Pakistan reiterate their steadfast support for the legitimate struggle of Kashmiri people to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination as enshrined in international law and the relevant UNSC resolutions.”

They said that the continued occupation of the valley remained a matter of “serious concern”.

“Such actions, coupled with provocative rhetoric and belligerent posturing, serve only to exacerbate regional instability and perpetuate human suffering,” they said.
